Legal information
Warning notice system
             This manual contains notices you have to observe in order to ensure your personal safety, as well as to prevent
             damage to property. The notices referring to your personal safety are highlighted in the manual by a safety alert
             symbol, notices referring only to property damage have no safety alert symbol. These notices shown below are
             graded according to the degree of danger.

                   DANGER
              indicates that death or severe personal injury will result if proper precautions are not taken.

                   WARNING
              indicates that death or severe personal injury may result if proper precautions are not taken.

                   CAUTION
              indicates that minor personal injury can result if proper precautions are not taken.

              NOTICE
              indicates that property damage can result if proper precautions are not taken.
             If more than one degree of danger is present, the warning notice representing the highest degree of danger will be
             used. A notice warning of injury to persons with a safety alert symbol may also include a warning relating to property
             damage.
Qualified Personnel
             The product/system described in this documentation may be operated only by personnel qualified for the specific
             task in accordance with the relevant documentation, in particular its warning notices and safety instructions. Qualified
             personnel are those who, based on their training and experience, are capable of identifying risks and avoiding
             potential hazards when working with these products/systems.
Proper use of Siemens products
             Note the following:

                   WARNING
              Siemens products may only be used for the applications described in the catalog and in the relevant technical
              documentation. If products and components from other manufacturers are used, these must be recommended or
              approved by Siemens. Proper transport, storage, installation, assembly, commissioning, operation and
              maintenance are required to ensure that the products operate safely and without any problems. The permissible
              ambient conditions must be complied with. The information in the relevant documentation must be observed.

Trademarks
             All names identified by ® are registered trademarks of Siemens AG. The remaining trademarks in this publication
             may be trademarks whose use by third parties for their own purposes could violate the rights of the owner.
Disclaimer of Liability
             We have reviewed the contents of this publication to ensure consistency with the hardware and software described.
             Since variance cannot be precluded entirely, we cannot guarantee full consistency. However, the information in this
             publication is reviewed regularly and any necessary corrections are included in subsequent editions.

Target group
                 This manual is intended for machine manufacturers and service technicians.


Benefits
                 As a result of the modular concept, Create MyConfig enables automatic series production and
                 the upgrade of different machines of a series with one package.

                 In contrast to the conventional procedure, individual operations on the machine are safer,
                 easier and faster to perform.
                 ● The production time for machines with SINUMERIK 840D sl or SINUMERIK 828D is
                   significantly reduced.
                 ● The upgrade time for end users is also reduced.
                 ● A high level of reproducibility is achieved through automatic data loading.
                 ● The quality of production and service is improved significantly.
                 ● Less expert knowledge is required by the commissioning engineers.
                 ● Modular data management for modular machines is supported at the machine
                   manufacturer's.
                 ● Modular machines can adapt to flexible SINAMICS topologies.
                 ● The commissioning process is documented in a log file.


Standard scope
                 This documentation only describes the functionality of the standard version. Additions or
                 revisions made by the machine manufacturer are documented by the machine manufacturer.
                 Other functions not described in this documentation might be executable in the control. This
                 does not, however, represent an obligation to supply such functions with a new control or when
                 servicing.
                 For the sake of simplicity, this documentation does not contain all detailed information about all
                 types of the product and cannot cover every conceivable case of installation, operation, or
                 maintenance.


Note regarding the General Data Protection Regulation
                 Siemens observes standard data protection principles, in particular the principle of privacy by
                 design. That means that
                 this product does not process / store any personal data, only technical functional data (e.g. time
                 stamps). If a user links this data with other data (e.g. a shift schedule) or stores personal data
                 on the same storage medium (e.g. hard drive) and thus establishes a link to a person or
                 persons, then the user is responsible for ensuring compliance with the relevant data protection
                 regulations.

1.3              Industrial security

                     Note
                     Industrial security
                     Siemens provides products and solutions with industrial security functions that support the
                     secure operation of plants, systems, machines and networks.
                     In order to protect plants, systems, machines and networks against cyber threats, it is
                     necessary to implement – and continuously maintain – a holistic, state-of-the-art industrial
                     security concept. Products and solutions from Siemens constitute one element of such a
                     concept.
                     Customers are responsible for preventing unauthorized access to their plants, systems,
                     machines and networks. Such systems, machines and components should only be connected
                     to an enterprise network or the Internet if and to the extent such a connection is necessary and
                     only when appropriate security measures (e.g. using firewalls and/or network segmentation)
                     are in place.
                     For additional information on industrial security measures that can be implemented, please
                     visit:
                     Industrial security (http://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity)
                     Siemens’ products and solutions undergo continuous development to make them more secure.
                     Siemens strongly recommends that product updates are applied as soon as they become
                     available, and that only the latest product versions are used. Use of product versions that are
                     no longer supported, and failure to apply the latest updates may increase customer’s exposure
                     to cyber threats.
                     To stay informed about product updates, subscribe to the Siemens Industrial Security RSS
                     Feed at:
                     Industrial security (http://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity)


                     Further information is provided on the Internet:
                     Industrial Security Configuration Manual (https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/ww/de/
                     view/108862708)

                     Interactions/restrictions for Create MyConfig with CNC



                     Note
                     CMC 4.8 HF3 - Do not write SINAMICS parameters / indices when using certain CNC versions
                     Do not write any SINAMICS parameters or indices that SINAMICS does not know in
                     manipulation tasks.
                     The following CNC software versions are affected:
                     ● CNC-SW 2.7 SP1
                     ● CNC-SW 4.4 SP1




                     NOTICE
                     CMC 4.8 HF3 - SINAMICS user-specified topology faulty with certain CNC versions
                     The SINAMICS user-specified topology is executed incorrectly in the majority of topologies
                     with certain versions and therefore cannot be used.
                     The following CNC software versions are affected:
                     ● CNC-SW 2.7 SP1
                     ● CNC-SW 4.4 SP1




                     Note
                     CMC 4.8 HF3 - Plugging in ALM and TM
                     Plug in the corresponding components for the Active Line Module (ALM) and Terminal Module
                     (TM) before using the "Determine DO type from hardware" function for ALM and TM.




                     Note
                     CMC 4.8 HF3 - When using the user-specified topology note the following:
                     If you are using a user-specified topology, NX modules and CU320-2 must be present.
                     You must not deactivate NX modules and CU320-2 in Topo and during the package execution.
                     Retrofitting is not possible.

                      Note
                      CMC 4.8 HF3 - Drive commissioning with user-specified topology
                      The drive commissioning with user-specified topology is only possible:
                      ● When the actual topology is a proper subset of the user-specified topology; components
                        may be deactivated.
                      ● No additional or different components must be present.




                      Note
                      CMC 4.8 HF3 / CNC SW 4.4 SP1 - Drive commissioning with user-specified topology
                      For drive commissioning with user-specified topology, the following differences occur in CNC
                      SW 4.4 SP1 in comparison to the automatic device configuration by SINAMICS:
                      ● The parameters p115 and p112 and are not set correctly.
                      ● The parameters p7602, p7604, p7606, p7621, p7623, p7625, p7641, p7643, p7645
                         (back-up Ydb), and p7882 are set differently than in the automatic device configuration.
                      ● The parameter p8801 is not written by the user-specified topology. In practical terms, this
                         has no effect.




                      NOTICE
                      CMC 4.8 HF3 - Access level or password of the NC are reset
                      If functions which reset the access level or the password of the NC are running in the PLC user
                      program on the NCU, proceed as follows.
                      ● Switch the PLC via the "S4=2" hardware switch statically to "Stop".
                      This restriction does not apply to packages with a new installation!
                      This constraint does not apply as of the following CNC software versions:
                      ● 2.7 SP2 HF2 and higher
                      ● 4.4 SP2 HF2 and higher

Introduction                                                                                                    2
                      Create MyConfig engineering software supports the machine manufacturer to create and run
                      projects for automated production and commissioning of machines with SINUMERIK 840D sl
                      or SINUMERIK 828D controls. Upgrades for these controls can also be configured and
                      automatically executed at the end user's.

                      The engineering software Create MyConfig comprises the four components - Diff, Expert, Topo
                      and Shield:
                      ● Diff is a comparison software that supports you in the provision of modular data.
                      ● Expert is a configuration software that supports you when creating a project. Deployment of
                        a project produces an executable package.
                      ● Topo topology software supports you to display and/or generate a comparison and/or target
                        topology for the automated commissioning of the SINAMICS drive system.
                        Click Topo to display and configure the axis-drive assignment.
                      ● Shield is the execution software, which does not need to be individually installed. When
                        deploying the project via Expert, an executable package containing the software component
                        Shield, scripts, instructions and data is created. After starting the package, it is processed
                        by Shield according to the configuration.

                      Independent tools
                      Create MyConfig also provides independent tools which you can use without the engineering
                      software:
                      ● Script Editor (Page 345)
                        For editing manipulation tasks, user libraries and diff scripts independently of Expert
                      ● DOList Editor (Page 560)
                        For editing reusable and cross-topology DO lists independently of Topo.
                      ● Resource Editor (Page 436)
                        For editing user texts in multilingual packages independently of Qt Linguist or Expert.

Installation                                                                                                   4
4.1               Overview
                      You have two options for installing engineering software "Create MyConfig" and the
                      "NcuShareService" application on your PC:
                      ● Installation using the installation wizard
                        The CMC package is installed via the so-called general setup.
                        The general setup involves the installation of Create MyConfig - and the installation of
                        Application License Managers (ALM).
                        Further information can be found in the following sections:
                         – User-guided setup (Page 30)
                         – Automated setup (silent installation) (Page 31)
                      ● Installation via command line
                        It can also be automatically installed without any user interaction.
                        An "OPFILE.txt" control file can be transferred as argument when starting the setup.
                        The setup process can be preconfigured in this control file. This means that it is no longer
                        necessary to manually work through the setup dialogs. The following sections describe the
                        option for installation via the command line.
                        Further information can be found in the following sections:
                         – Structure of the "OPFILE.txt" control file (Page 32)
                         – Command line call (Page 34)
                         – Changing installed program parts (Page 35)




4.2               Hardware requirements
                      A PC/PG must meet the following requirements for the installation and operation of CMC.
                      ● The installation drive should have approx. 500 MB of free memory.
                      ● Additional memory is required for the prerequisites and to create your own projects.
                      ● All graphics-capable printers supported by the operating system can be used.
                      ● A network connection or USB data medium (USB stick, USB hard disk, etc.) is required for
                        the reinstallation/upgrade of the PCU50/NCU/PPU.
                      ● A USB data medium with or without Linux boot system (USB stick, USB hard disk, etc.) or
                        a network connection is required for the reinstallation/upgrade of the NCU/PPU.

4.4 User-guided setup


4.3            Software requirements
                  CMC is a 32/64-bit application and requires one of the following software platforms:

                  PG/PC         MS Windows 7 SP1 (32- and 64-bit) Professional, Ultimate or Enterprise
                                MS Windows 10 (64-bit) Professional, Enterprise
                  PCU50         MS Windows 7
                  IPC 627D      MS Windows 7 with installed PCU-Basesoftware
                  IPC 427D      MS Windows 7 with installed PCU-Basesoftware
                  IPC 477D      MS Windows 7 with installed PCU-Basesoftware
                  IPC 427E      MS Windows 7 with installed PCU-Basesoftware
                                Windows 10 IoT Enterprise 2016 LTSB (64-bit) with installed PCU-Basesoft‐
                                ware
                  IPC 477E      MS Windows 7 with installed PCU-Basesoftware
                                Windows 10 IoT Enterprise 2016 LTSB (64-bit) with installed PCU-Basesoft‐
                                ware

                  Furthermore, CMC requires the following installed products:
                  ● Web browser
                  ● Acrobat Reader or a comparable tool for displaying PDF documents




4.4            User-guided setup
                  Create MyConfig is installed via a user-guided setup (general setup).
                  The Automation License Manager (ALM) which is required for the script execution is also
                  installed via the user-guided setup.

                  To do this, start the "Setup.exe" in the root directory of the CD:
                  Drive:\[CD setup path]\.

                  The CMC setup files can now be found in the following directories:
                  For the 64-bit version: Drive:\[CD setup path]\setup\CMC\setup\x64
                  For the 32-bit version: Drive:\[CD setup path]\setup\CMC\setup\x86

                  Note
                  Information for CMC 4.8 SP1
                  ● CMC 4.8 SP1 can be installed and used in parallel to previous versions of CMC 4.5, 4.6 HF1
                      and 4.7 SP2 HF1.
                  ● Any existing preliminary versions of CMC 4.8 SP1 must be uninstalled before a new version
                      of CMC can be installed.
                      You uninstall the preliminary version via Control Panel > Software.
                  ● Components of CMC 4.8 SP1 can also be installed individually.

4.5               Automated setup (silent installation)
                      The following two files are required for the silent installation via the general setup.
                      You can adapt the files to your requirements.

                       Drive:\[CD setup path]\Ra_auto.ini
                       Drive:\[CD setup path]\setup\cmc\CMC.ssf
                      You can create your own "Ra_auto.ini" file, or you can use the file provided under
                      "Drive:\[CD setup path]\Ra_auto.ini". If you use this file, you must adapt the path
                      in the command line call.
                      You can create your own "Ra_auto.ini" file by calling the general setup:

                       Drive:\[CD setup path]\setup.exe /record
                      The "Ra_auto.ini" file is written to the "%TEMP%" directory. You can select a different
                      directory in the Setup dialog. You can accept the "Ra_auto.ini" file without making any
                      changes.
                      The "Drive:\[CD setup path]\setup\cmc\CMC.ssf" file is called for each installation
                      via the general setup.

                      The file contains the following sections:

                       [GENERAL]

                       [VERSIONS]

                       [OPFILEENTRIES_BEGIN]
                       [OPFILEENTRIES_END]

                       [LANGUAGES]

                       [GERMAN]

                       [ENGLISH]
                      Changes are required for an automated installation. The most important changes must be
                      made in the [GERMAN] and [ENGLISH] sections.

                      Remove the comments before the lines:

                      At [GERMAN]
                       SetupFileParameters=/W /L1031 /V"commandline=\"\"\"-OF:OPFILE.txt
                       \"\"\""
                      At [ENGLISH]
                       SetupFileParameters=/W /L1033 /V"commandline=\"\"\"-OF:OPFILE.txt
                       \"\"\""
                      Further changes may be required in the [OPFILEENTRIE_BEGIN] section.

Options and arguments

                       Options         Arguments and description
                       L               <Language ID>
                                       Option L (language) indicates the language ID for displaying the language in the dialogs
                                       and messages.
                                       The language ID does not influence the installed program language.
                                       The following arguments are admissible:
                                       ● 1031 for German
                                       ● 1033 for English
                       W               The option does not include any arguments.
                                       "setup.exe" is not executed until the installation has been completed - and only then is
                                       it closed.
                       V               <Msiexec (command line options)>
                                       Parameters can be specified as arguments to call up the Windows Installer. The argu‐
                                       ment must be specified in straight quotation marks.
                                       The documentation for the command line arguments of Windows Installer is provided in
                                       MSDN (Microsoft Developer Network).


                      Note
                      A list of all of the options and additional information can be viewed at the following link:
                      Command line parameter for setup.exe (https://flexeracommunity.force.com/customer/articles/
                      en_US/INFO/Setup-exe-Command-Line-Parameters)

4.8 Starting Create MyConfig


                  There are three versions:


Version 1
                  1. In the Windows Control panel, select "Programs and functions".
                  2. Select "Create MyConfig", and then click on "Change".
                  3. Select the program parts that you wish to add or remove.


Version 2
                  ● Start the ""setup.exe"" file again on the DVD.
                     – You then go to the same dialogs - and you can proceed as for version 1.
                     – The precondition is that the same "setup.exe" is used as was used to install the version.


Version 3
                  ● Use control file "OPFILE.txt (Page 32)" to subsequently add or delete program components.
                    If, for features, you specify another configuration, then precisely this is installed.
                     – If you have already installed "Topo," and you also wish to install "Diff," the "Features"
                       parameter looks like this:
                       Features=Topo,Diff
                     – If only want to install Diff instead of the installed Topo, then the "Features" parameter
                       looks like this:
                       Features=Diff
                  These three versions can be combined. For example, this means you can first use version 1,
                  for a subsequent change, version 3, and later, for a new change, version 2.

6.2               Introduction

                      Note
                      Setup of documentation: Operating Manual / online help
                      The contents of Section Diff are identical in the Operating Manual and the online help.


                      Diff is software for displaying and comparing SINUMERIK archives, folders, general and
                      special files of the SINUMERIK 840D sl control.
                      You can also change and save SINUMERIK archives with Diff.
                      Selected data can be exported from SINUMERIK archives or data can be imported into
                      SINUMERIK archives.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                       45
Create MyConfig - Diff
6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                  Data class archives of the SINUMERIK 828D control have restricted functionality, i.e. identifiers
                  cannot be inserted or imported into this archive.
                  Diff is furthermore capable of creating archives directly from a control or loading archives to a
                  control. Only values of existing identifiers can be changed - or identifiers and their associated
                  values removed.

                  Diff comprises the following three components:

                  ● SINUMERIK archive →         Display and comparison of NC, drive or display data from SIN‐
                    comparison                  UMERIK archives or files.
                    (Page 46)
                  ● Folder comparison →         Display and comparison of folders, SINUMERIK archives and
                    (Page 104)                  archives in ZIP, TGZ and TAR format.
                  ● File comparison   →         Display and comparison of files.
                    (Page 124)
                  The three components of Diff can be called individually and any number of times in the
                  application and are each displayed as a tab.
                  The Diff software can be used to support the configuration of packages with Expert, and
                  independent of Expert, also as standard comparison software.
                  In all three components, you can edit the opened archives, folders or files.
                  The data determined with Diff is provided in such a way that it can be incorporated directly into
                  a project.
                  The advantage of Diff that makes it so unique is the fact that it can process SINUMERIK
                  archives in the PC or punched tape format and also special SINUMERIK files and SINUMERIK
                  data structures.
                  Diff shows NC and drive data in a structured fashion in the SINUMERIK archive comparison.




6.3            SINUMERIK archive comparison


6.3.1          General information on the SINUMERIK archive comparison
                  Any number of comparison objects (SINUMERIK archives or Sub files) can be imported,
                  displayed and compared in a SINUMERIK archive comparison.
                  The comparison is realized at the data level.

                  The SINUMERIK archive comparison supports the comparison of the following objects:
                  ● SINUMERIK archives in PC format and in punched-tape format
                  ● Drive archives in ASCII and ACX format
                  ● NC/drive/display data files (INI, OPT, TEA…) in ASCII format
                  ● Manipulation tasks of a CMC project (only the value assignments outside of script)
                  ● Data nodes within a comparison object




                                                                         SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
46                                                                        Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                 Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                    6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                       The SINUMERIK archive comparison extracts the NC, drive, and display data from the
                       SINUMERIK archives and displays these in a structured fashion.
                       Unlike file comparison involving INI files, data is not compared line by line, but according to its
                       identifiers. If the same identifiers occur a multiple number of times, these are only displayed
                       once and the value of the last one that was imported is used.
                       The SINUMERIK archive comparison can be performed between different objects opened for
                       comparison, but also within one object (selective).
                       The comparison result is prepared in a structured fashion.
                       Data from the objects being compared can be copied to the clipboard and then used in other
                       applications (Expert, ...).
                       It is possible to remove or insert identifiers and change the values of existing identifiers for
                       SINUMERIK archives.
                       Diff permits the user to resave an open SINUMERIK archive with modified data as SINUMERIK
                       archive.

                       Note
                       In the SINUMERIK archive comparison, Diff always displays the data contained in the
                       comparison object if no settings were made in the comparison configuration to exclude data
                       (Expert list or filter).
                       For SINAMICS drive data, there are parameters (r or p) that can be displayed online on the HMI.
                       However, they are not part of an archive and therefore cannot be displayed by Diff.

                     Note
                     Load archive from control / load to control
                     To create an archive from the control or load an archive to the control, you are prompted to set
                     a password for the "Manufacturer NC access level" via the "Set password" dialog.
                     When the password has been entered once and the "Save password" checkbox activated, the

Description of the areas/functions in the SINUMERIK archive comparison window
                      The individual functions of the SINUMERIK archive comparison are described in more detail
                      below:

                      ① Data view tab
                      In the "Data view" tab, you can display the data in 2 different views: in the Normal or Selective
                      mode. To do this, switch between the 2 "Normal" and "Selective" tabs.
                      By switching over the tab, you can set an opened archive from "Data view" to "Folder view". As
                      a consequence, you do not have to additionally open Folder comparison.




                                                                                     SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
60                                                                                    Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                               Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                 6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                      ② Folder view tab
                      The folder structure of an archive is displayed in the "Folder view". The representation and
                      functionality of the Folder view corresponds to that of the Folder comparison (Page 104).
                      By switching over the tab, you can set an opened archive from "Folder view" to "Data view".

                      ③ Edit mode button
                      The Edit mode can be activated or deactivated by clicking the button. You can only make
                      changes, delete values and add values or identifiers in the "Data view" or "Folder view" tabs
                      when the Edit mode is activated. You must deactivate the edit mode to toggle between these
                      tabs.

                      Note
                      The NC root files "*.ini" and the drive data "*.tea" cannot be edited.


                      ④ Normal tab
                      In this area, the data nodes of the comparison objects are shown in a tree structure in the
                      "Normal" comparison mode.
                      In the "Normal" comparison mode, the data structures of all comparison objects (archives, files)
                      are placed one on top of the other and the comparison result is visualized using special node
                      icons.
                      For example, the NC data of axis 1 (AX1) is always compared with the data of axis 1 or the data
                      of drive object 2 (DO2) compared with the data of drive object 2 of another archive.
                      The data structure is formed from all of the data end nodes involved in the comparison of the
                      objects.
                      In this mode, the end nodes of all comparison objects that are located within the selected folder
                      are compared with one another.

                      Table 6-8      Meaning of the icons

                           The equal character in the area node indicates that the data of the objects being com‐
                           pared is identical below this area node.
                           The unequal character in the area node indicates that not all of the data of the objects
                           being compared is identical below this area node.
                           The equal character in the end node indicates that the data of the objects being compared
                           is identical within the end node.
                           The unequal character in the end node indicates that not all of the data of the objects
                           being compared is identical within the end node.
                      The values specified in brackets after a data node specify how many identifiers of a node are
                      displayed and how many identifiers there are in a node.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                           61
Create MyConfig - Diff
6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                  Examples:

                  Table 6-9    Node/identifier display

                                     This node contains 1173 identifiers, all of which are displayed.
                                     This node displays 1086 of a total of 1173 identifiers.
                                     Fewer identifiers than those available are displayed because of the expert
                                     list or the filter.

                  ⑤ Selective tab
                  In this area, the data nodes of the comparison objects are shown in a tree structure in the
                  "Selective" comparison mode.
                  In the "Selective" comparison mode, the data structures of all comparison objects, such as
                  archives and files, are placed one below the other. The the structure is separately established
                  for every comparison object.
                  Contrary to the "Normal" comparison mode, in the "Selective" comparison mode, all data end
                  nodes of the same type can be compared with one another as required.
                  You can select the data that you wish to compare by activating the end nodes.

                  ⑥ Extend selection / Reduce selection buttons
                  Extend selection / Extend All: You can either display a selected folder or the complete data view
                  with all subfolders and nodes in the tree structure.
                  Reduce selection / Reduce All: You can either reduce the selected folder or the complete data
                  view to the main folder. As a consequence, all subfolders and nodes are then no longer visible.

                  ⑥ Display result: Different / Equal / Not available in all comparison objects
                  These values provide information as to how many identifiers in the comparison results have
                  unequal (red) or equal (black) values or which values do not exist in all comparison objects
                  (blue/green arrows).

                  ⑦ Expert list and filterconfigurations
                  If the functions "Expert list" and "Filter" are active in the comparison configuration, the relevant
                  icons will be displayed.
                  Double-clicking the icons opens the expert list or filter in the comparison configuration.

                  Note
                  Using "Expert list" and "Filter," you can exclude non-relevant identifiers from the comparison,
                  so that these are no longer displayed.


                  ⑧ Display of the comparison configuration
                  The comparison configuration that is being used in the actual comparison is displayed in this
                  field.
                  The comparison configuration is opened with a double-click.

                                                                                                          Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                         6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                      ⑩ Display short description for the marked parameters
                      A brief description of the selected parameters is displayed in the text area with yellow
                      background.

                      ⑪ Result from the Normal tab / Selective tab
                      The data of the nodes selected in areas ④ and ⑤ is prepared in a tabular form in this area of
                      the user interface.
                      The identifiers are listed in the column to the far left, and in all of the additional columns, the
                      associated values of the individual comparison objects (archives, nodes).

                      The comparison results are color-coded to make it easier to interpret the results:
                      ● Identifiers shown in black indicate that all values of the comparison object for this particular
                        identifier are the same.
                      ● Identifiers shown in red indicate that not all values of the comparison object for this particular
                        identifier are the same.
                      ● Values shown in blue are values that the user changed in the "Selective" mode.
                      The number as prefix in the column header of the values defines the comparison object
                      (archive, file) to which these values belong.

                      ⑬ Short designation of data end node
                      The data end nodes have a code that defines the data area from which the data originated.
                      For SINAMICS data, the following information is contained in the node designation.

6.3.3          Configuration


SINUMERIK archive comparison
                  You call the dialog to configure the SINUMERIK archive comparison via the "Comparison
                  configuration" button .
                  In the "Configuration - NC data comparison" dialog, you can manage various comparison
                  configurations. For example, you can create, edit and delete comparison configurations.
                  You define all criteria to be considered for a SINUMERIK archive comparison in a comparison
                  configuration.
                  In order to provide the configurations to other users, you can export and import configurations.
                  You will find further information in Section "Exporting and importing configurations (Page 146)".




                                                                                     SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo

                                 4

                       ①      List of the available comparison configurations
                       ②      Buttons for managing the configurations
                       ③      Main nodes in the structure tree
                       ④      Background color

                      ① List of the available comparison configurations
                      The existing comparison configurations are listed in this area of the "Configuration - NC data
                      comparison" dialog. You can select the required comparison configuration by clicking it.
                      Configurations shown in gray are user-specified configurations; you can change these, but you
                      cannot delete them, and you can restore them at any time

                      ② Buttons for managing the configurations
                      You can manage the configurations using these buttons.
                      A new configuration is created via "Add", which you can adapt.
                      You make a copy of the selected comparison configuration via "Duplicate".

Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                        65

                  With "Restore default", the changes to the specified comparison configuration are undone.

                  Note
                  The "Restore default" button is only active if a user-specified configuration has been selected,
                  the contents of which are no longer the same as the default setting.
                  This means, that in addition to restoring the default setting, this button can also be used to
                  check whether the contents are identical with those of the default setting.


                  ③ Main nodes in the structure tree
                  You can save the properties that belong to the selected configuration in this area of the dialog;
                  these properties include display criteria, filter criteria and a comment.

                  ④ Background color
                  So that the user can immediately recognize how to select certain comparison configurations,
                  you can define a separate background color for each comparison configuration.


Display tab
                  In the "Display" tab, you define which main nodes should be displayed in the data structure tree,
                  assuming that data is available in the comparison object (archive or file) for this main node.
                  Further, you can define whether the data should be sorted in alphabetic order or similar to that
                  used in an NC in the data list.


Expert list tab
                  Using the Expert list, you can specify a number of identifiers that should either be included or
                  excluded for the comparison.
                  Always enter the identifiers completely in the "Expert list". The only exception is the field data
                  in the identifier.

                  Example:
                  A $MA_CTRLOUT_NR[0] entry in an inclusion list precisely includes this identifier.
                  A $MA_CTRLOUT_NR entry in an inclusion list includes all identifiers that belong to this field, i.e.
                  $MA_CTRLOUT_NR[0] and $MA_CTRLOUT_NR[1].

Value range tab
                  In the "Value range" tab, the value-based comparison of floating-point numbers is displayed at
                  significant points.




                  Floating point numbers are saved separately and internally in the computer in mantissa and
                  exponent.
                  The exponent is adapted in such a way that the mantissa is normalized, i.e. in the range of 1 <=
                  m < 10.
                  The maximum possible number of significant digits is thus 7 for floating values and 15 for
                  double values.
                  Other inaccuracies can occur as a result of parameter calculations, which can be consciously
                  ignored during the comparison.
                  When the comparison algorithm is activated, the difference of the values is normalized via the
                  absolute value of the values. If this is then less than the specified significant digit (the mantissa),
                  the values are considered equal.


Comment tab
                  Any comments for the selected comparison configuration can be saved in the "Comment" tab.

6.3.4             Copying/exporting data from the SINUMERIK archive comparison
                      In the SINUMERIK archive comparison, data identifiers and the associated values can be
                      copied to the clipboard or exported to a file.
                      For instance, the copied or exported data can be used in manipulation tasks of Expert, in Excel
                      for documentation, in another software application or where relevant, also in a SINUMERIK
                      archive comparison in Diff.
                      In the SINUMERIK archive comparison, depending on the data marking, there are two different
                      copy and/or export formats "Value assignment" and "Value table".


Copy/export format - "Value assignment"
                      For the copy/export format "Value assignment", data is extracted in the form "identifier=value".
                      This means that data is extracted with unique, fully qualified identifiers, a value for each
                      identifier as well as information about the source data area - and are saved in a form that can
                      be directly used in manipulation tasks of Expert.
                      This type of copy and export is the most frequently used type.
                      To copy or export data, select the values in the value column as shown below.


Example 1: Copying SINAMICS data

                  values and their identifiers to the clipboard or a file.

                   [B3_S3_PS3] ;V2.40.43.00
                   p45=1
                   p100=0
                   p105=1

Introduction
                  In the SINUMERIK data comparison, data can be pasted from the clipboard or imported from

                  Use only data in the clipboard or in a file in the form "identifier=value" (copy/export format,
                  "Value assignment").

                  Note
                  The copy/export format "Value table" from Diff is not supported for paste/import.


                  Using the context menu, it is possible to paste/import data to a value column ②.

6.3.6          Data jobs in the SINUMERIK archive comparison


6.3.6.1        Overview
                  In the SINUMERIK archive comparison, using data tasks, data can be converted, imported and
                  exported.
                  A configuration and an Excel template belong to a data task.


Supplementary conditions for data tasks
                  ● Data tasks are only available in the "Selective" comparison mode.
                  ● Data tasks can only be applied to data end nodes.




                                                                           SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
76                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                              Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison


Application examples for data tasks
                      ● Importing encoder data.
                        Encoder data saved in an Excel file (template) can be imported into an archive.
                      ● Exporting optimization data.
                        For the identifiers of optimization data saved in an Excel template, values can be added and
                        saved as Excel file.


Principle of operation of import tasks
                      When executing import tasks, values are imported into the clipboard from the "Import area" of
                      an Excel template.
                      In Diff, these values can be inserted at a data end node. When inserting values, the values of
                      existing identifiers can be overwritten and new identifiers can be inserted.


Principle of operation of export tasks
                      When executing export tasks, data identifiers are determined in an "Export area" of an Excel
                      template. These identifiers are searched for in a selected data end node in the data structure
                      of the SINUMERIK archive comparison and their values are transferred into an Excel template.
                      The "Save As" dialog allows the completed Excel template to be saved.
                      The "Save As" dialog is displayed, which allows the completed Excel template to be saved.


Principle of operation of conversion tasks
                      When executing conversion tasks, data identifiers are determined from an "Export area" of an
                      Excel template. These identifiers are searched for in a selected data end node in the data
                      structure of the SINUMERIK archive comparison and their values are transferred to an Excel
                      template.
                      The conversion rule saved in the same Excel template is processed by Excel without any
                      visualization. In so doing, values are generated for the saved import identifiers and these are
                      then imported to Diff from the "Import area". The imported values are saved in the clipboard,
                      and can be inserted into Diff at a data end node.
                      When inserting values, the values of existing identifiers can be overwritten and new identifiers
                      can be inserted.
                      The Excel file with the converted data can be saved.


6.3.6.2           Configuring data jobs
                      The dialog to configure data tasks is called from the "Tools" > "Data comparison" > "Configure
                      data task…" main menu.
                      The dialog to configure data tasks is equivalent to the dialog for the comparison configuration
                      and should be used in the same way.
                      You can also export or import configurations, for instance, to provide them to other users (see
                      Exporting and importing configurations (Page 146)).

6.3.8           CMC scripts in Diff


6.3.8.1         Introduction


Analysis and manipulations of archives via CMC scripts in Diff
                    Diff supports the advanced analysis and manipulation of archives via CMC script. You can
                    implement complex data exports, for example, via the script functions for writing files. The
                    Script Editor can be used to create and edit the scripts. A command line interface for executing
                    the CMC scripts in Diff is provided for automation tasks.

                    License
                    You require a license to use CMC scripts in Diff.
                    The function as extension "DIFF Scripting" is under license.


Further information
                    In Diff you can apply CMC scripts on SINUMERIK archives.




                                                                           SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
88                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                 6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                      This allows you to make complex controlled data exports from archives, without having to
                      create a CMC package. You can also manipulate the data archive. As Shield processes the
                      CMC script and archive, a large percentage of the convenient functions of Shield are also used.
                      You can start the scripts from the Diff interface - or using a command line call.

                      Syntax used
                      All elements of the CMC script language from Expert can be used apart from the following
                      package-specific exceptions.
                      Exceptions:
                      ● ResText()
                      ● ResFile()
                      ● Redo()
                      ● Version()
                      ● #include
                      ● Prepare()
                      ● Patch()
                      ● Access to display data of the HMI, sections:
                         – BD[SL]
                         – [SL]
                         – BD[SL].$MM_...
                      ● PCU / NCU:
                        You cannot use areas PCU and NCU for the argument <area> in functions and procedures.
                      ● CMC system variables Up.$...


6.3.8.2           Script Editor


Introduction
                      CMC provides the "Create MyConfig Script Editor", which is subsequently called just "Script
                      Editor".
                      A syntax check is performed when you work with the "Script Editor". Further, you are supported
                      by syntax highlighting, IntelliSense and a comprehensive context menu, for example.
                      You can create, edit and check scripts for different applications by selecting a script library.

6.3.8.3        Script libraries
                  Frequently used script blocks can be stored in libraries as procedures or functions so that these
                  script blocks are available for several projects or CMC scripts in Diff.
                  You can create and change script libraries via the Script Editor.
                  The script libraries are integrated in the CMC project in Expert in the "Package" tab via the "List
                  of script libraries".


Notes on script libraries
                  Using script libraries - and therefore your own functions and procedures - is also possible in
                  CMC scripts in Diff.
                  You create a script library with the "Create MyConfig Script Editor". You save the script library
                  next to the CMC script for Diff or in a path of the environment variable %UP_LIB_PATH%.
                  You can obtain everything you need to know about a script library from the documentation
                  about Create MyConfig Expert > Section "Editing script libraries" (Page 418).

                  Note
                  Using script libraries in CMC scripts in Diff
                  You have the following ways to publish your own libraries if you want to use your own functions
                  and procedures from your script libraries in CMC:
                  ● Store your libraries next to the CMC script for Diff. In this way, all scripts are in the same
                     folder.
                  ● Store the libraries in a path (folder) of the environment variable %UP_LIB_PATH%.
                  ● Include your archive path in the variable.
                  Environment variable %UP_LIB_PATH% is only relevant when executing CMC scripts in Diff.
                  The Create MyConfig Script Editor as individual application and Shield know this variable.




                  Note
                  Environment variable %UP_LIB_PATH%
                  Only the Create MyConfig Script Editor as individual application and Shield know and process
                  the environment variable %UP_LIB_PATH%, which contains the paths to your script libraries.
                  After a standard installation of Create MyConfig, the following paths are at %UP_LIB_PATH%:
                  ● C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create MyConfig 4.8\UpLib
                  ● C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create MyConfig 4.8\UpLib
                  You can add your own paths to these environment variables.

92                                                                         Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                 Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                  6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison




                      Note
                      Recognition of script libraries through Shield
                      When starting a CMC script in Diff via the user interface or a command line call, Shield reads
                      the script libraries in succession in the following order
                      ● Libraries next to the script
                      ● 1st path in %UP_LIB_PATH%
                      ● 2nd path in %UP_LIB_PATH%
                      ● ...
                      ● nth. path in %UP_LIB_PATH%
                      If the definition of a procedure or function is present in more than one script library (multiple
                      definition of the same function or procedure), Shield generates an appropriate error message
                      at the manual start of the CMC script via the user interface of Diff. You then have the option of
                      continuing or cancelling.
                      When the CMC script is started via the command line, Shield writes the error message to the
                      logbook. Shield uses the first definition found in accordance with the search order described
                      above.




                      Note
                      Recognition of script libraries through the Script Editor
                      The Script Editor reads all existing script libraries only once at the start of the application.
                      If you have created a new script library or changed an existing one, restart the Script Editor so
                      that the Script Editor reads in the changes.




                      Note
                      Environment variable %UP_LIB_PATH% in Expert
                      You can obtain information about environment variables %UP_LIB_PATH% in Expert at:
                      Expert > Script language > Script libraries > Secondary conditions when using script libraries
                      (Page 421).

                      You must always use fully qualified sections to be able to read and write access archived data,
                      e.g NC[C1], PS[B3_S3_PS3].
                      Use simple identifiers under fully qualified sections.
                      You only use fully qualified identifiers for read access operations.

6.3.8.6             Using system variables

                      System variables for CMC scripts in Diff are described in this Section, and examples of their use
                      given.


Up.$Env.BatchMode
                      Command line execution of CMC scripts in Diff is always realized in the "Batch mode".
                      Using system variable Up.$Env.BatchMode, you can interrogate as to whether the CMC
                      script is in the "Batch mode", i.e. the CMC script was started via the command line.


Example
                      If you do not wish to call any dialogs while running the script in the "Batch mode", then make the
                      call dependent on the dialog of variables Up.$Env.BatchMode.

                      If Up.$Env.BatchMode == false
                       Msg("The CMC script was started from the user interface of Diff.")
                      EndIf


Up.$Script.ScriptFile
                      Variable Up.$Script.ScriptFile contains the absolute path of the script file that is
                      executed.
                      Using this variable, you check whether the correct CMC script was started.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                                       95
Create MyConfig - Diff
6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison


Example

                  If Up.$Script.ScriptFile != "P:\Manufact\Diff_Script\myscript.upscr"
                   Error("The incorrect CMC script was started! It is possible that
                   this CMC script is not current!")
                  EndIf

                  Note
                  Case sensitivity of paths
                  It is important that you take into account the case sensitivity if you perform a string comparison
                  of paths. Under Windows, this is not relevant in the file system.
                  When comparing string values in the CMC script you must take into account the case sensitivity.




Up.$Script.ArcFile
                  For command line execution, the system variable contains the absolute path of the result
                  archive, which was specified using the command line switch /outarc.
                  When starting the CMC script via the user interface, the variable contains the absolute path of
                  the (result) archive on which the CMC script is applied.


Example
                  MSG("The archive '$(Up.$Script.ArcFile)' is manipulated by the CMC
                  script.")


Up.$Script.Result
                  You require this system variable for data export of your CMC script in Diff. All files that you
                  assign to these system variables in the CMC script are transferred from Diff to the instance that
                  calls the script.
                  When starting the CMC script from the user interface of the Diff, the files are opened after the
                  script has been run and transferred to the user. The user saves the files with "Save as" in the
                  linked standard application at the required location.
                  When starting the CMC script from the command line, after the script has been executed, the
                  files are saved or transferred corresponding to the argument at switch /result.
                  You only require system variable Up.$Script.Result if these two conditions are satisfied:
                  ● When using procedures that generate files,
                    File operations, e.g. TraceToFile()
                  ● When using relative paths in these procedures,
                    e.g. because the CMC script is to run on various configured computers.

96                                                                         Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                 Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                  6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison



                      Note
                      Observe relative paths
                      Only relative paths must be transferred to these system variables.
                      Absolute paths are not permitted.




Example 1 - exporting a file

                      Content CMC script "myScript.upscr":

                      TraceToFile(".\myTrace.txt", "my trace output")
                      Up.$Script.Result = ".\myTrace.txt"

                      Content batch script (CMD) for command line:

                      @echo off
                      echo script is running ...
                      set cmc_diff="C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create
                      MyConfig 4.8\Diff.exe"
                      set script="myScript.upscr"
                      set arc_file="mync.arc"
                      set out_arc="mync_new.arc"
                      set script_log="myScript.html"
                      set result="C:\Temp\myResult.txt"

                      %cmc_diff% /script %skript% /inarc %arc_file% /outarc %out_arc% /
                      result %result% /scriptlog %script_log% /log cmdLog.xml
                      echo Errorlevel is: %Errorlevel%
                      Pause

                      Result after executing the batch and CMC script:
                      After executing the CMC script using the command line call, the content of file "myTrace.txt" is
                      located in file "C:\Temp\myResult.txt".
                      After executing the CMC script when started at the Diff user interface, the content of file
                      "myTrace.txt" is located in the editor. You save the file using "Save as" at a location that you can
                      arbitrarily select.


Example 2 - exporting several files
                      When exporting several files, use a semicolon to separate the files. Assign the files as string
                      variable to system variable Up.$Script.Result.
                      The path of a folder is saved in the batch script for the argument of switch /result. The
                      exported files are saved in this folder.

                  FileCopy(ARC, "NC/initial.ini", RTS, ".\initial.ini")

                  Up.myWorkingDir = "."

6.3.8.10       Example, manipulating archive data
                  A CMC script to manipulate NC axis machine data could, in practice, look like the following.
                  The precondition is that no axis gaps are generated and the data sets actually exist.
                  If axis gaps exist, and/or data sets are missing, then you must make an appropriate check and
                  integrate the appropriate processing.




                                                                        SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
102                                                                      Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                          Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                               6.3 SINUMERIK archive comparison


Content, script "Manipu_NC_Axis_Values.upscr"


                      If UP.$Script.EditMode != true
                       Error("You have forgotten to activate the edit mode!")
                      EndIf
                      NC[C1] ;Fully qualified section
                      Up.nAxis = 1
                      While(Up.nAxis < $ON_NUM_AXES_IN_SYSTEM+1)
                       Up.nDataSet = 0
                       While(Up.nDataSet < 6);write value for all 5 data sets
                         If $MA_IS_ROT_AX[AX$(Up.nAxis)] == 0 ;axis is a linear axis
                          N36200 $MA_AX_VELO_LIMIT[$(Up.nDataSet),AX$(Up.nAxis)] =
                          $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX$(Up.nAxis)] * 1.12
                         Else ;axis is a spindle
                          N36200 $MA_AX_VELO_LIMIT[$(Up.nDataSet),AX$(Up.nAxis)] =
                          $MA_GEAR_STEP_MAX_VELO_LIMIT[$(Up.nDataSet),AX$(Up.nAxis)] *
                          1.13
                         EndIf
                         Up.nDataSet += 1
                       EndWhile
                       ;all data without data set
                       If $MA_IS_ROT_AX[AX$(Up.nAxis)] == 0 ;axis is a linear axis
                         N36060 $MA_STANDSTILL_VELO_TOL[AX$(Up.nAxis)]=4
                       Else ;axis is a spindle
                         N36060 $MA_STANDSTILL_VELO_TOL[AX$(Up.nAxis)]=0.012
                       EndIf
                       N36030 $MA_STANDSTILL_POS_TOL[AX$(Up.nAxis)]=3
                       N36040 $MA_STANDSTILL_DELAY_TIME[AX$(Up.nAxis)]=0.5
                       Up.nAxis += 1
                      EndWhile


Content batch script (CMD) for command line


                      @echo off
                      echo script is running ...

                      set cmc_diff="C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create
                      MyConfig 4.8\Diff.exe"
                      set skript="Manipu_NC_Axis_Values.upscr"
                      set arc_file="mync.arc"
                      set out_arc="mync_new.arc"

6.4            Folder comparison


6.4.1          General information
                  In a Folder comparison of Diff, you can compare two comparison objects with each other, insert
                  or delete files or folders, and store the modified objects again. The comparison and display of
                  the comparison results is realized at the folders and files level. This means that the contents of
                  the files are compared optionally, but not displayed.
                  The folder comparison supports comparison and editing of the following objects:
                  ● Folders/directories,
                  ● SINUMERIK archive in the PC format
                  ● SINUMERIK archive in the punched tape format
                  ● ZIP archive
                  ● TGZ archive
                  ● TAR archive
                  Because unpacked archives usually represent a structure consisting of folders and files, similar
                  rules apply to comparing and editing.
                  In the folder comparison, files with the same name are compared for size, date, version, and
                  binary contents.
                  The comparison result is prepared both qualitatively and quantitatively.
                  From the comparison objects, folders and files can be copied to the clipboard and to other
                  applications (Expert, Windows Explorer, etc.).

⑧      Status bar



Description of the areas/functions in the Folder comparison window
                    The individual functions of the folder comparison are described in more detail below:

                    ①Folder structure - Representation of the folders with the associated comparison objects in
                    the tree structure
                    In this area, the folders of the comparison objects are shown in a tree structure arranged one
                    on top of the other. The comparison result is visualized using special folder icons.

                    ② Colored comparison of the comparison objects
                    The content of the folder selected in the ① area is displayed next to each other for both
                    comparison objects (②). The center column ③ with the comparison result icons also serves
                    as separation between the left-hand and right-hand comparison objects.
                    The comparison results are color-coded to make it easier to interpret the results:
                    ● Objects that are only available on the left-hand side are shown in green.
                    ● Unequal objects or properties available on both sides are shown in red.
                    ● Equal objects or properties available on both sides are shown in black.
                    ● Objects that are only available on the right-hand side are shown in blue.
                    The contents of the column can be sorted in ascending or descending order by clicking the
                    column header.

                    Note
                    The contents of the files are only compared in the binary notation if this has been preselected
                    in the comparison configuration (see Configuration (Page 118)).
                    The date for the comparison is not relevant for folders.

                    Note
                    PLC blocks identification
                    If PLC blocks are marked yellow, they are Safety Integrated plus blocks.




                    Figure 6-14    PLC blocks identification - Safety Integrated plus

                    ③ Column of the comparison result icons
                    Column with the comparison result icons, to separate the left-hand and right-hand comparison
                    objects.
                    When the edit mode is activated, you can change the icons for synchronization purposes by left-
                    clicking or via the context menu.

                      Significance of the comparison icons:

                             A green arrow indicates that the folder is only available in the left-hand comparison
                             object.
                             The unequal character indicates that the contents of the folder are not identical.
                             The equal character indicates that the contents of both folders are identical.
                             A blue arrow indicates that the folder is only available in the right-hand comparison
                             object.

                      ④ Assignment of the comparison results icon/value (status bar bottom right)

                      The value in front of the slash specifies how many of these files can be seen in the selected
                      folder.
                      The value after the slash shows the total number of these files that are contained in both
                      comparison objects.

                      Example:


                      Specifies that there are 8 unequal files from a total of 14 in the currently selected folder.

                      ⑤ Special features context menu
                      The "Open", "Send to" and "Copy" entries can be used to view and extract files from archives.
                      The entry "Open with file comparison" or a double-click opens the files contained in the selected
                      line in the data comparison of Diff.
                      The other entries can be used to edit a selected file or a selected folder.

                      ⑥ Comparison configuration
                      A filter is used in the comparison configuration (see Configuration (Page 118)).
                      The comparison configuration is opened with a double-click.

                      Note
                      Using inclusion and exclusion filters, it is possible that not all of the files of the folder or archive
                      are displayed any longer.


                      ⑦ Display of the current comparison configuration (status bar)
                      The comparison configuration that is being used in the actual comparison is displayed in this
                      field (see Configuration (Page 118)).
                      The comparison configuration is opened with a double-click.

Comparison tab

                  ④ Compare file size
                  For activated size comparison, the size of the files and folders is considered.
                  If you do not activate the option checkbox, a check is only made whether files and folders exist
                  in both comparison objects.
                  This option is activated as standard.

                  ⑤ Date of the last change to the file option button
                  When the date/version comparison is activated, then for this selection, Diff also takes into
                  account the date that the file was last changed - and displays this in either black or red.
                  The date is not relevant for folders.

                  ⑥ Date field/version/drop-down list of regular identification expressions option button
                  SINUMERIK archives can contain cycles.
                  The cycle version number is specified in the file. When making a comparison, the version
                  number provides more information than the date and can be used for the comparison.
                  In order to be able to compare the version numbers, the files in the first 10 lines are checked for
                  the character string, which is then described using a regular identification expression.
                  A regular expression that is generally used is already selected in the specified comparison
                  configuration "SINUMERIK archive".
                  You can also create user-defined regular expressions in the drop-down list.
                  You can find an introduction to regular expressions under "Using regular expressions in Diff".

                  ⑦ "Additional comparison criteria" checkbox
                  The content of the files is only compared byte-by-byte when you select the additional
                  comparison criterion "Compare binary content of the files".

                      Table 6-21     Examples of filters:

                       *.ini                      The * (asterisk) expression represents any number of any characters.
                                                  If the entry is defined in the inclusion filter, only file names with the file exten‐
                                                  sion ini are displayed, and all others are hidden. If "*.ini" is present in the
                                                  exclusion filter, all file names with the "ini" extension are not displayed.
                       cycle8?.spf                The question mark represents precisely one character (any character).
                                                  If you have defined the entry in the inclusion filter, files with the "cycle8" name
                                                  plus any arbitrary character and the "spf" file extension are displayed, and all
                                                  others are hidden.
                                                  File names with the designation "cycle8?.spf" can therefore be called as fol‐
                                                  lows: cycle80.spf, cycle81.spf, cycle8a.spf..., etc.

6.4.5           Copying from the folder comparison
                  Files, folders or complete folder structures can be copied from the comparison objects of the
                  folder comparison to the clipboard and then, e.g. in Expert, inserted in a component.
                  This means that it is possible to extract files from SINUMERIK, ZIP, TAR or TGZ archives,
                  without having to use a Create MyConfig external software.

6.4.6             Archive as user or SDB archive
                      The following archives with different properties are available for theSINUMERIK 840D sl:
                      ● Commissioning archive (Commissioning archive)
                      ● SDB archive (PLC hardware upgrade archive, PLC HW Config archive)
                      ● USER archive
                      The specified archives are also designated as "SINUMERIK archive" with file extension ARC.
