                      In the folder comparison, the file type is selected and saved in the dialog under main menu File
                      > Save under.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                           123
Create MyConfig - Diff
6.5 File comparison


                  The following archives can be generated:
                  ● Commissioning archive
                         – "Standard SINUMERIK archive", just the same as it is also created in SINUMERIK
                           Operate, it can include all data areas and control commands for a memory reset, loads
                           standard data etc.
                  ● USER archive
                         – Can only contain the data areas (folders) HMI, PLC, and NC; only these are backed up.
                         – Does not include any drive and NC machine data - and no PLC-SDB blocks (HW
                           configuration).
                         – When loading, the memory is not reset, standard data is not loaded and no NCK reset is
                           executed.
                         – It is only possible to import USER archives via SINUMERIK Operate in the system data
                           nodes archive area.
                  ● SDB archive
                         – PLC hardware upgrade archive, just the same as also SINUMERIK Operate generates.
                         – Can only contain data areas (folders) PLC and CP - only these are backed up.
                         – Only the system data blocks SDB0 to SDBn (0B00000 to 0BFFFFF) are saved in the
                           PLC folder.
                         – When loading, the PLC memory is not reset, i.e user data and programs are kept.




6.5            File comparison


6.5.1          General information
                  In a file comparison using Diff, you can compare the contents of two files line-by-line.
                  The comparison result is processed from qualitative and quantitative perspectives.
                  Contents can be copied from the files line-by-line to the clipboard and used in other applications
                  (Expert ...).
                  In the edit mode, you can delete lines or characters directly in the file comparison, insert them
                  or copy them backwards and forwards between files.
                  It is also possible to simultaneously and externally process a file opened in the comparison.

                      ① Comparison result overview
                      The comparison result is shown over the complete content of both files in this bar as an

                      The colored dashes represent lines that are only available on the left-hand side, only on the

                       Color display                Meaning of the lines in the file comparison
                       Green                        Only available in the left-hand file.
                       Red                          Content is different.
                       Black                        Both files are identical.
                       Gray                         Identical in the relevant part of the line.
                       Blue                         Only available in the right-hand file.

                      ④ Comparison result symbols and color coding of lines
                      The lines of the files to be compared are displayed next to one another in this area and are color-
                      coded to make it easier to interpret the comparison result.

                                The green arrow and the line number with green background indicate that this line
                                only exists in the left-hand file.
                                The not equal sign and the line numbers with red background indicate that the con‐
                                tent of the line is not identical.
                                The black equals sign indicates that both lines are identical.
                                The gray equals sign indicates that the relevant part of the line match.
                                The blue arrow and the line number with blue background indicate that this line only
                                exists in the right-hand file.

                      Note
                      Non-relevant parts of a line, e.g. spaces or comments, can be defined in the comparison
                      configuration.
                      Further information can be found in Section Configuration (Page 137).

Filter tab
                      Using filters, parts of a line can be included in or excluded from the comparison based on
                      regular expressions.
                      Characters excluded from the comparison are shown in gray in the comparison results. This
                      means that the contents of a file are always displayed completely, but marked in color.
                      If only the relevant characters are identical in the line but non-relevant characters are different,
                      the comparison icon will be a gray equals sign.

                                                                                                



                      




                      




                      ①      The functionality of the inclusion and exclusion filter is activated using a check mark for "Parts of
                             a line..."
                             NOTE:
                             The filter icon is shown in the status bar if this function is activated.
                      ②      Filter entries can be created, edited and deleted via the context menu.
                      ③      Every filter entry can be individually activated or deactivated.

                  Examples of filters:

                      *;.*                      The regular expression (see AUTOHOTSPOT) which is used for ③ compri‐
                                                ses the following characters:
                                                A space, an asterisk, a semicolon, a period and an asterisk.
                                                The characters have the following significance:
                                                Space stands for itself
                                                Asterisk → is a quantifier for any number of leading characters as prefix
                                                Semicolon → stands for itself
                                                Period → stands for any character
                                                If this expression is used as exclusion filter, then it excludes all of the semi‐
                                                colons in the file and the following characters in this line that can be of any type.
                                                Comments identified using a semicolon are displayed, but are excluded from
                                                the comparison.

Alignment tab
                      In the "Alignment" tab, you can define how the individual lines of both files should be aligned
                      with one another after the comparison.



                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                         




                                                                                                                         


                                                                                                                         



                                                                                                                         




                       ①      Using this selection, you can define that all lines of the two files are aligned continuously next to
                              one another (line 1 next to line 1, line 2 next to line 2, etc.).
                              A search is not made across lines regarding identity or similarity.
                       ②      As an alternative to ①, this selection which defines that identical lines should be aligned next to
                              one another is more frequently used in practice.
                              This selection can be further refined or extended by making the appropriate entries for ③, ④
                              and ⑤.
                       ③      In the files to be compared, you can define sections that should be taken into consideration and
                              for identical section identifiers, these should be aligned next to one another as priority.
                              When the option is selected (using the context menu or double-click) a regular expression (see
                              AUTOHOTSPOT) should be saved in the entry field to describe the section identifier.
                              NOTE:
                              The lines found also have a yellow background in the comparison display.
                       ④      Further, you can define that in the files to be compared, lines with identical partial character
                              strings are aligned next to one another as first priority. When the option is selected, a regular
                              expression to describe the partial character string must be saved in the entry field.
                              For example, this function is used to define that in files which have the structure "identifier=
                              value", only identical identifiers are placed next to one another (compared).
                              NOTE:
                              The lines that are found also have a light yellow background in the comparison display.
                              NOTICE:
                              When selection ③ is activated, lines with identical partial character strings are only placed next
                              to one another (compared) if they are located in the same section.

                          means it is defined as to whether similar lines, depending on the degree of similarity, are shown

6.8             Use of regular expressions in Diff


6.8.1           General information on regular expressions
                     Regular expressions represent a general notation to describe text patterns. They are frequently
                     known as a type of programming language to test and manipulate texts.
                     A regular expression is a character string with syntactic rules which defines significant text
                     patterns or character strings in a general form. Regular expressions are used in Diff to identify
                     a significant character string and, if required, to filter it (e.g. all block numbers or all comments
                     in a cycle).
                     A regular expression comprises two types of characters:
                     ● Literal characters
                     ● Meta characters


Literal characters
                     Literal characters are characters that only represent themselves in a regular expression and
                     have no special significance.
                     A search with a regular expression that only contains literals, therefore corresponds to a
                     conventional character search.


Meta characters
                     Meta characters are characters that have a special function within regular expressions.

                     Some meta characters follow:
                     $ ^ { } [ ] ( ) | . * + ? \ -.
                     Similar to natural languages, literals can be considered as being the vocabulary, with meta
                     characters being the grammar of regular expressions.




                                                                               SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
156                                                                             Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                       Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                       6.8 Use of regular expressions in Diff


Escape sequence
                      If a meta character is required as literal character to formulate a regular expression, i.e. it must
                      only stand for itself, then the character must be masked with what is called an escape
                      sequence. This is achieved by prefixing a backslash "\".

                      Example
                      A regular expression should identify an open square bracket "[".
                      A square bracket must be prefixed with a backslash "\". Because a single square bracket is a
                      meta character, i.e. has a special function, see character classes.
                      In this case, "\[" must be written in the regular expression.




6.8.2             Meta characters in the regular expressions
                      The most important meta characters are shown in the following subsections which are
                      contained in the dialect of the regular expressions of Create MyConfig.


Character classes
                      In a regular expression, a character class defines one character, which may be one of the
                      characters contained in the character class.

                       Meta charac‐                                            Description
                       ters
                              .          Corresponds to any character with the exception of \n (line break).
                             [ ]         A character set available for selection can be defined using square brackets. The
                                         expression in the square brackets precisely stands for one character from this selec‐
                                         tion.
                           [acdb]        Corresponds to one single character which is contained in the specified character
                                         string. This means one a, one b, one c or one d. The sequence of the characters within
                                         the character class is of no significance.
                          [^acdb]        Corresponds to any, individual character which is not contained in the specified char‐
                                         acter string. If a ^ is not located at the beginning of the definition, then it should be
                                         considered as literal.
                                         For "character negation" the ^ can only be located within the square brackets and
                                         here, in turn, may only be used at the beginning!
                                         Outside a square bracket, ^ has a different meaning, see below: "Constructs".
                        [0-9a-fAF]       Adjacent characters can be specified as a range by using a hyphen.
                                         If the hyphen is written at the beginning or at the end of the character class or with
                                         backslash, i.e. \- then it stands for itself and is not valid as specifying a range.
                              \w         A character which is a letter, a number or an underscore.
                              \W         A character which is neither a letter, number nor underscore.
                              \s         Corresponds to any space character, i.e. space character, tabulator, line feed spec‐
                                         trum.
                              \S         Corresponds to any non-space characters.
                              \d         Corresponds to any decimal number, corresponds to [0-9].
                              \D         Corresponds to any non number, corresponds to [^0-9].
                              \t         Corresponds to a tab stop character.



SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                                    157
Create MyConfig - Diff
6.8 Use of regular expressions in Diff


                    Meta charac‐                                         Description
                    ters
                          \n        Corresponds to a line break.
                         \x20       Corresponds to an ASCII character in the hexadecimal notation (precisely two posi‐
                                    tions).
                         \u0020     Corresponds to a unicode character in the hexadecimal notation (precisely four po‐
                                    sitions).



Constructs

                    Meta charac‐                                         Description
                    ters
                           |        Several regular expressions can be combined to form a single one using alternation
                                    (logical OR).
                                    Example: cat|dog|tiger. (cat or dog or tiger)
                                    The match to the far left has priority.
                          ( )       The grouping is used to combine parts of regular expressions and to limit the range
                                    of validity of an alternation.
                                    Example: _(abc|xyz)_
                           ^        The meta character for the beginning of the line does not describe a character in the
                                    actual sense, but instead a position in a line.
                                    Example: ^[aA] requires a lower-case a or upper-case A at the beginning of the line.
                                    The ^ character in square brackets has a different meaning, it is used as negation of
                                    the character string.
                           $        The meta character for the end of the line does not describe a character in the actual
                                    sense, but instead a position in a line.
                                    Example: [aA]$ requires a lower-case a or an upper-case A at the end of the line.



Quantifier
                   Using quantifiers, you can specify how many times a specific component of a regular
                   expression must occur in order for a found character string to be considered a match. A
                   quantification expression is valid for the character or character set which is located directly in
                   front of it.

                    Meta charac‐                                         Description
                    ters
                           ?        Requires a null or a match.
                                    Example: _? or (abc|xyz)?.
                           +        Requires one or any number of matches.
                                    Example: a+ or [0-9]+.
                           *        Requires null or any number of matches.
                                    Example: \w* or (abc)*.
                          {n}       Requires precisely n matches.
                                    Example: (abc){2}.
                         {n,}       Requires a minimum of n matches, but there can also be more.
                                    Example: (abc){2,}.
                         {n,m}      Requires at least n matches, however a maximum of m matches.
                                    Example: \w {2,17}.




                                                                             SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
158                                                                           Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                        Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                       6.8 Use of regular expressions in Diff


6.8.3             Examples of regular expressions

                       Regular expression        Charac‐   Description
                                                 ter
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]                         Describes a section, e.g. [Version]
                                                           At the beginning of the line there should be an "open square brack‐
                                                           et" [ and then there should be at least one character other than a
                                                           "close square bracket" ] followed by a "close square bracket" ].
                                                           The remainder up to the end of the line is not specified.
                       ①②③④⑤...                            Numbers indicate the position of the character in the regular ex‐
                                                           pression.
                       The regular expression is described below from the left to the right:
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ①^        Here, the beginning of the line, i.e. the described expression should
                                                           be located at the beginning of the line.
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ②\        Escape character; the "open square bracket" [ should stand for
                                                           itself as literal and not as meta character of a character set.
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ③[        Character stands for itself, i.e. at the beginning of the line there
                                                           should be an "open square bracket[.
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ④[        Starting definition of a character set (character is a meta character).
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ⑤^        Here, a negation character, i.e. the characters specified in the char‐
                                                           acter set, should not occur.
                                                           The character negation is only possible within square brackets,
                                                           therefore, brackets are used for characters ④ and ⑧.
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ⑥\        Escape character; the "close square bracket" ] should stand for
                                                           itself as literal and not as meta character of a character set.
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ⑦]        This character stands for itself.
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ⑧]        End definition of a character set
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ⑨+        Requires one match or as many matches as specified, i.e. there
                                                           must be at least one character, which is not a "]".
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ⑩\        Escape character; the "close square bracket" ] should stand for
                                                           itself as literal and not as meta character of a character set.
                       ^\[[^\]]+\]               ⑪]        This character stands for itself.



                       Regular expression        Charac‐   Description
                                                 ter
                       ^[^=]+=                             Describes a value assignment (identifier = value)
                                                           e.g. Version = 1.0.3
                                                           At the beginning of the line there should be at least one character,
                                                           which is not an equal sign "=". This expression (^[^=]+) stands
                                                           for the "identifier" in the value assignment.
                                                           This should then be followed by an equal sign "=" and the remainder
                                                           of the line, the value, is not specified.
                       ①②③④⑤...                            Numbers indicate the position of the character in the regular ex‐
                                                           pression.
                       The regular expression is described below from the left to the right:
                       ^[^=]+=                   ①^        Here, the beginning of the line, i.e. the described expression should
                                                           be located at the beginning of the line.

Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                                        159
Create MyConfig - Diff
6.8 Use of regular expressions in Diff


                    Regular expression      Charac‐     Description
                                            ter
                    ^[^=]+=                 ②[          Start of the definition of a character set (character is a meta char‐
                                                        acter).
                    ^[^=]+=                 ③^          Here, a negation character, i.e. the characters specified in the char‐
                                                        acter set should not occur.
                    ^[^=]+=                 ④=          Equal sign (literal) stands for itself.
                    ^[^=]+=                 ⑤]          End of the definition of a character set.
                    ^[^=]+=                 ⑥+          Requires one match or as many matches as specified, i.e. there
                                                        must be at least one character, which is not an equal sign.
                    ^[^=]+=                 ⑦=          Equal sign (literal) stands for itself.



                    Regular expression         Character            Description
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)                                Describes a CHANDATA operation in an NC-INI file,
                                                                    e.g. CHANDATA(1)
                                                                    CHANDATAshould be at the beginning of the line, fol‐
                                                                    lowed by a "open round bracket", followed by at least
                                                                    one digit, followed by a "close round bracket".
                    ①②③④⑤...                                        Numbers indicate the position of the character in the
                                                                    regular expression.
                    The regular expression is described below from the left to the right:
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)           ①^                   Here, the beginning of the line, i.e. the described ex‐
                                                                    pression should be located at the beginning of the line.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)           ②CHANDATA            This literal character stands for itself, i.e. a search is
                                                                    made for a CHANDATA.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)           ③\                   Escape character; the "open round bracket" should
                                                                    stand for itself as literal and not as meta character of a
                                                                    group.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)           ④(                   This character stands for itself.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)           ⑤\d                  Corresponds to any decimal number.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)           ⑥+                   Requires one match or as many matches as specified,
                                                                    i.e. there must be at least one decimal number.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)           ⑦\                   Escape character; the "close round bracket" should
                                                                    stand for itself as literal and not as meta character of a
                                                                    group.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)           ⑧)                   This character stands for itself.

7.1.3           Industrial security

                   Note
                   Industrial security
                   Siemens provides products and solutions with industrial security functions that support the
                   secure operation of plants, systems, machines and networks.
                   In order to protect plants, systems, machines and networks against cyber threats, it is
                   necessary to implement – and continuously maintain – a holistic, state-of-the-art industrial
                   security concept. Products and solutions from Siemens constitute one element of such a
                   concept.
                   Customers are responsible for preventing unauthorized access to their plants, systems,
                   machines and networks. Such systems, machines and components should only be connected
                   to an enterprise network or the Internet if and to the extent such a connection is necessary and
                   only when appropriate security measures (e.g. using firewalls and/or network segmentation)
                   are in place.
                   For additional information on industrial security measures that can be implemented, please
                   visit:
                   Industrial security (https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity)
                   Siemens’ products and solutions undergo continuous development to make them more secure.
                   Siemens strongly recommends that product updates are applied as soon as they become
                   available, and that only the latest product versions are used. Use of product versions that are
                   no longer supported, and failure to apply the latest updates may increase customer’s exposure
                   to cyber threats.
                   To stay informed about product updates, subscribe to the Siemens Industrial Security RSS
                   Feed at:
                   Industrial security (https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity)


                   Further information is provided on the Internet:
                   Industrial Security Configuration Manual (https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/ww/en/

                   Interactions/restrictions for Create MyConfig with CNC



                   Note
                   CMC 4.8 HF3 - Do not write SINAMICS parameters / indices when using certain CNC versions
                   Do not write any SINAMICS parameters or indices that SINAMICS does not know in
                   manipulation tasks.
                   The following CNC software versions are affected:
                   ● CNC-SW 2.7 SP1
                   ● CNC-SW 4.4 SP1




                    NOTICE
                    CMC 4.8 HF3 - SINAMICS user-specified topology faulty with certain CNC versions
                    The SINAMICS user-specified topology is executed incorrectly in the majority of topologies
                    with certain versions and therefore cannot be used.
                    The following CNC software versions are affected:
                    ● CNC-SW 2.7 SP1
                    ● CNC-SW 4.4 SP1




                   Note
                   CMC 4.8 HF3 - Plugging in ALM and TM
                   Plug in the corresponding components for the Active Line Module (ALM) and Terminal Module
                   (TM) before using the "Determine DO type from hardware" function for ALM and TM.




                   Note
                   CMC 4.8 HF3 - When using the user-specified topology note the following:
                   If you are using a user-specified topology, NX modules and CU320-2 must be present.
                   You must not deactivate NX modules and CU320-2 in Topo and during the package execution.
                   Retrofitting is not possible.

                      Note
                      CMC 4.8 HF3 - Drive commissioning with user-specified topology
                      The drive commissioning with user-specified topology is only possible:
                      ● When the actual topology is a proper subset of the user-specified topology; components
                        may be deactivated.
                      ● No additional or different components must be present.




                      Note
                      CMC 4.8 HF3 / CNC SW 4.4 SP1 - Drive commissioning with user-specified topology
                      For drive commissioning with user-specified topology, the following differences occur in CNC
                      SW 4.4 SP1 in comparison to the automatic device configuration by SINAMICS:
                      ● The parameters p115 and p112 and are not set correctly.
                      ● The parameters p7602, p7604, p7606, p7621, p7623, p7625, p7641, p7643, p7645
                         (back-up Ydb), and p7882 are set differently than in the automatic device configuration.
                      ● The parameter p8801 is not written by the user-specified topology. In practical terms, this
                         has no effect.




                      NOTICE
                      CMC 4.8 HF3 - Access level or password of the NC are reset
                      If functions which reset the access level or the password of the NC are running in the PLC user
                      program on the NCU, proceed as follows.
                      ● Switch the PLC via the "S4=2" hardware switch statically to "Stop".
                      This restriction does not apply to packages with a new installation!
                      This constraint does not apply as of the following CNC software versions:
                      ● 2.7 SP2 HF2 and higher
                      ● 4.4 SP2 HF2 and higher

7.2               Introduction

                      Note
                      Documentation setup: Operating Manual / Online Help
                      The contents of Section Expert are identical in the Operating Manual and the online help.


                      Expert is the engineering software for creating a CMC project.
                      An executable package for the production or upgrading of machines is generated from the CMC
                      project with the Deployment function.
                      The package contains a configurable sequence of production or upgrading steps and the
                      associated data.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                        167
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.2 Introduction


                     In Expert, you specify the configuration of the package, the dialog for operator interactions and
                     the individual upgrade steps in the form of a hierarchical step tree. You specify the required
                     data or data to be manipulated and files.

                     Project folder
                     You can configure the majority of the settings easily via the "Project folder" directly in the
                     "Package", "Dialogs" and "Steps" tabs via a context-sensitive context menu.
                     A Verification run (Page 181) informs you if there are any errors in the configuration.

                     Source explorer
                     The source explorer (Page 182), similar to the Windows Explorer, is integrated for the
                     integration of files in the components. Files can be either copied or linked. Linked files are only
                     accepted in the package at the time of deployment.

                     Script Editor
                     Expert provides the "Create MyConfig Script Editor (Page 345)", which effectively supports you
                     when creating scripts.
                     You can also start the"Script Editor" as an individual application via the Windows Start menu,
                     if you want to edit "*.upscr" or "*.uplib" script files independent of Expert.

                     Resource Editor
                     Further, "Create MyConfig Resource Editor (Page 436)" is integrated in Expert, which
                     effectively supports you when creating language resources for configuring user interface
                     languages of the various packages.
                     If you want to edit "*.ts" language resource files independent of Expert, you can also start the
                     "Resource Editor" via the Windows Start menu as an individual application.

                     Executable package
                     The "Deployment" function creates a package that can be executed under Linux or Windows
                     depending on the configuration.

                     Documentation
                     An integrated online help (F1), which is identical to this documentation, supports you in the
                     correct configuration.

                     Note
                     Qualified personnel
                     The configuration can only be performed by qualified personnel.

                      NOTICE
                      Data can no longer be found
                      If projects, components, and associated data is moved more than once without storage in a
                      buffer, automatic path adaptation may no longer be possible. Components or linked data can
                      then no longer be found.
                      You should therefore always perform a verification run after packages or components are
                      moved.
                      When projects and components are copied with unfavorable supplementary conditions for
                      automation path adaptation, the project may access the original components or linked data.




7.2.4              Verification run
                      The "Verification run" is integrated in Expert and shows the errors in the configuration.

                      Note
                      The verification run does not completely identify syntax errors.
                      Expressions with replacement operator cannot be verified for the correct syntax.

                      Note
                      Axis-drive assignment
                      An axis-drive assignment is not verified for completeness, i.e. the topology can be deployed
                      even without any assignment.




Activating the verification run
                      You can start the verification run of a project either via the main menu "Project > Verification
                      run" or directly in the toolbar via  "Verify project".


SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                               181
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.2 Introduction


                     Normally, the "Verification run" is displayed together with the "Source explorer" and "Cross
                     references" tabs in the lower window area of Expert. If you want to move this area like a
                     dockbable window, read Section "Overview of Expert user interface (Page 168)".




7.2.5              Source explorer
                     "Source explorer" is integrated in Expert, which you can use similar to the Windows Explorer.
                     For the "Source explorer", only read operations are listed in order to avoid unintentionally
                     deleting, shifting or changing data.
                     An external file manager can also be used to copy files and folders to the components - or to
                     link these.


Copy
                     You can drag folders and files from the "Source explorer" and drop these into a component.
                     Copying is performed by pressing the <Ctrl> key. Linking is performed when the <Ctrl+Shift>
                     keys are pressed. Otherwise you are prompted as to what should be done.
                     Copy and paste "Copy & Paste" can also be applied.


Refresh
                     The <F5> key refreshes the display of the "Source explorer"


Double-click
                     You can minimize the "Source explorer" by double-clicking on the title bar. You can maximize
                     the "Source explorer" by double-clicking again.
                     When a linked file is double-clicked, the "Source explorer" changes to its particular path.




7.2.6              Converting projects from existing CMC versions

                     When opening a project or a component, Expert checks the existing CMC version. If the CMC
                     version of the project to be opened is earlier than the installed CMC version, Expert converts
                     the project and the internally and externally linked components.
                     If a project was created with an incompatible version, you cannot open the project. The "*.upz"
                     project versions as well as the package version and status of Expert, e.g. Preliminary, are
                     specified.
                     The conversion is only started after a confirmation prompt, which the user must confirm.
                     The confirmation prompt also specifies the CMC version that was used to create the project to
                     be opened and allows the creation of bak files before the conversion.
                     The "*.bak" backup files can be deleted subsequently via the "Tools" > "Convert" > "Delete
                     backup files (*.bak)" main menu.

182                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                           Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                      7.2 Introduction


                      We recommend that each project be manually backed up or archived with all of the associated
                      internal and external components before the conversion.
                      We also recommend that a conversion is performed only from the previous to the current CMC
                      version. Do not skip any CMC versions.


7.2.6.1           Conversion
                      Projects that were created with the versions SCI version 2.6, CMC version 4.4/4.5/4.6 or
                      CMC version 4.7 are automatically converted when called.
                      Packages that were created with these versions cannot be converted during a direct import.
                      Note the procedure when converting packages from existing Expert versions.


Procedure
                      1. Import the packages with the appropriate existing Expert version.
                      2. Open and convert the created project with the current CMC Expert.
                      3. Save the project and forward the package with the current version as "*.exe", "*.uaz" or
                         "*.usz".


7.2.6.2           Changes to system variables

                      Note
                      Changes to system variables
                      For Create MyConfig, as of version 4.7 SP2, there have been changes to the system variables
                      for the "NCU/PPU initial state" and "System configuration" dialogs.
                      Take note of the following section.




New NCU/PPU initial state dialog
                      The "Data backup of CF card" function has been removed from the "NCU/PPU access" dialog
                      page and moved to the new "NCU/PPU initial state" dialog page. As a result, after execution of
                      the "NCU/PPU access" dialog page, based on the determined software release, a decision can
                      be made per script as to whether it is necessary to execute the "NCU/PPU initial state" (Backup)
                      dialog page.
                      The involved system variables have changed, although they are still accepted in configuration
                      files. In scripts, an error message is issued in the verification run and an adjustment must be
                      made.

                      Up.$Dialog.NcuAccess.Backup                  →    Up.$Dialog.NcuOrigin.Backup
                      Up.$Dialog.NcuAccess.Archive                 →    Up.$Dialog.NcuOrigin.Archive

7.3 System support


System configuration dialog
                  The "Use data" property in the "System configuration" dialog has been removed.
                  Thus, the "Use data" configuration in the "System configuration" dialog for the NC, PLC and
                  DRV control areas is no longer possible.

                  The following system variables have been dropped:
                  ● Up.$Dialog.SystemConfig.NcProcess
                  ● Up.$Dialog.SystemConfig.PlcProcess
                  ● Up.$Dialog.SystemConfig.DrvProcess
                  The affected system variables are ignored in configuration files. In scripts, an error message is
                  issued in the verification run and an adjustment must be made.




7.3            System support


7.3.1          Differences during commissioning between SINUMERIK 840D sl and
               SINUMERIK 828D


Overview

                  Differences during configuration
                  The following table shows the essential differences during configuration of packages between
                  SINUMERIK 840D sl and SINUMERIK 828D:

                                                          SINUMERIK 840D sl                 SINUMERIK 828D
                      Replace PLC blocks                         Yes                         Only data blocks


                      Set HW Config                              Yes,                           Restricted,
                                                            via SDB archive          via special HW Config data class
                                                                                                  archive)1
                  1
                        In the CMC installation folder at Sample\Install_828D_Systemsoftware\, there is a template
                        for a HW Config archive for 828D systems.



HW Config in the case of SINUMERIK 828D
                  Depending on the system, one of the greatest differences between the two control system
                  series is the hardware configuration. While the hardware for 840D sl systems can be configured
                  in great detail via system data blocks (SDB), in the case of 828D systems possible hardware
                  configurations are pre-configured and can be set via NC machine data.
                  For package execution under Shield, you must specify the HW Config for both systems equally
                  on the "System configuration (Page 241)" dialog page.

184                                                                        Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                          Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                7.3 System support


                      The template in the CMC installation folder "828D-SDB-Template.ard" contains the necessary
                      machine data. This template can be used as follows:
                      ● MD11240 $MN_PROFIBUS_SDB_NUMBER[n]
                      ● MD11241 $MN_PROFIBUS_SDB_SELECT
                      Set the machine data according to the control documentation. You can then use the newly
                      created Archiv "*.ARD" as an offline archive in the "System configuration (Page 241)" dialog.




7.3.2             Support CU320
                      A description is subsequently provided as to how the CU320 is supported by Create MyConfig
                      when configuring packages and when executing packages.


Support of the CU320 through Create MyConfig

                      The following processes are supported:
                      ● Administration of the drive data (DO) via the archive (copy, delete).
                      ● Manipulation and access to SINAMICS parameters as for CU Integrated (bus 3) via the
                        archive (script, manipulation task).
                      ● System configuration for the drives as for CU Integrated.
                      ● Comparison, user-specified and extended user-specified topology as for CU Integrated.
                      ● Configuration of the axis-drive assignment as for CU Integrated, execution during runtime.
                      ● Exclusion of slaves above a selectable address of device configuration.
                      ● External CUs can be excluded from the SINAMICS device configuration and the access to
                        data by the HMI/CMC (archiving, manipulation and display).
                        You can find further information at:
                        "Prepare (Page 415)" function and SINUMERIK DOConCD.


                      Note
                      Take the following requirements into account:
                      ● Make sure that the CU system software and the NCU system software have the same
                         version.
                      ● Correctly configured PLC SDBs (HW Config) are required.


                      The following processes are not supported by Create MyConfig:
                      ● FW update and installation of the CU software.
                      ● Adding, changing, deleting files on the CF card.
                      ● Access to the file system of the CU.

7.4             Conversion of projects
                     Projects that were created using previous CMC 4.5, CMC 4.6 and CMC 4.7 versions are
                     converted when they are opened so that the project data can be displayed and edited.
                     Projects that were created using preliminary versions of CMC, cannot be converted. It is only
                     possible to automatically convert projects from older versions before CMC 4.7 SP2 HF1 to a
                     limited extent.
                     Step conditions and manipulation instructions must be adapted or supplemented manually, if
                     necessary.
                     System variables are not converted, and when necessary, must be manually adapted.
                     Further information on this is provided in Section "Conversion (Page 183)".

                     Backup files
                     Backup files that are created during the conversion can be used to restore the initial state prior
                     to the conversion. Backup files which are no longer required can be removed at any time via a
                     menu command.

                      With the    button "Show/hide inactive dialogs", you can show or hide dialogs that are not

Defining general properties for all dialogs
                      You can define generally applicable properties for all dialogs.

                      Name
                      In the table column below "Name", dialog pages with a black checkbox can be activated or
                      deactivated for "Editing" directly in the dialog list or via the "Edit" property in the property field.
                      Dialog pages with a gray checkbox are always required to execute the package, in accordance
                      with the configuration of the areas in the "Package" tab, and cannot be deselected.

                      Editing mode for all dialogs
                      By right-clicking one of the table columns (Name, Mode or Messages) or a dialog page, you can
                      uniformly define the Mode property for all dialogs: "Editing mode for all dialogs".
                      The following options are offered and are activated when the package is executed:

                       Manual                    The dialog page is completely displayed.
                                                 The operator can make changes and must trigger that the dialog page ad‐
                                                 vances or is executed.


                       Automatic                 The dialog page is completely displayed.
                                                 The operator cannot make any changes.
                                                 The dialog page is automatically executed.


                       Progress                  Processing corresponds to the "Automatic" mode without the configuration
                                                 information being displayed.



                      Display messages for all dialogs
                      Also by right-clicking one of the table columns (Name, Mode or Messages) or on a dialog page,
                      you can uniformly define the Messages property for all dialogs: "Display messages for all
                      dialogs".

Meaning of the Events

                      The following table describes what you achieve when using a certain event:

                      Table 7-16     Event - Meaning

                       Event                Meaning / Time of script execution
                       OnInit               The script is executed before the dialog page is displayed.
                                            OnInit is used, for example:
                                            ● To (conditionally) skip this dialog page
                                            ● To issue queries to the operator and process them before the dialog page
                                              opens
                                            ● To change settings of this dialog page via system variables based on the
                                              current execution


                       OnNext               The script is executed in the dialog immediately after clicking "Next".
                                            OnNext is used, for example:
                                            ● To check operator inputs after clicking the "Next" key
                                            ● To return to the input
                                            At this point in time, set values of the dialog page are checked by exporting system
                                            variables.
                                            You can interrupt the dialog execution in the script with the Redo() (Page 408)
                                            procedure. In this case, you can correct settings of the dialog page.
                                            You can restart execution of the dialog page. The "OnNext" script is also executed
                                            again.


                       OnEnd                After processing has been completed, the script is executed at the end of a dialog
                                            page.
                                            Here, using write access to system variables, you can set which of the following
                                            dialogs is to be executed or not.


                      The events are shown schematically in the following graphic "Executing the dialog pages -
                      schematic overview".


Executing scripts in the dialog pages
                      The execution of the dialog pages and any dialog scripts (in the yellow box) is shown
                      schematically in the following diagram.
                      The procedures that can potentially control the sequence of the dialog or script are listed as
                      example.
                      In the dialog script, you can in principle use any of the elements of the script language.
                      Further information is contained in Section Script language (Page 345), but also observe the
                      constraints listed in Section "Data accesses" (Page 358).
                      The context menu supports you when generating your script.

                      if Up.$Dialog.NcuSetup.Mode == Up.$Dialog.NcuSetup.Modes.NONE

                     if (up.$Env.NCU=="SIEMENS SINUMERIK 840D sl NCU730.3 PN"||

                      Up.$Dialog.SystemConfig.SdbFile = "7203ohneCUklass.arc"
                      return()

                     Up.$Dialog.SystemConfig.DrvSources.ORIGIN

                      Verification before the start of execution of the "Step tree" dialog page whether step "6" was
                      activated with the ID "_gp4x".

                      If Up.$Step[_gpx].Activated==false
                        warning("In this version, step 6 must be activated.")
                        redo()

Example: Query with response selection by the operator in dialogs or steps
                      up.leavewhile=false
                      while (up.leavewhile==false)
                        up.quest=inputchoice("Select the resolution","1024*768;640*480;continue
                        without input")
                        if up.quest=="1024*768"
                          up.quest=1024
                        endif
                        if up.quest=="640*480"
                          up.quest=640
                        endif
                        if up.quest=="continue without input"
                          msg("A resolution must be entered!")
                        else
                          up.leavewhile = true
                        endif
                      endwhile



7.5.2.4           Installation and configuration of SINAMICS TEC
                      Create MyConfig supports the installation of SINAMICS TEC on the "CNC software" dialog
                      page at "CNC software (*.tgz)" > "List of additional software"
                      SINAMICS TEC is activated or deactivated using supplied functions in a manipulation task.

                      SinamicsTecActivate("tec_name", Up.doVar)
                      SinamicsTecDeActivate("tec_name", Up.doVar)

                                                            automatic actuation of the standard button.

                                                            script are always displayed.
                                            All

Data backup CF card
                      The following settings are available for the "Data backup CF card" property:

                       Perform backup       Yes      You can select a data backup of the NCU/PPU on this dialog page at the
                                            No       start of package execution.
                                                     The content of the CF card, including the current active archive data
                                                     (NC, PLC, DRV) is backed up in a folder named after the CF card ID.
                                                     If a data backup is found next to the package when starting, it can be
                                                     selected in the package selection for restoration.
                                                     When the backup is restored, the backed-up archive data is reloaded
                                                     automatically.
                                                     In addition to the data backup "*.tgz", this folder also contains instruc‐
                                                     tions "*.txt" and a package *.usz for a Linux package or "*.exe" for a
                                                     Windows package, for restoring the data backup.
                                                     A confirmation prompt appears if a backup not belonging to this CF card
                                                     ID is to be restored.
                                                     You can find further information in Section "Package execution
                                                     (Page 485)".


                       Setting disabled     Yes      The settings made during the configuration can only be viewed by the
                                                     operator during execution, but not changed.
                                            No



                      Note
                      For "Setting disabled" property
                      The setting for selecting the data backup can be disabled for the operating procedure.
                      The licenses of the control are also backed up. When restoring a backup, a query appears as
                      to whether the licenses from the backup are to be restored, or the licenses on the control are
                      to be retained.




Archive

                       Back up archive      Yes      A complete archive can also be created for the diagnostics, with a set‐
                                                     ting for all data to be backed up.
                                            No       The complete archive is stored in a folder named based on the CF card
                                                     ID with the name "Backup_<Date>.arc".

CNC software (*.tgz)
                      The following settings are available for the "CNC software (*.tgz)" property:

                       List              tgz files that contain the CNC software are provided by Siemens Support.
                                         You can insert the tgz files in a list as copy or as link.
                                         Linked files are not taken into this list until the package is deployed.


                       Preselection      At "Preselection" you can:
                                         ● Select a file from the list
                                         ● Insert a file
                                         ● Insert a file as link
                                         ● Store an absolute or relative path
                                           Relative paths start with "./" and are relative to the storage location of the package.
                                           Absolute or relative paths (not links) are not cancelled until the package execution
                                           of Shield.
                                         An example of the preselection could be: ./std31a10c_hmi.tgz.



                      Note
                      If you start the package from a service system USB FlashDrive, then generally booting is from
                      the CF card after this dialog.

                      Preferably, this function is used when installing SINAMICS TEC. You can also install any tgz
                      files.
                      For further information on SINAMICS TEC, refer to Section "Installation and configuration of
                      SINAMICS TEC (Page 201)".
                      The following settings are available for the "Additional software (*.tgz)" property:

                       List              To install several tgz files in a sequence, you must save the required "*.tgz" files in this
                                         list.
                                         The tgz files are then automatically installed in the list from the top to the bottom in the
                                         sequence that you defined.
                                         You define the sequence of the tgz files to be installed by selecting a file and and then
                                         navigating to the required position using the buttons or the context menu "Move up"
                                         or "Move down".
                                         You can insert the tgz files in the list as copy or as link.
                                         Linked files are not transferred into this list until the package is actually deployed.

Overview of the "System configuration" dialog
                      The source or output data is provided via the "System configuration" dialog page.
                      This data is then manipulated later on the "SINAMICS topology" and "Step tree" dialog pages.
                      At the end of execution of the "Step tree" dialog page, the changed data is transferred to the
                      control or to the result archive.
                      On the "System configuration" dialog page, you can specify for every archive area (NC, PLC,
                      DRV) whether it should be used.
                      For "Origin of data", select from where the data of the individual areas should be sourced.
                      The "Origin of data" can be blocked individually for each area by the project engineer in order
                      to prevent changes by the operator during the package execution.

Origin of data           Note
                         This selection can be blocked by the project engineer in order to prevent changes by the operator
                         during the package execution.


                         Initial state           If in the package configuration, "Package" > "Data areas" > "Use NCU/PPU" has
                                                 been activated in the tab, the archive data can be loaded directly from the con‐
                                                 trol with the "Initial state" setting.
                                                 Note
                                                 No data is reset when upgrading the CNC software. The archive is used that is
                                                 available in the system after data migration.
                                                 During a re-installation of the CNC software, a blank DRV archive would result.


                         Automatic               The "Automatic configuration" selection runs through the drive unit configuration
                         configuration           during the package execution in the same way as SINUMERIK Operate.
                                                 "Automatic configuration" mode initially restores the SINAMICS factory settings.
                                                 Then, automatic HMI device configuration (including DO sorting, BICO inter‐
                                                 connection, etc.) takes place.
                                                 In this mode, you can work with a "comparison topology (*.ust)", which must be
                                                 inserted in the "SINAMICS topology" dialog page. This means that the auto‐
                                                 matically identified SINAMICS target topology can be compared with a com‐
                                                 parison topology generated offline.
                                                 During "Automatic configuration", SINAMICS determines the target topology
                                                 that specifies all modules connected at this time, including their DRIVE-CLiQ
                                                 wiring.
                                                 In the subsequent package execution, the most recently created online archive
                                                 is always used. It is only possible to change the topology by adding, removing
                                                 or replacing components via SINUMERIK Operate. Or you must perform a con‐
                                                 figuration again.
                                                 Note
                                                 First encoder on the CU or downstream of the HUB
                                                 If during a drive data generation via "Automatic configuration", a first encoder
                                                 (SMI or SMC) is connected downstream of a HUB or to the CU, then a complete
                                                 automatic configuration of the drive by SINAMICS and Shield is not possible.
                                                 Parameter ""P1982"" (Pole position identification on) is set to "1" by SINAMICS
                                                 instead of "0" and cannot be corrected automatically here.
                                                 The user can correct the parameter manually or also in the step tree of a CMC
                                                 package. Set parameter "P1982=0" in the step tree in a component for all drives
                                                 whose first encoder is connected downstream of the HUB or to the CU.


                         User-specified top‐ With the selection "User-specified topology", a user-specified topology (*.utz) is
                         ology               loaded during package execution.
                                                 For drive commissioning, a "user-specified topology" can be loaded that may
                                                 also contain modules that will not be added, wired and activated until later during
                                                 commissioning.
                                                 The necessary data objects are created by SINAMICS, also for the modules that
                                                 are not yet present, so that the user data can already be loaded during package
                                                 execution.
                                                 In the subsequent package execution, the most recently created online archive
                                                 is always used.

                      the topology files.

                       List                      Clicking the      button opens the "DO list" dialog.
                                                 Enter the "DO variable" and its associated data here:
                                                 ● DO type

                                                 ● DO name
                                                 ● Description
                                                 Or you link or import an externally stored file.

                     The following can be defined for a DO variable:

                     Parameter                Description                                             Character
                     DO variable              Unique name within the package (without                 Characters:
                                              specifying Up.)                                         A-z_0-9


                     DO type                  Type depending on the selected category:
                                              Category                Type
                                              Control Unit            Integrated (NCU)
                                                                      SINAMICS
                                                                      Extended (NX)
                                              Line Module             ACTIVE INFEED CONTROL
                                                                      SMART INFEED CONTROL
                                                                      BASIC INFEED CONTROL
                                              Motion Control          SERVO
                                              Terminal Module         TM31
                                              Terminal Board          TB30
                                              Hub Module              DMC20 / DME20
                                              CULINK                  CULINK
                     DO No.                   DO number to be assigned to the drive object.           1-54
                                              NOTE
                                              No number may be assigned for the CU_Link DO type.


                     DO name                  DO name to be assigned to the drive object.             Characters (max.
                                                                                                      24):
                                                                                                      A-z_0-9
                     Description              Additional information for the operator.                -


                     The assignment of the DO number, the DO name and the description is optional.
                     The DO variable list is not used for verifications by Expert during the verification run.
                     The DO variable list from Expert is only used during package execution if the comparison
                     topology or user-specified topology is not used. The DO variable list is therefore only of
                     importance for the purely manual method of operation, where the user on the machine toggles
                     the DO variables to the DOs.
                     By assigning a DO variable, all components are identified that belong to a drive object (e.g. a
                     Motor Module, two Sensor Modules).
                     During package execution, values are assigned to the properties of the DO variables so that,
                     for example, indirect addressing of the DOs for reading and writing parameters can be
                     performed.
                     The DO variable list can be imported or linked as "*.uvdx" or "*.uvd" file. We recommend using
                     the same list in Expert and Topo. The easiest way to implement this is to store the DO variable
                     list externally and then link it in Expert and Topo.
                     Exporting DO variable lists and editing externally stored files of the "*.uvdx" or "*.uvd" type is
                     possible only via Topo.

260                                                                             Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                            Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                     7.5 Project folder


                      Note that as of CMC 4.8, the UVDX (extended DO list) format should preferably be used. For
                      downwards compatibility, DO lists in UVD format can still be used.
                      When UVDX files are used in Expert, only the DO data contained in the file is used. Any
                      included component information is evaluated only by Topo.

                      Note
                      For DO manipulations using a comparison topology, user-specified topology, or DO list
                      When changing the DO number, the assigned PS file is renamed and parameters "p101" and
                      "p978" of the higher-level CU are adapted.
                      The DO name is entered in parameter "p199" of the relevant DO, and the DO variable name in
                      parameter "p9489".
                      BICOs are not adapted automatically. This should be noted particularly for the Line Module.

                      Note
                      Conflicts in the case of identical names
                      Conflicts between DO variables with the same name with regard to type, number or name,
                      result in errors.

                      Note
                      The TM31 Terminal Module is not supported by CNC SW 4.4 SP1 with Create MyConfig.

                                             The lists are also saved in the package during deployment and can be selec‐

                                             At "Preselection" you can:

                                             ● Insert a file

                                               Absolute or relative paths (not links) are not cancelled until the package
                                               execution of Shield.



Archive
                     The settings for the creation of archives before and after execution of the step tree are specified
                     by the project engineer. Settings are not displayed during package execution.
                     You can use the archives for the diagnostics. The archives are not required for the production
                     or the upgrade of a machine.
                     The following settings are available for "Archive":

Create before step tree        Yes           Here, you specify whether an archive with the NC, PLC and DRV areas is to
                               No            be created before the execution of the step tree.
                                             The archive always includes archive areas available at the event instant, in‐
                                             dependent of how the actual use is configured.
                                             The backup is performed for the NC area with the setting that all data is to be
                                             saved.
                                             For setting "Yes", the archive is saved with the name 'StepBegin_<Da‐
                                             tum>.arc'.
                                             The archive is stored in the folder named after the CF card ID which is located
                                             next to the package after the package execution.
                                             If no NCU is involved with the package execution, the archive is stored in the
                                             'CF-NoneNCU' folder.
