7.5.2.37          Archive data transfer (package execution)
                      While this dialog page is being displayed, the manipulated archive data of NC, PLC and DRV
                      is transferred to the control.
                      The "Archive data transfer" is not listed in Expert because the dialog, without having to be
                      configured, is automatically called from the package if the package data is transferred from at
                      least one of the NC, PLCDRV areas to the control.
                      The archive data of folder NC, PLC, DRV have their source corresponding to what has been
                      configured on dialog page "System configuration" - and are possibly manipulated, removed or
                      added by the package.
                      All archive data, which is available at the end of dialog page "Step tree" is transferred to the
                      control.

                      Note
                      System variable for the "Origin of data"
                      It is not permissible that the system variable for "Origin of data" is at "Do not use", as otherwise
                      archive data is not transferred to the control.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                            277
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.5 Project folder


                     Archive data is also not transferred to the control if the corresponding system variable was set
                     to UNUSED when configuring or during package execution.


Example script For switching "Origin of data" to "UNUSED"
                     Using a script, you can change the system variable at the latest in the OnEnd dialog script of the
                     "Step tree" dialog page. This means that you can transfer archive data areas to the control – for
                     instance that were incorporated via a component – even if the original configuration was
                     different.
                     Up.$Dialog.SystemConfig.NcSource =
                     Up.$Dialog.SystemConfig.NcSources.UNUSED

7.5.3             Steps

                      Under the "Steps" tab, you create a hierarchically structured step tree.


Structuring of the steps
                      Using the step tree, you can model the widest range of versions of machines belonging to a
                      series.
                      You can achieve the various machine variants by structuring the steps in several levels - in main
                      steps and substeps. You can activate or deactivate individual steps in the step tree.
                      Properties are defined for each step during configuration. You can configure the control
                      elements for activation of the steps both for the m out of n selection and for the 1 out of n



SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                            285
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.5 Project folder


                     selection. The step activations that you have specified can also be changed by the operator on
                     the machine during the package execution.


Package execution
                     When executing the package, the step tree is executed from top to bottom along the step
                     sequence marked in green. If the checkbox of a step is green, then this step is executed.
                     When executing a step, a possibly existing step script is first checked. If the step script defines
                     that the step is to be processed further, the components linked to the step will be executed in
                     the configured sequence. Execution then proceeds to the next step.
                     When creating the step tree, using the context menu, arrange the sequence of these steps as
                     they should be executed when executing the package.
                     The step name can be freely selected. The numbering has no functional significance and is only
                     used to improve the overall orientation.
                     The step tree is simultaneously used for navigation when processing/editing components.
                     You can copy, cut out and insert steps using the context menu. This covers all the properties
                     of a step and its subordinate steps (conditions, component links, notes, etc.).

                     Note
                     Response of external and internal components for steps
                     The external components allocated to the step are linked and are not copied. The link remains.
                     If steps with internal components are copied between projects, you can select between "Paste"
                     and "Insert as link".
                     If "Paste" is selected, a copy is inserted as internal component in the target project.
                     If "Insert as link" is selected, the component remains in the original project and is linked as an
                     external component.

                     ● Steps

7.5.3.5           Linking steps


Introduction
                      When commissioning machines, sometimes several projects must be managed.
                      To simplify things for the user, partial or entire step trees from different projects can be linked
                      to one another. As a result of this, recurring step sequences from different projects can be
                      decentrally created and maintained, but only centrally managed and executed in one package.
                      Some examples of this are operator panels, tool magazines, PLC components, etc.
                      Thanks to this technique of linking the step trees, the commissioning can be reduced to the
                      execution of only one package. The linking of steps allows considerable time savings.
                      The commissioning engineer sees a complete step tree during project execution. The use of
                      subprojects is no longer visible here.
                      Due to the linking in step trees, the commissioning of modular machines is supported even
                      more efficiently.


Example
                      In the following example, the position of a project as the main or subproject is explained and the
                      possible linking depth is shown.
                      In principle, any executable project can serve as a main project or subproject (an error-free step
                      tree is sufficient in the subproject). A project is designated as a subproject if it serves as a
                      source of the step linking for another project. The main project is thus the project that contains
                      step links from one or more (sub-)projects.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                           295
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.5 Project folder




Green connecting line                          Permissible step logic operations from:
                                               ● Subproject Project 2 to main project Project 1 and
                                               ● Subproject Project 3 to main project Project 2.
Red connecting line                            Impermissible step logic operation:
                                               Step [2] of the subproject Project 2 is already used in main project Project 1
                                               (linking depth = 1).

                      The position of the projects as main project or subproject
                      Project 1 is the main project and can execute only with Project 2 (here subproject).
                      Project 2 is both the main project and the subproject. From the perspective of Project 1, it is the
                      subproject. As the main project, it can execute independently with Project 3 (here subproject).
                      In this example, Project 3 is a subproject, although it can also execute independently as main
                      project.


Rules
                      There is no configurable project property that defines a project as main project or subproject.
                      Only the application of the project specifies whether a main project or a subproject is involved.
                      Any project can thus be used as main project or as subproject.

                      The following rules must be observed when linking steps:
                      ● In a main project (MP), several links from the same or different subprojects (SP) can exist.
                      ● The step trees linked from subprojects must not contain any links to another subproject
                        (linking depth = 1).
                      ● Subprojects are separate projects and can execute separately even when linked to a main
                        project.
                      ● The steps are linked by the configuration. When the project is deployed, the configured links
                        are dissolved and the linked steps of the subproject (SP) are inserted into the main project
                        (MP).
                      ● The linked steps retain their step ID from the subproject, in which a namespace is added in
                        the main project for each link, in order to ensure unambiguous identification.
                        The ID namespace is automatically assigned during configuration. This also prevents an
                        ID namespace from being assigned twice.
                        The ID namespace can be changed by the user.



                                                                                SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
296                                                                              Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                            Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                     7.5 Project folder


                      ● A defined namespace in a main project only applies for precisely one link step (blue) with the
                        steps located below it (gray). Thus, the step ID does not have to be changed in the main
                        project or subproject.
                      ● Identical step IDs in the main project and subproject are also possible and permitted.
                      ● Existing queries of the step ID (Step configuration) do not have to be adapted in the main
                        project and subproject.
                      ● The linked steps can be recognized in the logbook by a step ID with namespace.
                      ● Steps with namespace before the step ID cannot be linked and cannot contain any linked
                        steps as substeps.
                      ● The execution of the dialogs (in the project folder) is performed exclusively in the main
                        project (MP) also for the steps inserted in the "Steps" tab.
                        Only the step tree is linked or taken over from the subproject(s).
                      ● The system variables used in the linked steps of the subproject (SP) always refer to the main
                        project (MP).
                         Note
                         Exceptions are:
                         ● Up.$Step[ID]
                         ● Up.$Dialog.StepSelection.CurrentID (see also System variables for the "Step
                           tree > CurrentID" dialog (Page 460))
                         The system variables can be used for the main project and the subproject.

                      ● The Up script variables are globally applicable in the main project and subproject.
                      ● The same names are permitted for the components in the MP and SP.
                      ● The properties of the step configuration ("Activation", "Activation disabled" and "Collapse")
                        can be alternatively managed in the main project or subproject.
                        Various use cases are thus supported. A subproject can thus be managed independently of
                        the main project if the "subproject" is selected in the main project at "Manage in".
                      ● For the main project, not only must the subproject be reachable, but also its components
                        located at the linked steps.


Namespace


Query steps
                      The queries in the main project, which concern a linked step in the subproject, are only
                      expanded by the specification of the namespace.
                      In the subproject, steps of the main project can be queried by specifying the namespace "."
                      (point).
                      If a subproject runs independently, the namespace specification " " becomes a return value
                      "null". This implementation ensures that a step query always uniquely refers to one and the
                      same step, in this case for "." in the main project. Take this fact into account when programming
                      the system.

                      Alphanumerical characters are permissible for the namespace. Reserved identifiers, such as

                      Do not use any reserved identifiers of the script language, e.g. "true", "false", "Up", "Main",
                      "null", in the namespace.

Properties of linked steps
                     For the step link and all substeps, all step properties are taken into the main project. The step
                     properties are displayed and saved in the project.
                     The step properties shown in gray cannot be changed in the main project. The ID namespace
                     produced by the step link can be changed at any time in the link step marked in blue.
                     Management of the step configuration is set to the subproject when creating a step link. This
                     setting can be changed to the management in the main project.

                     step, the step configuration is always managed in the main project.

Updating the step links
                      The step links can be selectively updated via the context menu or the "Update step tree
                      completely (F5)" button. The update is also performed automatically when opening the project,
                      when starting the verification run, and when starting to generate the cross reference list.
                      If the SP (subproject) or the step in the SP cannot be reached when updating, then a message
                      in the verification run window makes reference to this fact, and the link step is displayed in red.
                      The properties of the linked steps also indicate the last known properties. If the update was
                      possible, then the link step is shown in blue - if there were no differences between the linked
                      steps in the MP (main project) and those in the SP.

                      Response when managing in the main project:
                      The linked step is shown in purple if at least one difference has been found, and the step
                      configuration is to be verified. A message and a list of the differences found are displayed in the
                      verification run window to make users aware of this fact.
                      By saving the project, users acknowledge and accept all changes to the linked steps.
                      After saving, the link step is shown in blue again.

                      Response when managing in the main project:
                      All changes in the SP are accepted in the MP. The link step remains blue.

                      When updating the step links, it is identified and displayed as to whether:
                      ● Steps have been added
                      ● Steps have been removed
                      ● Steps have been shifted
                      ● Level type has been changed
                      To update, the saved SP is read accessed, even if this project is open.




7.5.4             Managing and using configurations


7.5.4.1           Overview
                      All settings that you specify in the properties fields of the "Package", "Dialogs" or "Steps" tab in
                      the project folder are configurations.
                      Some of the configurations are represented as system variables so they can also be written or
                      read subsequently via configuration files or scripts, e.g. during or before execution.
                      When the term "configurations" is used within this section, just this subset of configurations for
                      which system variables also exist is meant.
                      In this case, the handling of configurations always means the handling of the associated system
                      variables, including their values.
                      The information as to which system variables are available in the "Package", "Dialogs" and
                      "Steps" tabs can be found on the user interface by clicking the "Display associated system
                      variables" context-dependent button.


SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                            303
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.5 Project folder


                     Further information on the individual system variables can be found in Section "Reference list
                     system variables (Page 447)".
                     The configurations are located in text files with the "*.upcfg" extension. You can edit the text
                     files using the "Script Editor (Page 345)" provided by CMC.
                     The format of the text files corresponds to that of a CMC task or a CMC script. Value
                     assignments are made in the form <System variable> = <Value>.
                     Comments are identified by a prefixed semicolon. You can also remove any number of
                     configurations from the configuration files and, for example, so limit the number being used.
                     When loading/using this configuration, only the settings contained in the project/package are
                     set with all other configurations remaining unaffected. Proceed in this manner when, for
                     example, in an existing package, a switchover is performed only between a new installation and
                     an upgrade for automatic execution.


7.5.4.2         Project configurations
                     Project configurations are configuration files used for the deployment of a project for a package.
                     These configuration files contain configurations of the "Package", "Dialogs" and "Steps" tabs of
                     the project folder for which system variables (Page 447) exist.
                     The project configurations are contained within the project or also externally next to the
                     package in a file.
                     For the deployment of the project via the command line or batch file, these configurations are
                     sent and activated via a command line switch.
                     This has the advantage that you can generate different packages automatically without making
                     changes to the project.
                     Further information can be found in Section "Command line call" > "Package deployment by
                     Expert" (Page 503).


See also
                     Specifying the configuration for Package (Page 186)


7.5.4.3         Package configurations
                     Package configurations are configuration files used for executing a package. These
                     configurations contain some or all configurations of the "Dialogs" and "Steps" tabs of the project
                     folder for which system variables (Page 447) exist.
                     These package configurations are contained within the package on the "Package
                     configuration" dialog page or also externally next to the package in a file.
                     For the execution of the package, one of these configurations is selected and activated on the
                     "Package configuration (Page 202)" dialog page. This has the advantage that one and the
                     same package is executed with different configurations (automatically) without changes to the
                     project/package. For example, a single switchover makes it possible with one package to
                     produce a machine at one time point and to upgrade a machine at another time point.




                                                                             SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
304                                                                           Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                      Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                                7.5 Project folder


7.5.4.4             Step configurations
                         Step configurations are configuration files used for executing a package. These configurations
                         contain some or all configurations of the "Steps" tab of the project folder for which system
                         variables (Page 447) exist.
                         These package configurations are contained within the package on the "Step tree" (Page 272)
                         dialog page or also externally next to the package in a file.
                         For the execution of the package, one of these configurations is selected and activated on the
                         "Step tree (Page 275)" dialog page. This has the advantage that one and the same package is
                         executed with different step configurations (automatically) without changes to the project/
                         package.
                         For example, a single switchover makes it possible with one package to produce a machine at
                         one time point with layout A and a machine with layout B at another time point.

7.6            Create MyConfig Report


7.6.1          Starting the report
                  CMC provides two variants of the "Create MyConfig Report":
                  ● The "Report" is integrated in Expert. You create the report directly in Expert.
                  ● The "Create MyConfig Report" is also available as standalone application. Independently of
                    Expert, you can create and display a Report of an existing "*.upz" CMC project without
                    opening the CMC project with the standalone application.

                  Starting the report in Expert
                  You create a current "Report" via the "Project" > "Report" main menu.
                  You obtain information on the project and the components used in the project.
                  You obtain information on a component selected in the step tree via the
                  "Component" > "Report" main menu.

                  Starting the report from the Windows start menu
                  The "Create MyConfig Report" standalone application is inserted in the Windows start menu
                  when installing CMC.
                  Start the "Create MyConfig Report" directly via the Windows start menu with the "Report 4.8
                  SP1" entry.
                  The standalone tool opens. Select a "*.upz" project via "File" > "Open…".




                  Figure 7-65   Create MyConfig Report: view opened as standalone application

7.6.2             Report information
                      The storage path of the project and the number of pages is displayed in a line at the top directly
                      below the toolbar.
                      The creation date and time of the report are displayed directly below the "Report" title.
                      This is followed by information on the project and the components.

                      The following properties of the project are displayed in the Report:
                      ● Name of the "*.upz" project
                      ● Current version of the project
                      ● User version: Is defined by the user
                      ● Date of change: Last change in the project
                      ● Change user: The user who made the last changes.
                      ● Specification of the language
                      ● Original directory of the project

                      The following properties are displayed for the components:
                      ● Specification of the component name and the properties described in the following.
                      ● Version: CMC version for which the component was created or the last change was made.
                      ● User version: Is defined by the user
                      ● Date of change: Last change in the component
                      ● Change user: The user who made the last changes.
                      ● Original directory: Where the component was first saved.
                      ● Current directory: Current storage location after moving the component.
                      Finally, the information when and from which user this report was created is displayed in the last
                      line of the report.

                       The contents of components, their actions, version and comment can be displayed, edited and

SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                                315

7.7 Component editor


Components and actions
                  In order that a component is executed during package execution, the component must be
                  linked with a step and the step must be selected for execution (green icon). An existing step
                  script can permit or prevent execution of the components.
                  The component contains actions. All the relevant instructions and data are inserted in the
                  respective actions under the relevant tab during configuration.
                  An action script that, among other things, controls the execution of the action, can be stored for
                  every action.


Actions tab
                  The actions to be performed by the component can be created and activated in the "Actions"
                  tab.

                  You can create the following actions:
                  ● Execute (Page 320)
                  ● Delete (Page 325)
                  ● Copy (Page 329)
                  ● Change (Page 332)
                  ● Manipulate (Page 340)

                  Sequence when executing actions
                  During the execution of a component by the package, the activated actions are executed in the
                  order of their listing in the "Actions" tab from top to bottom. An action is activated when the
                  checkbox in front of the action is activated.




                  Figure 7-66   View of the "Actions" tab with display of the individually opened actions

                  You can change the order of the actions in the "Actions" tab as follows:
                  ● Via the toolbar in the "Actions" tab
                  ● Via the Up - "Alt+Up" or Down - "Alt+down" context menu
                  Actions opened for execution are assigned their own tabs in the Component Editor, which are
                  given the name of the action.




                                                                             SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
316                                                                           Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                              Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                   7.7 Component editor


                      You can adapt the order of the Actions tab with drag and drop. However, this has no influence
                      on the order of execution of the actions.
                      For execution, it makes no difference whether an action is open or closed.

                      Note
                      With regard to the order and execution of actions, only the list in the "Actions" tab is relevant.




Editing an action
                      To edit an action, you must first open it by double-clicking or via the context menu. The tab for
                      this action is opened and you can configure the actions to be executed.


Executing / copying actions
                      You can insert files and folders below the "Execute" and "Copy" actions both as a copy and as
                      a link. It is also possible to mix copied and linked objects.


Deleting / editing / manipulating actions
                      In the "Delete", "Edit" and "Manipulate" actions, the appropriate instructions can be used to
                      directly create tasks, to import them from a file or to link them to an external file. In all cases,
                      direct editing of tasks is possible with the "Script Editor" integrated in Expert. The advantage of
                      this is that support is always offered by Expert.


Linking actions
                      All links are only cancelled when the package has been deployed and the data has been
                      accepted in the package. The advantage of the link is that, among other things, the source data
                      can be updated or edited independently of the project before deployment.


Version data/comment
                      A version can be assigned to the component. This version is noted in the logbook during
                      package execution.
                      Information about the component can be stored in the "Comment" field. The text is not
                      displayed during execution and is also not adopted in the logbook.

Creating and editing an action script
                      There are two ways to create and edit an action script in the editor:

7.7.2          Execute


7.7.2.1        Description, execute action


Execute action
                  The "Execute" action allows a program, command or script to be executed. For example, you
                  can install software components from SIEMENS or other suppliers - or perform special
                  manipulations in the archive or other target areas.

                  The following target areas are supported:
                  ● NCU / PPU
                  ● PCU 50
                  ● Linux (runtime system)
                  ● Windows (runtime system)
                  All the files and folders required for "execution" can be inserted as a copy or link at the
                  appropriate target area. When deployed, the links are canceled and the folders and files are
                  accepted in the component.
                  Target areas shown in gray do not contain any data or instructions.

                  Note
                  Selected data areas define target areas
                  Which target areas are displayed depends on the data areas (archive, PCU, NCU / PPU) that
                  were activated for use.
                  The data areas are defined in the project folder in the "Package" tab (Page 186).
                  If a data area is deactivated subsequently, all target area nodes that cannot be hidden due to
                  content are shown red.

                      Note
                      Display of the target area
                      ● Gray - target area does not contain any data.
                      ● Red - data in the target area is not used.
                      ● Blue - linked data with resolution for deployment.
                      ● Purple - linked data with resolution during runtime.


                      You can specify a command or an executable file in the "Execution of:" text field. You can also
                      pass arguments separated by spaces, e.g. file names, switches.
                      Write commands or file names that contain spaces in straight quotation marks.
                      Special operators (Page 367) can be inserted anywhere in the text field.

                      Note
                      The name of the selected file can be transferred to the "Execute" text field using the associated
                      button (↵).




Execute - NCU
                      During execution, all folders and files are unzipped into a temporary folder. This temporary
                      folder is used as work directory when "executing" and is then deleted.

                      Note
                      Temporary folder
                      The temporary folder is not the package storage. This means a "./" used for "Execution of"
                      does not point next to the package, but to the temporary folder.


                      The script outputs are transferred to the logbook. In this case, the error messages (stderr) of the
                      programs called in the script are entered in italics.
                      The return value of the script is evaluated as terminating error code. A return code not equal to
                      "0" results in an error message. The user must decide whether the package should be canceled
                      or continued.
                      Further information can be found in Section: "Notes relating to the execute action (Page 324)"


Execute - PCU 50
                      During execution, all folders and files on the PCU are unzipped to a temporary folder. This
                      folder is used as work directory during execution and is then deleted.

                      Note
                      Temporary folder
                      The temporary folder is not the package storage. This means a "./" used for "Execution of"
                      does not point next to the package, but to the temporary folder.

Execute - runtime system
                      A package can be deployed for various runtime systems.
                      Two scripts must be written to deploy a package for Linux and for Windows that makes special
                      changes via "Execute" in the "Archive" area.
                      Depending on the runtime system, Windows or Linux, the corresponding node is executed
                      automatically and the other skipped during execution.
                      All folders and files are unzipped to a temporary folder; this folder is then used as the work
                      directory and subsequently deleted.

                      Note
                      Temporary folder
                      The temporary folder is not the package storage. This means a "./" used for "Execution of"
                      does not point next to the package, but to the temporary folder.


                      The script outputs are transferred to the logbook. In this case, the error messages (stderr) of the
                      programs called in the script are entered in italics.
                      The return value of the script is evaluated as terminating error code. A return code not equal to
                      "0" results in an error message. The user must decide whether the package should be canceled
                      or continued.

                      Example
                      All files, except for "OEM001.SPF", should be deleted from the CMA.DIR directory of the NC.
                      As there is no special delete instruction for this purpose, a script is generated which saves the
                      file to be obtained, subsequently deletes the folder and then returns the file.
                      The particular script file is copied to the component and entered as a command during
                      execution.

7.7.2.2        "Notes relating to the execute action"

                  Note
                  System variables for the environment
                  Use "System variables for the environment" in a script file for Windows "cmd" or Linux "sh",
                  because only these script files are known to the script interpreter.
                  If, however, "System variables for the environment" are used in "Execution of" the component,
                  for Linux use a "sh" as prefix, and for Windows, a "cmd" as prefix before the command.
                  The "System variables for the environment" can be used in all CMC scripts.
                  Example:
                  If !FileExist(RTS,"%UP_PACK%/WCD/file.txt")
                  As alternative to UP_PACK, the system variable Up.$Pack.Dir can also be used for
                  "Execution of" and in all CMC scripts.
                  Example:
                  md "$(Up.$Pack.Dir)/WCD"If !FileExist(RTS,"$
                  (Up.$Pack.Dir)/WCD/file.txt")
                  System variables for the environment
                  UP_PACK - Location from where the package was started
                  UP_ARC - Temporary storage location of the archive tree with the NC, PLC, CP and DRV
                  subfolders
                  UP_CFID - ID of the CompactFlash card
                  Available only for packages with the "NCU/PPU" data area.
                  UP_SHARE - Folder for exchange release between "PCU" and "NCU/PPU"
                  Available only for Windows packages with the "NCU/PPU" data area.
                  This "System variable for the environment" points to the shared folder in Windows and to the
                  mount point in Linux.
                  UP_PCU_ROOT - Computer name of the "PCU".
                  Available only for packages with the "PCU" data area.
                  UP_ARC_ROOT - Folder of the archives to be processed.
                  Available only for packages that use only the " Archive" data area.

324                                                                     Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                              Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                  7.7 Component editor




                      Note
                      Exit Script
                      If no script-internal error handling is performed, a script should preferably always be exited with
                      exit "0".




                      Note
                      Command interpreter under Windows
                      For Windows, prefix the command line scripts to the command interpreter.
                      For example:
                      Cmd.exe /c test.cmd




                      Note
                      Using shell scripts for Linux
                      When using shell scripts "*.sh" for Linux, always ensure that in the Unix file format you only
                      save LF; and not CR/LF.
                      The shell identifier must be located in the first line, e.g.:
                      #!/bin/sh
                      The script must be started using a shell call, e.g.:
                      sh my_script.sh
                      If you specify commands directly with place holders or environment variables, then use a shell
                      as prefix e.g.:
                      sh rm /user/*.log.
                      If you specify a file for execution, then use "./" as prefix, e.g.:
                      ./test.sh.

                      The following options are available to create tasks:

Script Editor
                      The names of the files and folders to be deleted are specified at "Instructions".
                      The place holders "*" (none or one or several characters) and "?" (any arbitrary character) are
                      permissible in file names.
                      On the other hand, no place holders are permitted in the folder names. Folders are deleted with
                      their complete content.
                      Only one delete operation is permissible for each line.
                      If a line starts with a comment character ";", then the line is not evaluated.

                      Examples:

                      Cycle*.spf           All cycles in the current folder are deleted.
                      *.*                  All files in the current folder are deleted. Subfolders are kept!
                      4711.WPD             Folder 4711.WPD with all of its contents is deleted.
                      0C00022              The FC22 is deleted.

7.7.3.2        Notes regarding the delete action

                  Note
                  Naming conventions for PLC blocks
                  To delete PLC blocks, they must be specified in the archive name convention.
                  The naming convention has the format: TTNNNNN, whereby TT stands for the hexadecimal
                  type, and NNNNN for the decimal number of the block.
                  Note that both specifications have to be completed with leading zeros to 2 or 5 positions.
                  PLC block types:
                  08 - OB - Organization block
                  0A - DB - Data block
                  0B - SDB - System data block
                  0C - FC - Function
                  0E - FB - Function block




                  Note
                  Case sensitivity on the NCU/PPU
                  In contrast to Windows, the file system used on the NCU/PPU differentiates between upper
                  case and lower case letters.




                  Note
                  Define copying for SINUMERIK Operate
                  For the target area "Operate", using known folders, create folder "All", "NCU" or "PCU". These
                  folders define for which SINUMERIK Operate the tasks are to be processed.
                  Below this folder, define the path to the files to be deleted.
                  The tasks saved under "All" are executed on the NCU/PPU and on the PCU. The tasks stored
                  in the other two folders are only processed on the associated system.

                                    and files up to package execution.
                                    At the target, the data is not imported and used directly by the package until package
                                    execution.

                    the objects are transferred to the component.

                      Change action in the "Preprocessor script" mode
                      In the "Preprocessor script" mode, contents can be incorporated script-controlled in files.

                      the package automatically creates the file in the target system.
                      Preprocessor instructions always begin with "#". Only these lines are evaluated as script by
                      the CMC package. Lines that do not begin with this character are imported into the file to be
                      created without checking.

                      The following preprocessor instructions are valid:

                      #Pragma Eol CRLF                        Defines the "end of line indicator" for the file as
                                                              ""CRLF"".
                      #Pragma Eol LF                          Defines the "end of line indicator" for the file as ""LF"".
                      #Rem                                    Marks a line as comment.
                      #If, #ELIF, #ELSE                       For controlled creation.
                      und #ENDIF                              Instead of #ELIF, you can also use #ELSIF.
                      ##                                      For inserting lines that begin with #.
                                                              For creating preprocessor scripts by a preprocessor
                                                              script.

                      Special operators (Page 367) can be inserted anywhere in a line to insert the contents of Up
                      variables for "Change".

                      Note
                      If folders, files, sections or identifiers are not available, then the package itself generates these
                      to implement a value assignment.




Operators

                       =        Assignment of a new value


                       ~        Delete date: Identifier and value are removed


                       ?=       Assigning a (new) value if no value is available




                      Example:

                      For the target area "Operate", using "known folders", create folder "All", "NCU" or "PCU".

                      affect one another.

7.7.6.1        Description of the manipulate action


Manipulate action
                  The "Manipulate" action allows machine data to be accessed, to the largest extent
                  independently of data storage in the control.
                  The data to be manipulated can be stored in the archive, e.g. NC data, drive data, as well as in
                  the HMI (display data).

                  Note
                  Selected data areas define target areas
                  Which target areas are displayed depends on the data areas (archive, PCU, NCU/PPU) that
                  were activated for use.
                  The data areas are defined in the project folder in the "Package tab (Page 186)".
                  If a data area is deactivated subsequently, all the target area nodes that cannot be hidden due
                  to content are shown in red.

                  Note
                  Display of the target area
                  ● Gray - target area does not contain any data.
                  ● Red - data in the target area is not used.
                  ● Blue - linked data with resolution for deployment.
                  ● Purple - linked data with resolution during runtime.


                  Data manipulation operations are supported in the following "target areas":
                  ●      NC data
                  ●      SINAMICS data
                  ●      Display data
                  ●      All
                  Any number of tasks can be created in the target area below the Manipulation tasks node. A
                  new task can be created, imported or linked via the context menu. The user assigns the task
                  name. You can change the target area at "Settings" > "Target area".

7.7.6.2        Notes regarding the Manipulate action


NC data
                  NC data is manipulated on the basis of the NC archive area.
                  If a context is not set with CHANDATA(n), channel 1 is assumed.

                  NOTICE
                  Multi-channel assignments
                  For multi-channel assignments, ensure that CHANDATA(1) is prefixed to data that is not
                  channel-dependent!


                  Manipulating NC data
                  If NC data is to be manipulated, in relation or depending on its old value (e.g.: For operators +=,
                  *=, etc.), ensure that this data is also included in the NC output data.

                  Provision of NC machine data
                  In the case of "Origin of data", "Initial state" or "Overall reset", all NC data is always provided.
                  For this purpose, the package sets the required machine data to the following values before it
                  provides all machine data:
                  N11210 $MN_UPLOAD_MD_CHANGES_ONLY='H0' ; machine data backup only for changed
                  machine data.
                  N11212 $MN_UPLOAD_CHANGES_ONLY=0 ; data backup type of the active file system.
                  These two machine data items retain these values over the package execution and afterwards.
                  If this is not wanted, you can set this machine data to the desired value in a manipulation task.

                  Loading an archive into the control
                  When loading an archive to organize the memory, the NC requires certain machine data
                  contained in the upload files prefixed to INITIAL.INI (NC.OPT, GLOBAL.IN, SCALING.INI
                  and CHAN.INI). Before manipulation, the package loads only data from INITIAL.INI to
                  memory, performs the manipulation operations and then writes back all the data. All previously
                  existing data is written back to its old position, both in the INITIAL.INI and in the upload files.
                  Additional data is attached to the data of INITIAL.INI, and according to the following rule,
                  also to the data of the upload files:
                  ● NC.OPT, if the identifier starts with $ON
                  ● GLOBAL.INI, if the identifier starts with $MN or $MA
                  ● SCALING.INI, if the identifier starts with $MN or $MA
                  ● CHAN.INI, if the identifier starts with $MN or $MC
                  If NC data is manipulated, the line checksum is generated and attached to all data.

                                                                                            Create MyConfig - Expert

SINAMICS data
                      Drive data is manipulated, based on the DRV archive area.


Display data
                      For SINUMERIK Operate, data is read from section [BTSS-Settings] of file hmi_md.ini in
                      the search sequence siemens → addon → oem → user, but written back only
                      to hmi_md.ini at user. When deleting data, this results in a reset to a user-specified value
                      of preceding files in the search sequence.


Comparing tasks in Diff
                      Manipulation tasks can also be used in Diff for comparison.
                      To this end, export the task to a file and open it in the SINUMERIK archive comparison of Diff.
                      All assignments in the form of "identifier = value" are then displayed in the data structure tree
                      of Diff and can be used for a comparison, etc.

7.8.5            Package variables

                    Package variables are variables that have significance only within a package. The control does
                    not recognize package variables. Therefore, package variables are not transferred to the
                    control.
                    The package variables comprise an identifier, preceded by the "Up." prefix.

7.8.6           Functions and procedures
                  In all scripts, you can use functions and procedures provided by Create MyConfig (CMC) – or
                  your own functions and procedures that you have defined in script libraries.
                  A new naming scheme has been implemented to clearly show the functional relationship of the
                  growing number of functions and procedures. The "Insert script" context menu has been
                  revised. The previously used names for the functions and procedures are still known within the
                  system as aliases, but will be omitted in future.


Comparison of functions and procedures
                  Functions and procedures are subprograms, which execute a defined code that has been
                  saved, using specific parameters. The parameters are transferred in the form of arguments.
                  The difference between functions and procedures is that procedures do not supply a direct
                  return value.
                  Functions supply one direct return value, e.g. a value that the operator had entered.

                  You can only use functions at the following locations:
                  ● Within comparisons
                  ● As argument of other functions or procedures
                  ● To the right of a "="

                  Special issue relating to procedures:
                  Procedures must be located alone in one line.

                  You can use the following as arguments for functions and procedures:
                  ● Constant value
                  ● Variable
                  ● Up variables
                  ● System variables
                  ● Local or global area data (control data from the archive)
                  ● Functions
                  Excluded are only those arguments that contain an ID parameter. An ID parameter is a string
                  without exclamation marks, e.g. RTS, ARC, NCU, PCU for argument <area> of function
                  FileExist().


Call examples


                  $MC_CHAN_NAME=InputText(Up.Label,$MC_CHAN_NAME) ;function with
                  variable arguments in the assignment
                  If Input("number of tools") < 600 ; function in condition

354                                                                         Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                            Create MyConfig - Expert

                      Up.small_magazine = Input("number of tools") < 600 ; function in
                      condition

                      MSG("do not forget magazine selection!"); procedure with constant
                      argument
                      TraceToFile(Up.file,Up.String); procedure with Up variable as
                      argument
                      FileWrite(RTS,"MyText.txt","line 1"<<'\r'<<'\n'<<"line

Notes regarding functions and procedures
                      Observe the subsequent notes:

                      Note
                      Double inverted commas
                      If user interface text contains a function in double inverted commas ", change the double
                      inverted commas into single inverted commas ' " ', so that these are not interpreted by the
                      CMC.
                      Example:
                      Msg("Component ' " ' HMI Install ' " ' ...")
                      This procedure must be used for all double inverted commas within strings, as is typically also
                      the case in the NC.

                      Note
                      Incorrect formatting
                      If an error occurs when formatting texts, e.g. because you did not close a "tag" or wrote it
                      incorrectly, this can lead to the entire formatting of the logbook being altered or corrupted
                      starting at this error location.

                      Note
                      Line breaks and text formatting
                      Line breaks can also be inserted in the user interface texts via '<br>'. Texts can be formatted.
                      You can find further information in Section "Text formatting options (Page 401)".

7.8.7          Commenting


Commenting - ; Comment
                  Comments are identified by a semicolon as prefix. As a consequence, all of the characters up
                  to the end of the line are no longer evaluated.
                  In order to comment out several lines simultaneously, select the corresponding lines and use
                  Ctrl+K+C.
                  To undo commenting out, use Ctrl+K+U.

                  Example
                              ; Comment across complete line
                              N20000 $MC_CHAN_NAME="Machine"                  ; Comment in line




7.8.8          Sections
                  Within the target areas (NC data, SINAMICS data, display data), the structured data is
                  addressed via specifying a section. Set sections act local to a script until another section is set
                  or the script (task) ends.
                  For details, see section Data accesses (Page 358).


Set section - [B?_S?_PS?], [SL], [C?], CHANDATA(?)
                  For data with the same name, which occur in various areas, before assigning a value, a
                  specifying section must be specified. This section is effective as long as no other section is
                  specified. Data accesses between areas are unaffected by this.

7.8.9          Area data


Area data - $MN_?, ... , $MD_?, p?, $MM_?, ...
                  All variables/identifiers without the package prefix Up. are interpreted as area data. This
                  includes, for example, machine data, setting data, option data, tool data, drive data, display
                  data, and user data.
                  The area data can be written on the left side of an assignment and be read on the right side of
                  an assignment.
                  In the task/script editor, area data can be inserted via the context menu "Insert script → Area
                  data...". Furthermore, the area data can be inserted via the Windows clipboard from Diff.

                  Note
                  You can get the options for the cross-area reading and writing of area data from section Data
                  accesses (Page 358).

7.8.11            Check structures

                      Script Editor
                      In the "Script Editor", the "Insert script" context menu provides support when creating a control
                      structure.

                      Control structures used in CMC
                      The following variants of the control structures are available:
                      ● If control structure (Page 361)
                      ● If-Else control structure (Page 361)
                      ● If-ElsIf control structure (Page 362)
                      ● If-ElseIf-Else control structure (Page 362)
                      ● While control structure (Page 363)
                      Display und use only in the preprocessor script:
                      ● #Pragma Eol control structure (Page 364)
                      ● #Rem control structure (Page 364)


7.8.11.1          If control structure / If-Else control structure


Conditional execution - If ... Else ... EndIf
                                    If exp
                                         block1
                                    Else
                                         block2
                                    EndIf

                      The control structure allows the conditional execution of two different instruction blocks
                      depending on whether the "exp" condition is fulfilled or not. If it is fulfilled (true), then the first
                      operation block "block1" is executed, else the second execution "block2" is executed.
                      Each of the two instruction blocks can, in turn, contain control structures; this means that any
                      nesting depth is possible.

                      Example
                                    CHANDATA(1)
                                    If Up.Velo_X != null
                                      If Up.Velo_X > ($MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1]+ 100)
                                        $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1] = Up.Velo_X
                                      Else
                                        $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1] = 1000
                                      EndIf
                                    EndIf




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                               361
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.8 Script language


7.8.11.2       If-ElsIf control structure / If-ElsIf-Else control structure
                  After the If condition alternative conditions can be checked by specifying ElsIf or ElIf.
                  The instruction block is executed after the first fulfilled condition. The instruction block after Else
                  is executed if no condition is fulfilled.

                  Conditional execution - If ... ElsIf... Else... EndIf

                               If exp
                                 block_1
                               ElsIf exp_2
                                 block_2
                               ElsIf exp_3
                                 block_3
                               …
                               Else
                                 block_E
                               EndIf


                  Note
                  For the alternative conditions, the keywords "ElsIf" and "ElIf" are used as equivalents.


                  The control structure allows the conditional execution of different instruction blocks depending
                  on whether the "exp" condition is fulfilled or not.
                  If this is fulfilled (true), then the first instruction block "block_1" is executed, otherwise it is
                  checked whether the second alternative condition "exp_2" is fulfilled or not.
                  If this is fulfilled (true), then the second instruction block "block_2" is executed, otherwise it is
                  checked whether the next alternative condition "exp_3" is fulfilled or not.
                  If this is fulfilled (true), then the third instruction block "block_3" is executed, and so on.
                  Once a condition or alternative condition is fulfilled, the associated instruction block is executed
                  and then the execution continues after the associated keyword "EndIf".
                  As long as the condition or alternative condition is not fulfilled, the subsequent alternative
                  condition is checked.
                  If no alternative condition is fulfilled, the instruction block "block_E" in the alternative branch
                  is executed after the keyword "Else".
                  If no alternative branch "Else" was specified, then processing is continued after the keyword
                  "EndIf" without executing an instruction block.




                                                                             SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
362                                                                           Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                             Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                   7.8 Script language


                      Each instruction block can, in turn, contain control structures; this means that any nesting depth
                      is possible.

                      Example 1
                                    CHANDATA(1)
                                    If Up.Velo_X != null
                                      If Up.Velo_X > $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1]
                                        $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1] = Up.Velo_X
                                      Else
                                        $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1] = 1000
                                      EndIf
                                    EndIf



                      Example 2 - Alternative condition
                                    IF (up.selection == 1)
                                     Log("selection 1")
                                    ELSIF (up.selection == 2)
                                     Log("selection 2")
                                    ELIF (up.selection == 3)
                                     Log("selection 3")
                                    ELSE
                                     Log("selection was not 1, 2 or 3")
                                    ENDIF



7.8.11.3          While check structure


Repeated execution - While ... EndWhile
                                    While exp
                                        block
                                    EndWhile

                      The control structure allows the repeated execution of the operation block "block" as long as the
                      "exp" condition is fulfilled.
                      The operation block can, in turn, contain control structures; this means that any nesting depth
                      is possible.

                      Example
                                    [B3_S3_PS99]
                                    Up.i = 0
                                    Up.CU_Hat_Servo = false
                                    While Up.i < 6 && !Up.CU_Hat_Servo
                                      If p978[$(Up.i)] != 255
                                        Up.CU_Hat_Servo = true
                                      EndIf
                                      Up.i += 1
                                    EndWhile

7.8.12         Operators


7.8.12.1       Overview operators
                  The following operator groups are available for scripts in dialogs, step scripts, and manipulation
                  tasks:
                  ● Assignment operators (Page 364)
                  ● Arithmetic operators (Page 365)
                  ● Logic operators (Page 366)
                  ● Comparison operators (Page 366)
                  ● Special operators (Page 367)


7.8.12.2       Assignment operators


Assignment operators - VAR = 123
                  The assignment operators constitute the core function of manipulation tasks, because they
                  write the control data. All assignment operators can also be applied to script variables.

                  Table 7-34    The following assignment operators are available:

                      ?=   Assign if blank or not available
                           Assign the specified value if no value is available.
                           No assignment is made if a value is already available.
                      =    Assign
                           Assignment of a new value.
                           The assignment is always executed. If the data item or variable is not yet available, it is created.
                           If it already exists, its value is changed.
                           (An assignment of "null" leads to the deletion of the variables or to the reset of the value to the
                           default, see deletion operator ~.)




                                                                                SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
364                                                                              Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                    Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                           7.8 Script language


                       ∼        Delete
                                The data and the value are removed.
                                For data relating to the control (NC/drive/display data) this generally means resetting the value
                                to the default of the control (of the software release).
                       +=       Add
                                Addition of the specified value to the existing value.
                       -=       Subtract
                                Subtraction of the specified value from the existing value
                       *=       Multiply
                                Multiplication of the specified value and the existing value.
                       /=       Divide
                                Division of the existing value by the specified value.
                       |=       OR operation
                                OR operation on the specified and existing value (set bits).
                       &=       AND operation
                                AND operation on the specified and existing value (reset bits).
                       :=       Assignment without evaluation
                                Assignment without evaluation to the right of the operator. The value is transferred to the
                                control as specified.
                                Everything to the right of "=" (e.g. a variable) is neither interpreted by the package nor pro‐
                                cessed.

                      If, for compiled operators: += -= *= /= &= |= no old value exists, an error message
                      results.

                      Examples
                                    N20000 $MC_CHAN_NAME="TUTORIAL"
                                    $ON_AXIS_FUNCTION_MASK~
                                    $MA_AX_VELO_LIMIT[0,AX1]?=2300
                                    R[0]+=10
                                    $MN_MM_TOOL_MANAGEMENT_MASK|='B10000'
                                    GUD_2=$MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1]
                                    Up.myVar ~ ; Delete variable
                                    Up.myVar = null ; Delete variable (alternative)

7.8.12.5          Special operators


Replacement operator - $(up.?)
                      The "replacement operator" makes it is possible to replace parts of an instruction, an identifier,
                      a value or a message text flexibly with the value of a package variable Up.identifier.

                      Note the following rules when applying the "replacement operator":
                      ● Use only with package variables.
                        Further information can be found in the Package variables (Page 350) section.
                      ● During replacement, straight quotation marks are removed from string values.
                      ● "Replacement operators" can be nested.

                      Examples for applying the "replacement operator"
                      ● In sections
                        [$(up.doX.pspath)] or [B3_S$(Up.slave)_PS$(Up.doNr)]
                      ● In identifiers
                        $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX$(UP.AXNr)]=1000
                      ● In parameter indices
                        If p107[$(Up.i)] == 254
                      ● In comparison operations
                        Version(PCU, "SINUMERIK Operate")>=$(Up.HMI)

Create MyConfig - Expert

                  ● In functions and procedures
                    MSG("Maschinennummer: $(Up.Masch_Nr)")
                  ● In command lines for "Execution of:"
                    Setup.exe > Log_$(Up.Masch_Nr).txt


                  Note

                  Note

7.8.12.6       String concatenation (Concatenate-Operator)
                  The string concatenation operator "<<" can be used to combine constant strings and variables
                  to form a resulting string.
                  This operator is mainly intended for the assignment of Up variables when used in functions or
                  procedures with string parameters.
                  The string concatenation operator can also be directly used in functions and procedures.
                  Exceptions include Prepare and Patch; in this case, the string concatenation operator cannot
                  be used.

                  Example
                  Up.real = 12.34
                  Up.text = "units"


                  Up.para = "Value of Up.real: " << Up.real << " " << Up.text
                  Log(Up.para)

7.8.13.1       StringLen


StringLen("<string>")
                  The StringLen() function determines the length of a <string> character string and returns
                  it as a decimal number.




                                                                        SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
368                                                                      Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                       7.8 Script language


                      In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                      manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.

                      Note
                      Counting characters
                      All characters of a character string are counted, the printable and also the non-printable.
                      '\r' and '\n' each count as one character and are counted.

7.8.13.2          StringMatch


StringMatch("<string>", "<search>")
                      The StringMatch() function searches in the <string> character string for the <search>
                      search pattern.
                      In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                      manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                      Regular expressions are used as search pattern. The return value of the function is a character
                      string.

                      Note
                      Compatibility
                      The function name has been changed from Match() to StringMatch().
                      For compatibility reasons, the Match() function name is still tolerated in this CMC
                      version. Match() will no longer be supported in subsequent CMC versions.
                      Only use the StringMatch() function. Change all earlier calls to this new function name.

                      Note
                      Using metacharacters as character literals
                      Take special care when using metacharacters as character literals in a regular expression.
                      You can find further information on regular expressions at Create MyConfig - Diff, Section "Use
                      of regular expressions in Diff (Page 156)".




Example
                      Up.NCU = StringMatch("NCU720.3 PN", "NCU([0-9]+)")                           ;Up.NCU "720"
                      Up.NCU = StringMatch(Up.$Env.NCU, "NCU([0-9.]+)")                           ;Up.NCU "720.3"

Create MyConfig - Expert
