7.8.13.3       StringPos


StringPos("<string>", "<search>", <pos>)
                  The StringPos() function searches in the <string> character string for the <search>
                  character string, starting at the <pos> position.
                  In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                  manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                  The <search> character string to be sought is specified via a regular expression. The case-
                  sensitivity in the <search> argument is not relevant and is not observed.
                  The function returns the position of the first occurrence of <search> as decimal number. If the
                  <search> character string was not found, a -1 is returned.
                  When assessing the returned positions, note that the first character in the <string> is on the 0
                  position. Spaces in the <string> are also characters, non-printable characters.

                  Note
                  Using metacharacters as character literals
                  Take special care when using metacharacters as character literals in a regular expression.
                  You can find further information on regular expressions at Create MyConfig - Diff, in Section
                  "Using regular expressions in Diff (Page 156)".




Example

                  Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "e", 0)                               ;Up.Pos = 3
                  Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "E", 5)                               ;Up.Pos = 17
                  Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "e", 25)                              ;Up.Pos = -1
                  Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "x", 0)                               ;Up.Pos = -1
                  Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "for", 0)                             ;Up.Pos = 10
                  Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "[efg]", 0)                           ;Up.Pos = 2


7.8.13.4       StringReplace


StringReplace("<string>", "<search>", "<replace>")
                  The StringReplace() function searches in the <string> character string for
                  the <search> character string and replaces it with the <replace> character string.
                  In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                  manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                  The return value of the function is a character string with the replaced characters.
                  The <search> character string to be sought is specified via a regular expression.




                                                                            SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
370                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                       7.8 Script language


                      The case-sensitivity in the <search> argument is relevant and is observed. Replacement is
                      made only when identical. If nothing to be replaced is found, the function returns the <string>
                      argument unchanged.
                      Multiple occurrences of the sought <search> characters are all replaced.

                      Note
                      Compatibility
                      The function name has been changed from Replace() to StringReplace().
                      For compatibility reasons, the Replace() function name is still tolerated in this CMC
                      version. Replace() will no longer be supported in subsequent CMC versions.
                      Only use the StringReplace() function. Change all earlier calls to this new function name.




                      Note
                      Using metacharacters as character literals
                      Take special care when using metacharacters as character literals in a regular expression.
                      You can find further information on regular expressions at Create MyConfig - Diff, Section "Use
                      of regular expressions in Diff (Page 156)".




Example
                      Use the name of the input archive for the name of the package execution logbook.

                       Up.$Dialog.PackageEnd.LogName =
                       StringReplace(Up.$Dialog.ArcSelection.ArchiveIn, ".arc","")
                      The use of an ""NC.ARC"" input archive by this instruction produces the "NC.htm" logbook.
                      As the file extension is replaced with an empty string and the package automatically adds the
                      "*.htm" extension when the logbook is saved.


7.8.13.5          StringSubStr


StringSubStr("<string>", <pos>, <len>)
                      The StringSubStr() function returns a subcharacter string from the <string> character
                      string, which starts at the <pos> position and has the length <len>.
                      In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                      manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                      The <pos> and <len> arguments are of the decimal number type.
                      Note that the first character in the <string> is on the 0 position. Spaces in the <string> are
                      also characters, non-printable characters.
                      If the subcharacter string was not found, a "" empty string is returned.


SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                             371
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.8 Script language


Example


                  Up.Str=StringSubStr("Ingenuity for life", 0, 9)                            ; Up.Str =
                                                                                             "Ingenuity"
                  Up.Str=StringSubStr("Ingenuity for life", 10, 3)                           ; Up.Str = "for"
                  Up.Str=StringSubStr("Ingenuity for life", 30, 9)                           ; Up.Str = ""
                  Up.Str=StringSubStr("Ingenuity for life", 0, 0)                            ; Up.Str = ""

                  If Up.Str == ""
                    MSG("No subcharacter strings found!")
                  EndIf




7.8.14         File operations

                  The functions and procedures that you can use for files are described in the following sections.

                  In the subsequent sections, the following values are uniformly permissible for argument
                  <area>:
                  ● RTS
                    For the runtime system (NCU, PCU, PC/PG), on which the package is executed.
                    You can specify the path, either in relative terms, starting next to the package - or in absolute
                    terms.
                    Environmental variables can be used.
                  ● ARC
                    For the archive folder, i.e. the image of the SINUMERIK archive.
                    You specify the path, either in relative terms, starting with NC, PLC, CP - or DRV.
                  ● NCU
                    For the NCU/PPU file system.
                    You specify the path in absolute terms, starting with "/" - and taking into account uppercase/
                    lowercase (case sensitive).
                  ● PCU
                    For the PCU file system.
                    You specify the path in absolute terms, starting with the drive letter, e.g. "D:\" or "D$\".


                  Note
                  Activating data areas
                  Note that only areas are reached that you have activated in the project folder in the "Package"
                  tab in the "Data areas" group.

7.8.14.1          FileCopy


FileCopy(<area>, "<sourcepath>", <area>, "<destinationpath>")
                      The FileCopy() procedure copies a file from a source to a target across areas.
                      In principle, this procedure can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                      manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                      The areas for the source and target are specified via the <area> argument.
                      The permissible values for the <area> argument are provided in Section "File operations
                      (Page 372)".
                      The <sourcepath> argument specifies the source path of the file to be copied. The
                      <destinationpath> argument specifies the target path of the file.
                      The paths always contain the storage location and the file name. If the file to be copied already
                      exists in the target, it will be overwritten without a prompt.
                      If the package runs on the NCU, copying to the PCU via <area> PCU is not possible.


Example 1

                      FileCopy(RTS, ".\Test.txt", NCU, "/user/Test_NCU.txt")


Example 2
                      Version files of the NCU are stored in the CF card folder next to the package.

                      Up.cf = "./CF-" << Up.$Env.CFID << "/"
                      FileCopy(NCU, "/user/system/etc/hwversions.xml", RTS, "$
                      (Up.cf)hwversions.xml")
                      FileCopy(NCU, "/siemens/versions.xml", RTS, "$
                      (Up.cf)siemens_versions.xml")

                      The <path> argument specifies the path of the file to be deleted and the file name.

7.8.14.3        FileExist


FileExist(<area>, "<path>")
                   The FileExist() function checks whether a folder or a file exists.
                   In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                   manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                   If the folder or the file with the absolute path <path> exists in the area <area>, the
                   FileExist() function returns the value "true".
                   Absolute and relative paths are permitted for the <path> argument. Relative paths refer to the
                   package location.
                   The use of environment system variables and package variables is possible and permitted.
                   The permissible values for argument <area> are provided in Section "File operations
                   (Page 372)".



                   Note
                   Observe case sensitivity
                   Observe case sensitivity in the path on the NCU/PPU at Linux.
                   Note that only data areas can be addressed that have also been activated in the project folder
                   when configuring the package.

                   Note
                   Compatibility
                   The function name has been changed from Exists() to FileExist().
                   For compatibility reasons, the Exists() function name is still tolerated in this CMC
                   version. Exists() will no longer be supported in subsequent CMC versions.
                   Only use the FileExist() function. Change all earlier calls to this new function name.




Call examples
                   FileExist(NCU, "/siemens/versions.xml") ;searches for the file on the NCU.
                   FileExist(NCU, "/install/arc") ;searches for the folder on the CF card of the NCU.
                   FileExist(PCU, "C:\Users") ;searches for the folder in drive C of the PCU.

                  used in the file.

                      MSG("It is a Linux (UNIX) file.")
                  ElsIf StringPos(Up.File, "\r", 0) != -1
                      MSG("It is a Mac file.")
                  Else
                      MSG("The content of the file comprises only one.") line
                  EndIf

                  Observe case sensitivity
                  Observe case sensitivity in the path on the NCU/PPU under Linux.

7.8.14.5          FileWrite


FileWrite(<area>, "<path>",“<string>“)
                      The FileWrite() procedure writes the character string <string> to a text file <path> in
                      the <area> area.
                      In principle, this procedure can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                      manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                      The procedure always creates a new file.
                      Using the <path> argument you specify the file with path and name in which the character
                      string is to be written.
                      You can specify the path <path> either relative to the package - or in absolute terms.
                      The use of environment variables is possible. Observe the case sensitivity under Linux.
                      The <string> character string may include characters of the UTF-8 character set or non-
                      printable characters.
                      The permissible values for the <area> argument are provided in Section "File operations
                      (Page 372)".

                      Examples
                      FileWrite(NCU, "/user/myfile.xml", Up.myfile).
                      FileWrite(PCU, "C:\Users\ myfile.txt", Up.myfile)
                      FileWrite(ARC, "NC\CST.DIR\Test.SPF", Up.myfile)
                      FileWrite(RTS,"MyText.txt", Up.myfile) ;creates the file next to the package.
                      FileWrite(RTS,"%UP_PACK%/MyText.txt", Up.myfile) ;path specification with
                      environment system variables under Windows; creates the file next to the package.
                      FileWrite(RTS,"$UP_PACK/MyText.txt", Up.myfile) ;path specification with
                      environment system variables under Linux; creates the file next to the package.
                      FileWrite(RTS,"$(Up.Pfad)/MyText.txt", Up.myfile) ;path specification via
                      script variable.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                              377
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.8 Script language


                  FileWrite(RTS,"$(Up.$Pack.Dir)/MyText.txt", Up.myfile) ;path specification
                  via system variable.

                  Note
                  Use of the end of line / line break
                  If your character string has several lines, you can implement it with the string chaining operator.
                  You can find further information in Section "String chaining (concate operator) (Page 368)".
                  Example
                  FileWrite(RTS,"MyText.txt","Zeile 1"<<'\r'<<'\n'<<"Zeile
                  2"<<'\r'<<'\n')
                  \r → Carriage return (CR or 0x0D)
                  \n → Line feed (LF or 0x0A)

                  Note
                  Attaching characters to an existing file
                  If you attach characters to an existing file, you can implement this in two ways:
                  1. Use the TraceToFile() procedure. This procedure has the advantage that it always has
                      high performance.
                      Only use TraceToFile() for the runtime system (RTS). First copy the file to the runtime
                      system, attach the file and then copy back the file.
                      This procedure can be used when you write several times to the file and only copy the file
                      back after all the write operations.
                      You can find further information in Section "TraceToFile (Page 387)".
                      Example
                      ;If the package is executed on the PG/PC
                      FileCopy(PCU, "D:\LastUpdate.txt", RTS, "LastUpdate.txt")
                      TraceToFile("LastUpdate.txt", "Step 4711 successful")
                      ...
                      FileCopy(RTS, "LastUpdate.txt", PCU, "D:\LastUpdate.txt")
                  2. Read the contents of a file with the FileRead() procedure.
                      Add your characters with the string concatenation operator (Concate-Operator) "<<" and
                      write the STRING back to the file with FileWrite().
                      Example
                      FileWrite(RTS, "RW.txt",FileRead(RTS,"RW.txt")<<'\r'<<'\n'<< "my
                      attached line")




7.8.14.6       QueryIni


QueryIni("<path>", "<section/id>")
                  The QueryIni() function reads values from INI files.
                  In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                  manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.




                                                                            SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
378                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                   Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                          7.8 Script language


                      You can use this function for all files whose structure corresponds to the format of an INI file and
                      are located on the runtime system (RTS) of the package execution.

                      These files have the following structure:
                      [Section]
                      Identifier = value
                      Using the <path> argument, you specify the file (with path and file name) from where a value
                      is read.
                      You can specify the file path fully qualified in accordance with the runtime system - or also
                      relative to the package.
                      Using <section/id>, you specify the section and the identifier for the value to be read.
                      <section/id> is not case sensitive. Exception: <path> on the NCU (Linux) is case sensitive.
                      The return value of the function is the value of the specified identifier in the section of the file.
                      The function returns "null" if the specified file, the section or the identifier is not found. Or, if there
                      is no equal character and no value at the identifier.
                      If there is an equals sign, but no value at the queried identifier, the function returns an empty
                      string "".

                      Note
                      FileCopy() function
                      If files are read that are not located on the runtime system of the package execution, using
                      the FileCopy() function you can temporarily copy these to the runtime system, from where
                      they can be read out.


                      You can use the environment system variables of the runtime system.
                      By testing the return value for "null", you can determine whether or not the function could find
                      the file, the section or the identifier.


Example 1
                      Query the "FirewallOpenPorts" identifier in the "LinuxBase" section in
                      the "basesys.ini" file.

                      Content of "basesys.ini"

                      [LinuxBase]
                      FirewallOpenPorts="TCP/5900 TCP/102 TCP/22"

                      Function call in Expert

                      Up.FOP = QueryIni("/user/system/etc/basesys.ini","LinuxBase/
                      FirewallOpenPorts")
                      MSG("The FirewallOpenPorts are :$(Up.FOP)")




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                                   379
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.8 Script language


                  Function return value
                  Up.FOP contains the function return value: e.g. "TCP/5900 TCP/102 TCP/22".


Example 2
                  The softkeys are checked for their existence and access level in "logdrive.ini".

                  Up.file = "/user/sinumerik/hmi/cfg/logdrive.ini"
                  If !FileExist(RTS,Up.file)
                   Warning("No 'logdrive.ini' file exists!")
                  Else
                   up.i=1
                   While up.i<25
                    If QueryIni(Up.file,"DEVICE_$(up.i)/AccessLevel") == null
                     Log("The $(up.i) softkey is not used.")
                    Else
                     up.AL=QueryIni(Up.file,"DEVICE_$(up.i)/AccessLevel")
                     If up.AL != "7"
                      Warning("The $(up.i) softkey has the AccessLevel $(up.AL)")
                     Else
                      Log("The access level of softkey $(up.i) is $(up.AL).")
                     EndIf
                    EndIf
                    up.i+=1
                   EndWhile
                  EndIf


7.8.14.7       QueryXml


QueryXml("<path>", "<xpath>")
                  The QueryXml() function reads the contents of XML files that are on the runtime system
                  ((RTS)) of the package execution.
                  In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                  manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                  The <path> argument specifies the XML file with path and file names (file path) from where the
                  content of an XML node should be read. Whereby, the file path can be specified fully qualified,
                  in accordance with the runtime system, or also relative to the package.
                  For Linux (NCU) the case sensitivity of the path is relevant, however, not for Windows (PC,
                  PCU).
                  The XPath expression in the <xpath> argument selects the XML node whose content should
                  be output.
                  The case sensitivity for <xpath> is always relevant.


                                                                            SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
380                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                               Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                     7.8 Script language


                      If the selected XML node was found by <xpath>, its content is returned as STRING. All other
                      XML nodes are ignored.
                      If the XML file or the specified node is not found, then the function returns "null".

                      Note
                      XML node
                      An XML node can be, for example, an element, an attribute or text.

                      Note
                      XML node <xpath> return
                      If several XML nodes selected by <xpath> are found, only the content of the first XML node
                      is returned.

                      Note
                      Reading files outside the runtime system
                      If files are read that are not located on the runtime system of the package execution, they can
                      be copied temporarily with the FileCopy() function to the runtime system, and then read.

                      Note
                      Use of environment variables
                      Environment variables of the runtime system can be used in the <path> argument.

                      Note
                      Return value "null"
                      By checking the return value for "null", it can be determined whether the function could not find
                      the file or the XML node.

                      Note
                      Warning in the logbook if the file is not an XML file
                      If the specified file is not an XML file, the function behaves as if the specified path is invalid.
                      The function provides the return value "null" and writes the message of the invalid path as
                      warning in the logbook.




Command line example
                      Up.valCustomerId = QueryXml( "/user/sinumerik/hmi/data/version/
                      identity.xml", "/Config_Identity/Addresses/Manufacturer/ Customer-
                      Id/text()")

                  Up.alarmTextIndex = 1

                      ;Determine the maximum number of alarm texts
                      Up.alarmTextMax = QueryXml(Up.pathToInput,"count(/TS/message/

7.8.14.8          TraceToFile


TraceToFile("<path>", "<string>")
                      The TraceToFile() procedure adds a <string> character string to a <path> file.
                      In principle, this procedure can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                      manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.



SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                              387
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.8 Script language


                  If the file does not exist, it is created by the procedure. If the file already exists, the text is added
                  at the end of the file.
                  The <path> argument specifies the file with path and name.
                  The path specification <path> can be relative to the package or absolute, but always refers to
                  the runtime system of the package execution.
                  The use of environment variables is possible. Observe the case sensitivity under Linux.
                  The text including a line feed to be written to the file via the <string> argument is added at
                  the end of the file.
                  ● \r\n = CRLF = 0D0A under Windows
                  ● \n = LF = 0A under Linux
                  The text may include characters of the UTF-8 character set.

                  Note
                  Possible uses
                  The TraceToFile() procedure only works in the runtime system (RTS) of the package
                  execution and therefore has a high performance. You can use the procedure, for example, to
                  write information from the package execution in an uncomplicated way to a file.




Example 1 of TraceToFile
                  TraceToFile("D:\Text.txt", "This is only the first test.")


Example 2 of TraceToFile
                  The channel name and the name of the first geometry axis are written to an Excel table.

                  Up.file = "Test.csv"
                  Up.i = 1
                  If FileExist(RTS, Up.file)
                   FileDelete(RTS, Up.file) ; New CSV should be created
                  EndIf
                  TraceToFile(Up.file, "Channel name; 1st geometry axis") ; header line
                  While Up.i < NC[C1].$ON_NUM_CHANNELS
                   TraceToFile(Up.file, "" << NC[C$(Up.i)].$MC_CHAN_NAME << ";" << NC[C
                   $(Up.i)].$MC_AXCONF_GEOAX_ NAME_TAB[0]); The first two "" generate
                   an empty string
                   Up.i += 1
                  EndWhile

7.8.15            Dialogs

                      You can call the functions and procedures subsequently listed in this section as dialogs on the
                      user interface of the packet execution and in CMC scripts in Diff.
                      The dialogs provide operators with information - or ask information from operators.

                      Note
                      Straight quotation marks
                      If user interface texts or string values in a function or procedure contain straight quotation
                      marks " ", the straight quotation marks must be enclosed within single quotation marks '
                      " '. In order that they are not interpreted by Create MyConfig, as is also usual in the NC.
                      Examples:
                      Msg("Component ' " ' HMI Install ' " ' ...")
                      TraceToFile(Up.File,"Up.Text= ' " ' my text '" ' ")

                      Note
                      Erroneous formatting
                      If an error occurs when formatting texts, e.g. because you did not close a "tag" or wrote it
                      incorrectly, this can lead to the entire formatting of the logbook being altered or corrupted
                      starting at this error location.

                      Note
                      Line breaks and text formatting
                      Line breaks can also be inserted in the user interface texts via '<br>'.
                      You can format texts. You can find further information in Section "Text formatting options
                      (Page 401)".

                      Note
                      Message preview
                      Call the "Message preview" dialog in the "Script Editor".
                      ● Via the "Message preview" context menu entry or alternatively
                      ● Via Ctrl + click on a line.
                         In this dialog, check the programmed message with regard to the formatting.
                      The dialog is closed again via the "Close" button.

                      Note
                      Handling special characters in strings
                      The straight quotation mark " is enclosed by inverted commas '"' within a string, but only counts
                      as one character.
                      You can only individually insert special characters for line feed '\n' and carriage return '\r' in
                      character strings using a string chaining operator <<. These characters also only count as one
                      character.

7.8.15.4          Introduction input functions

                      Two types of Input functions are available:
                      ● Input functions that are not linked to a particular type
                      ● Input functions that are linked to a particular type

                      Input functions linked to a particular type return a typical value, contrary to input functions that
                      are not linked to a particular type:
                      ● "string"
                      ● "integer"
                      ● "real"
                      ● Enumerator value as "string"
                      ● "unsigned integer"
                      The type-specific input functions require a default value. The user-specified value can be
                      specified directly or applied only at runtime via variables.
                      All of the input functions are always displayed in the Dialogs tab in the "Step tree" dialog,
                      independently of the "Display messages" selection.

                      Default value
                      The arguments of the type-specific input functions must include a default value so that fully
                      automatic package execution is possible without requiring any operator action. This
                      preassignment value can be changed for manual package execution.

Input("<label>")
                   The Input() function is a non-type-specific function.
                   In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                   manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                   You can query a value during the script execution with the Input() function.
                   Whereby, the entered value determines the type. This means that only those values that match
                   a permitted type can be entered, e.g. 1; 5,8; 0x0; "Test", true, etc.
                   If you do not enter any values, the function returns "null". This can be caught in the script
                   code.
                   You can explain the entry via the <label> argument.

7.8.15.6        InputChoice


InputChoice("<label>", "<button1>;<button2>")
                   In the package execution, the InputChoice() function displays a dialog with icons.
                   In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                   manipulation tasks and CMC scripts in Diff.
                   In the dialog, you can make a direct selection by pressing individual buttons.
                   The selection that is made is returned as a character string (the button labeling).
                   The entry is explained using the <label> argument. An icon can be optionally selected at the
                   beginning of the <label> argument, separated by a semicolon, which is displayed in the
                   dialog during package execution.




                                                                             SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
392                                                                           Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                             Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                    7.8 Script language


                      You can select between the following icons <label>:
                      ●     Selection without icon
                      ● *I; selection with "information" icon
                      ● *Q; selection with "question mark" icon
                      ● *W; selection with "warning" icon
                      ● *E; selection with "error" icon
                      The <button> argument can be used to specify the identifiers for several buttons, separated
                      by semicolons.
                      Two successive semicolons result in a line feed, i.e. all of the subsequently listed buttons are
                      displayed in a new line. In this way, buttons can also be arranged one below the another.
                      The freely selectable identifiers simultaneously define the possible return values of the function.

                      Control characters in the <button> argument:
                      ● * Accept / input
                      ● ^Reject / cancel with ESC
                      ● & Alt-Shortcut
                      The control characters '*‘ and '^‘ can be used to specify the default button for confirming or for
                      cancelling with ESC at the beginning of an identifier.
                      The control character '&' in the identifier for buttons defines the subsequent letters as "Alt-
                      shortcut" (key combination Alt+<letter>).
                      During package execution, each button can then also be operated via the keyboard, using the
                      uniquely assigned key combination. Ensure an unambiguous letter assignment across all
                      buttons.
                      The Alt-shortcuts are not case-sensitive.


Example Selection without icon

                      Up.ret = InputChoice ("Beispiel ohne Symbol", "*&OK")




                      Figure 7-89    Example without icon

                      "*&OK")

7.8 Script language


7.8.17         Miscellaneous


7.8.17.1       Skip


Skip()
                  The Skip() procedure can be used in dialog scripts, step scripts and action scripts to skip the
                  dialog, the step or the action.
                  Using Skip() in a CMC script in Diff means that the script is terminated; it acts like Return().
                  Use for non-deselectable dialogs and in manipulation tasks is not permissible.
                  You can find further information in Section "Dependencies of the dialog pages of data areas
                  (Page 195)".
                  The method of operation of the Skip() procedure is described in Sections "Dialog scripts
                  (Page 196)", "Step scripts (Page 291)" and "Action scripts (Page 317)".

                  Note
                  Exception
                  The Archive, NCU/PPU and PCU access and System configuration dialog pages are not
                  skipped if "Yes" is set in the Package tab at Package > Data areas > Use archive.
                  In this case, an error message is output during package execution or during the verification run
                  in Expert.




7.8.17.2       Redo


Redo()
                  The Redo() procedure is used in dialog scripts for "OnNext" and "OnEnd" to repeat the inputs
                  in the dialog or the complete dialog processing.
                  Using OnInit in dialog scripts, in step scripts, in action scripts in manipulation tasks or in CMC
                  scripts in Diff is not permissible.
                  The method of operation of this procedure is described in Section "Dialog scripts" > "Executing
                  scripts in dialog pages (Page 198)".
                  The Redo() procedure should preferably be used in the dialogs in the "OnNext"event for
                  monitoring manual entries.


7.8.17.3       Return


Return()
                  The Return() procedure can be used in all scripts to terminate the current script execution.
                  Its use in manipulation tasks terminates the execution of this manipulation task.

7.8.17.4          ExtCall


ExtCall("<path>")
                      The ExtCall() procedure calls an external manipulation task.
                      In principle, this procedure can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,

                      For this task, no verification run is performed in Expert and as a consequence, the syntax is not

                      The "CMC scripts in Diff (Page 88)" are edited with the "Create MyConfig Script Editor

                      encoding (without BOM) when saving the file. Use UTF-8 encoding as soon as you use
                      accented characters and special characters outside the ASCII 7-bit character set in the code
                      characters.




7.8.17.5          DateTime


DateTime("<dt>")
                      The DateTime() function allows the determination and use of the current date and the current
                      time.
                      In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                      manipulation tasks and "CMC scripts in Diff (Page 88)".


SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                              409
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.8 Script language


                  The <dt> argument informs the function about the format in which the date and time is
                  provided. Examples are provided below.
                  When calling the function without an argument, i.e. with an empty string " " for <dt>, the date
                  and time are formatted according to ISO 8601 "yyyy-MM-ddThh:mm:ss".
                  Also observe uppercase/lowercase within the <dt> argument.


Example
                  To generate a unique name for the logbook, proceed as follows, for example:
                  Up.dt = DateTime("yyyy-MM-dd.hh-mm-ss")
                  Up.$Dialog.PackageEnd.LogName = "$(Up.$Pack.DeployName)_$(Up.dt)"
                  The file extension "htm" or "exe" is automatically generated by the package, depending on the
                  configured password protection.

                  Note
                  You can also assign other files (archive...) with specifically generated names in this fashion.




Examples of units of time
                  Up.year = DateTime("yyyy") ; the year as four digit number
                  Up.month = DateTime("MM") ; the month as number with a leading zero
                  (01-12)
                  Up.day = DateTime("dd") ; the day as number with a leading zero (01
                  to 31)
                  Up.hour = DateTime("hh") ; the hour with a leading zero (00 to 23)
                  Up.minute = DateTime("mm") ; the minute with a leading zero (00 to 59)
                  Up.second = DateTime("ss") ; the second with a leading zero (00 to 59)
                  Up.milliseconds = DateTime("zzz") ; the milliseconds with leading
                  zeroes (000 to 999)
                  Up.dt = DateTime("yyyy-MM-dd hh:mm:ss.zzz") ; previous examples in
                  combination

7.8.17.9       MathRound


MathRound(<value>, <precision>)
                  You round-off values when calling the MathRound() function.
                  In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts,
                  manipulation tasks and "CMC scripts in Diff (Page 88)".
                  The <value> argument designates the identifier, e.g. Up variable, machine data, NC data,
                  drive data, display data, whose value is to be rounded.
                  Specify the number of places to be rounded to via the <precision> argument. The rounded
                  value is assigned to the specified variable. All identifiers, which have values that can be of the
                  corresponding result format of the function are permitted as variables, e.g. Up variables,
                  machine data, NC data, drive data, display data.


Example

                  Round(<value>, <precision>)

                               Up.pVerst = round(p1460[0], 2) -> 0.62

7.8.17.10         Version


Version(<area>, "<app>")
                      You determine the version of an installed application using function Version().
                      In principle, this function can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts and
                      manipulation tasks, but not in CMC scripts in Diff.
                      The <area> argument specifies from which control area the version is determined. Possible
                      values for <area> are NCU or PCU.
                      Note that only those versions which have also been activated in the project folder when the
                      package was configured, can be queried in the areas.
                      For package area PCU, all SIEMENS applications installed on the PCU, which have been
                      entered in the PCU registry with key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Siemens\AUTSW,
                      are determined.
                      For package area NCU/PPU, the versions are determined from the /siemens/
                      versions.xml file.
                      The <app> argument specifies the application whose version is queried. If the version of the
                      specified application <app> cannot be determined, the function returns the value "null". In
                      this way, it is possible to react when a version cannot be found.
                      For the name of the application <app>, an abbreviated, unambiguous specification is sufficient,
                      e.g. "SINUMERIK CNC" instead of "SINUMERIK CNC-SW 31-5".

                      Note
                      All applications that are found are displayed on the "Version Display" dialog page.




Example of a query for whether a higher or lower version exists

                      Query, as to whether the version of the NCK is lower than or equal to 83.03:
                      Version(NCU, "NCK") <= 83.03

                      Version of SINUMERIK Operate higher than or equal to 4.7 and cycles are installed:
                      Version(PCU, "SINUMERIK Operate") >= 4.7 && Version(NCU, "Cycles") !
                      = null


SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                                413

                  Version of SINUMERIK Operate higher than or equal to 4.7 and ShopMill is installed:
                  Version(PCU, "SINUMERIK Operate") >= 04.07 && Version(PCU,
                  "ShopMill") != null

                  For example, the queries can be used in control structures (If, While).




7.8.18         Preprocessor


7.8.18.1       #include


#include "<path>"
                  The "#include" instruction is a deployment directive.
                  In principle, this directive can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts and
                  manipulation tasks, but not in CMC scripts in Diff.
                  The preprocessor instruction accepts an external file, e.g. script or manipulation task for the
                  check and/or deployment.
                  ● When a package is deployed, the contents of the external file are taken over in the
                    manipulation task instead of the #include statement.
                  ● The files to be included are also checked by the verification run.
                  ● You can specify the file path of the external file <path> to be included either in absolute or
                    relative terms.
                    <path> contains the storage location and the file name, e.g.
                    D:\Temp\Skript.txt or .\Skript.txt..
                    For internal manipulation tasks, the relative path refers to the storage folder of the
                    component.
                    For external manipulation tasks, the relative path refers to the storage folder of the external
                    task.
                    In the step and dialog scripts, the relative path refers to the folder where the package is
                    saved.
                    The path can contain Windows environment variables, e.g. %SUB_PATH%.
                  ● Ctrl + click on the line or use of the "Open external task" context menu entry opens the file
                    in the "Create MyConfig Script Editor".

                      Special functions and special procedures are elements of the CMC script language that are
                      only used in very special cases when a problem cannot be resolved in the usual way.


7.8.19.1          Prepare


Prepare("<data>", "<value>")
                      The Prepare() procedure allows the pre-assignment of defined machine data, which is set by
                      the package at a later point in time. This point in time depends on the machine data.
                      In principle, this procedure can be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts and
                      manipulation tasks, but not in CMC scripts in Diff.
                      The specified machine data <data> is described directly in the control with the specified value
                      <value>.

                      Machine data / time of the function call
                      The following table shows which data is permitted and the point in time up to which it must be
                      written to ensure that the machine data still takes effect.

                       Machine data (MD)                                Latest point in time for a function call
                       $MN_SINAMICS_MAX_SLAVE_ADDRESS[0-3]              OnInit "System configuration" dialog page




Example
                      For the 840D sl, to exclude all CU320-2 DP as of slave address "8" on the PROFIBUS DP1
                      (X126) from the automatic device configuration, display and archiving, the function is used as
                      follows:
                      Prepare("$MN_SINAMICS_MAX_SLAVE_ADDRESS[0]",7)

7.8.19.2         Patch


Patch("<path>")
                       The Patch() procedure allows an internal component to be called.
                       The procedure can generally be called in all dialog scripts, step scripts, action scripts and

                       The user is responsible for the content of the component, i.e. whether it can be executed at the

                       Always specify the project and component name without a file extension "*upz", "*.upc".

Scripts library-specific syntax
                      For the definition of procedures and functions, the command scope has been extended by the
                      keywords "proc" and "func".
                      When you create a new definition, start the line with one of the keywords. This is followed by a
                      procedure name or function name, transferred arguments and on opening curly bracket. The
                      definition is completed with a closing curly bracket.


Example

                      Example of a procedure with the name "MyProcedure" and without transferred arguments

                       proc MyProcedure() {
                        ;User script
                       }


Example
                      If a procedure or function is to have transferred arguments, then as identifier use "$".
                      The arguments defined in this way have no type, i.e. you can use every data type known to the
                      scripting.
                      A maximum of 9 arguments can be transferred per definition. The query in the procedure or
                      function is performed by the construct Up.$1 to Up.$9.
                      The arguments therefore correspond to a UP variable and can be used directly in queries,
                      assignments or used again as function arguments.
                      Note that functions must have a return value. The return value is transferred by the return
                      function and can be represented by numerical values, character strings and UP variables. On
                      the other hand, it is not permissible that procedures return a value.

                      Example of a function with the name "MyFunction" and with 2 arguments and return value

                       func MyFunction($, $) {
                          Up.Arg1 = Up.$1
                          Up.Arg2 = Up.$2
                        ;User script
                          If Up.Result == true
                           Return(0)
                          Else
                           Return(-1)
                          Endif
                       }


Optional specifications
                      The example listed above completely describes a function defined by the user. You can add
                      optional specifications which facilitate later use.


SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                        419
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.9 Script libraries


                       Through a comment with the keyword "Description:", you can add a brief description of the
                       procedure or function.
                       A comment with the keyword "Arg1:" to "Arg9:" describes the transferred argument in more
                       detail. These specifications are taken into account in the later display in the context menu.
                       In this way, the project engineer can ensure during the function creation that another user
                       knows what the function performs and which arguments have to be used.
                       However, a supplementary condition for the use of the functionality is that there are no empty
                       lines between the comments and the function definition.

                       Example of a function definition
                       A function definition without the optional specifications results in the following standard display
                       in the context menu.

                        func MyFunction($, $) {




                       Example of a function definition with optional specifications
                       If you add the optional specifications to the definition, the display is extended by the information
                       shown in the following.

                        ;Description: Example of a function definition
                        ;Arg1:<string>
                        ;Arg2:<doVar>
                        func MyFunction($, $) {

7.9.4             Supplementary conditions for the use of script libraries
                      When using script libraries, the supplementary condition that the name of a procedure and the
                      name of a function must only be defined once applies. If you define a procedure or function
                      several times, this results in an error in the verification run.
                      However, a procedure and a function with the same name are permitted.
                      Processing a script within a procedure or a function is not logged in the logbook as default
                      setting. However, if you require this to be logged, then use function Logging() to activate
                      logging within your procedure or function.


Integrating libraries when creating a new project
                      Only when creating a new project, does Expert copy all of the libraries contained in the
                      subsequently listed paths to the project.
                      The paths are only applicable for the standard installation of Create MyConfig:
                      ● C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create MyConfig 4.8\UpLib
                      ● C:\ProgramData\SIEMENS\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create MyConfig 4.8\UpLib
                      As default setting, the paths contain the standard libraries supplied by Create MyConfig.
                      If you also save your own libraries in these paths, then these libraries are also integrated into
                      each new project as copy.
                      As standalone application, the "Create MyConfig Script Editor" and Shield load the
                      "%UP_LIB_PATH%" environment variable.
                      Expert and the integrated "Script Editor" do not know this environment variable.

                       This environment variable contains the paths to your script libraries for CMC scripts in Diff. As

7.9.5            CMC standard script libraries


7.9.5.1          Functions/procedures of the "Utilities" library
                       The ClrBit(), SetBit() procedures and the isBit() function are available in the
                       "Utilities" library. You can manipulate or query the individual bits of any variables with these
                       procedures or the function.


isBit (<bit>,<value>)
                       The isBit () function determines whether a bit is set. When the specified bit is set, the
                       function returns the value "true" or "false".
                       In principle, the isBit () function can be called in all:
                       ● Dialog scripts
                       ● Step scripts
                       ● Action scripts
                       ● Manipulation tasks
                       ● CMC scripts in Diff
                       You specify which bit is to be queried via the <bit> argument. The bits of a value are counted
                       from right to left starting with bit "0".
                       The <value> argument designates the identifier in whose value a bit is queried.
                       Identifiers can be, for example:
                       ● Up variables
                       ● Machine data
                       ● NC data


                                                                               SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
422                                                                             Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                          Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                  7.9 Script libraries


                      ● Drive data
                      ● Display data

                      Example
                      Up.bit_is = isBit(20,$MN_USER_DATA_HEX[0])


SetBit (<bit>,<value>)
                      The SetBit () procedure sets a bit to the value "1".
                      In principle, this function can be called in all:
                      ● Dialog scripts
                      ● Step scripts
                      ● Action scripts
                      ● Manipulation tasks
                      ● CMC scripts in Diff
                      You specify which bit is to be queried via the <bit> argument. The bits of a value are counted
                      from right to left starting with bit "0".
                      The <value> argument designates the identifier in whose value a bit is to be set.
                      Identifiers can be, for example:
                      ● Up variables
                      ● Machine data
                      ● NC data
                      ● Drive data
                      ● Display data

                      Example
                      $MN_USER_DATA_HEX[0] = SetBit(4,$MN_USER_DATA_HEX[0])


ClrBit (<bit>,<value>)
                      The ClrBit () procedure resets a bit to the value "0".
                      In principle, this procedure can be called in all:
                      ● Dialog scripts
                      ● Step scripts
                      ● Action scripts
                      ● Manipulation tasks
                      ● CMC scripts in Diff
                      You specify which bit is to be reset via the <bit> argument. The bits of a value are counted
                      from right to left starting with bit "0".

Create MyConfig - Expert

                       The <value> argument designates the identifier in whose value a bit is to be reset.
                       Identifiers can be, for example :
                       ● Up variables
                       ● Machine data
                       ● NC data
                       ● Drive data
                       ● Display data

                       Example
                       $MN_USER_DATA_HEX[0] = ClrBit(10,$MN_USER_DATA_HEX[0])


7.9.5.2          Functions/procedures of the "SINAMICS" library
                       The SinamicsTecActivate () and the SinamicsTecDeactivate () procedures are
                       available in the "SINAMICS“ library. The procedures activate or deactivate technological
                       functions in the drive.


SinamicsTecActivate("<TECNAME>", <DoVar>)
                       The SinamicsTecActivate() procedure activates technological functions of the drive.
                       The technological functions must be available on the CF card at the start of the CMC package.
                       You can also install the technological functions via "Additional software (*tgz)" in the same
                       package.
                       The procedure ensures that the corresponding index of the r4956[x] parameter is set in the
                       servo or the r4993[x] parameter in the CU.
                       The <TECNAME> argument must contain the name of the technological function, in accordance
                       with parameter p4955[x] (OA DO-specific Indentifier).
                       The <DoVar> argument contains the path of the DO to inform the procedure in which drive
                       object the technological function must be activated.
                       The specific user parameters of the technological functions must be set independently through
                       manipulation tasks.
                       In principle, this function can be called in all:
                       ● Dialog scripts
                       ● Step scripts
                       ● Action scripts
                       ● Manipulation tasks
                       ● CMC scripts in Diff

                       Examples

7.10              Configuring user interface languages for packages


7.10.1            User interface texts and user interface languages for packages


7.10.1.1          Overview


Configuration of multilingual packages
                      The support for multilingual packages has been extended. You can store user texts in different
                      languages in Expert, and these are automatically displayed in the selected language during
                      package runtime.
                      You can access language-dependent resources in the script via the ResText() and
                      ResFile() functions. The user texts are all information texts in fields with a yellow
                      background, the names of steps in the step tree and the texts in dialogs and messages that are
                      generated by scripts.
                      The following standard languages are available for the configuration corresponding to
                      SINUMERIK Operate:
                      English, French, German, Italian, Chinese (Simplified), Spanish.
                      In addition to HTML and text files, images can also be integrated in the package as resources.



                      Note
                      Language selection at the start of the package
                      The introduction of multilingual user texts in packages has caused the language selection to be
                      moved to the start of the package.
                      Restricted switching over of the package user interface language is possible during execution
                      via the key combination "Ctrl + L".

Create MyConfig - Expert
7.10 Configuring user interface languages for packages


Introduction
                  A CMC package displays two types of user interface texts during the processing through CMC-
                  Shield, these are system texts and user texts.
                  The system texts are the texts that are permanently stored in the system. Texts with a gray
                  background are generally system texts, e.g. the title of the dialog page, the labeling of the
                  standard buttons, selection boxes, etc. All texts that are not explicitly configured by the user, are
                  system texts.
                  The user texts are all texts that are configured by the project engineer while creating the
                  package in a project. The user texts are, for example, all information texts in fields with a yellow
                  background, the names of steps in the step tree and the texts in dialogs and messages that are
                  generated by scripts.


7.10.1.2       Standard languages of the user interface
                  Six standard languages are available for the user interface texts. You configure the user
                  interface texts in Expert. These texts are then displayed for the package execution. The
                  language that is displayed for the package execution is already defined by the project engineer.
                  Whereby there is the variant where the operator selects the standard language once at the start
                  of the package execution.
                  No changes are required for the system texts with regard to the six standard languages,
                  because they are always part of the package.
                  You must configure the user texts in Expert for the desired standard languages and store them
                  in language resource files.

                  The following standard languages are available for SINUMERIK Operate:

                  Table 7-39   Supported standard languages in Create MyConfig

                   Language                                          Language code*
                   English                                           ENG
                   French                                            FRA
                   German                                            DEU
                   Italian                                           ITA
                   Simplified Chinese                                CHS
                   Spanish                                           ESP

                  *The language codes correspond to the language abbreviations of the language files used in the
                  SINUMERIK Operate operating software




7.10.2         Basic procedure for configuring the user interface languages

                  You create a project with user texts that you store in the corresponding properties fields of the
                  dialogs and steps in a standard language (Page 425) which you have selected. When you have
                  completed the configurations, export your standard language in standardized "*.ts"language
                  resource files. Forward the language resource files that you have created to a translation office
                  for translation into one or more of your desired standard languages.

7.10.3             Language resource files
                      The language resource files are available for managing the user interface languages.

                      The following language resource files are created in the respective language resource folder:
                      ● "Dialog.ts" - contains information texts of the dialogs.
                      ● "Step.ts" - contains information texts of the steps and the step names.
                      ● "User.ts" - contains texts that are used in the scripts.
                      You can find the entry to the language resource folders in the project folder via the "Package"
                      tab > "Language" >"Manage resources" > "List of the language resources" dialog.
                      The language resource files are assigned to the respective language via the language resource
                      folder.
                      The language resource files are created with the "Resource Editor (Page 438)" integrated in
                      Create MyConfig.
                      The language resource files are provided in an XML format that conforms to the requirements
                      of the ""Linguist"" translation tool. This format is also used for SINUMERIK Operate.

                      Note
                      Only change the resource files with the "Resource Editor"
                      Because of their special format, we recommend that the resource files are changed only with
                      the integrated "Resource Editor".
                      Any errors that result from using an unsuitable tool can make the file unusable.

                      Note
                      Project example for the user interface languages
                      A project example for the user interface language is contained in the "Examples" folder in the
                      installation directory for Create MyConfig 4.8 SP1.

                      managed via the "List of language resources" dialog.

7.10 Configuring user interface languages for packages


                  You can open the dialog in Expert at: "Project folder" > "Package" tab > "Language" > "Manage
                  resources" via the   button.
                  Double-click a "*.ts" language resource file to open the "Resource Editor (Page 438)".
                  The resource files are generally below the language folderin the "List of language resources".
                  During the package execution, those resource files are used that correspond to the language
                  selection in the assigned language folder. If the package does not find a file in the language
                  folder, the file is automatically sought in the "res" root folder and used.
                  The "res" root folder also contains the language folders.

                  This behavior of the package has two advantages:
                  1. During the conversion of a project lower than CMC 4.8 to the current version, all resource
                     files are stored in the "res" root folder. This is required because the language is unknown
                     and therefore there is no automatic assignment to a language folder. You can move these
                     files to a language folder at any time.
                  2. Resource files that are used language-neutrally in all languages, and therefore do not have
                     to be translated, do not have to be stored in each language folder. These files, e.g. images,
                     are only stored once in the "res" root folder. This avoids multiple update work.

                  The 1st standard language is the language in which you have stored the texts in plain text on

                  would mean double the update work. The texts of the 1st standard language are already
                  updated in the user interface.
                  A note on Do not create "Dialog.ts" and "Step.ts" in the configuration language can be found in
                  Section "Procedure for 2nd to 6th standard language (Page 433)".

                     via the "New language"      button.




                  3. Double-click to open the "eng" folder.

Creating the "Dialog.ts" and "Step.ts" files

                  Note
                  Do not create "Dialog.ts" and "Step.ts" files in the 1st standard language
                  Do not create the "Dialog.ts" and "Step.ts" language resource files in the language folder which
                  corresponds to the language in which you have already stored texts on the user interface of
                  Expert.
                  Non-observance during package execution can result in a conflict between the texts from the
                  language resource files and the texts that you have already stored in the user interface. The
                  system prefers the texts of the TS files.
                  The different sources can result in you seeing texts during package execution that you have not
                  configured in the user interface. This conflict can occur if you have not updated the TS files.
                  In order that you do not have to update the texts twice, we recommend that you:
                  Create the "Dialog.ts" and "Step.ts" files only for the standard languages that you really want
                  to be translated.
                  Let the language resource files be translated only at the end of the project processing.

                   The "Create MyConfig Resource Editor" is integrated in Expert for displaying and editing the

                      The dialogs and steps are configured in the project folder in the "Dialogs" and "Steps" tabs. All

                      You can also enter comments that are not displayed during package execution.
                      All the changes are accepted and the editor closed after confirmation with the "OK" button. Click
                      "Cancel" to close the "Resource Editor" without accepting the changes.
                      You can add known IDs or perform other usual text operations via the context menu.

7.10.7          Export of the language resource files for translation
                    The "*.ts"language resource files are structured in a format that simplifies the translation of the
                    contained texts.
                    The language resource files"*.ts" are provided in an XML format that conforms to the
                    requirements of the ""Linguist"" translation tool and is compatible with this. This format is also
                    used by SINUMERIK Operate. Export all your language resource files from the project in order
                    to forward them to your translation office and to import them back into the project after
                    translation.

                    To export the files, proceed as follows:
                    1. In the folder in the "List of language resources" dialog, select the files of your basic language
                       or the 1st standard language that you want to translate.
                    2. Click the appropriate "*.ts"language resource file.
                    3. Right-click and select "Export…" in the context menu.
                    4. Place the language resource files in the desired path and language folder to transfer for
                       translation.


                    Note
                    Text in angle brackets
                    Text placed within angle brackets in the language resource files must never be translated.
                    For example:"<source>text</source>"
                    This text represents an identification (ID) for the text to be output, which must be identical for
                    all languages.

7.10.8            Import of the language resource files after translation
                      After the translation of your language resource files, import them into your project as described
                      in the following.
                      Whereby, you overwrite the existing files which you exported before the translation. Non-
                      translated texts of your 1st standard language, e.g. your native language, are replaced by texts
                      of the standard languages 2 to 6.




7.10.9            Use of the ResFile() function


ResFile("<file>")
                      The ResFile() function is for the use or call of text resources in the form of files.
                      To display the contents of a file, you can use the ResFile() function via the properties fields
                      for information texts in the "Dialogs" and "Steps" tabs as an alternative to plain text. Use in the
                      script is also possible.
                      The file specified via the <file> argument must be, with the same name in different
                      languages, below the respective folder in the "List of language resources". The file must be in
                      the "*.txt", "*.htm" or "*.html" format.
                      The associated file is then used for the package execution in accordance with the selected
                      language. Whereby, the file is first sought in the language folder, e.g. "deu" for the selected
                      language "German" and used. If the file is not found in the language folder, it is sought one level
                      higher in the "res" root folder of the "List of language resources" and, if available used. This
                      mechanism also allows the same file to be used for different languages, without having to store
                      the file several times.


Example of ResFile()
                      Calling the function in the information text of the "Package configuration" dialog page:
                      =ResFile("HintForKonfiguration.txt")




                      Figure 7-136     Package configuration - Information text

7.10 Configuring user interface languages for packages


7.10.10        Use of the ResText() function


ResText("<resid>"[, "<arg>"]*)
                  The ResText() function calls text resources in the form of information texts from the "User.ts"
                  language resource file.
                  The "User.ts" file is blow the respective language folder in the "List of language resources". The
                  texts from the "User.ts" belonging to the language are then used for the package execution in
                  accordance with the selected language.
                  If you work with language-dependent text, the ResText() function is used in scripts, e.g.
                  message boxes, input dialogs, etc., as an alternative to plain text.
                  To call the "Information text" of the "User.ts" file, specify the "ID" in the "User.ts" file via the
                  <resid> argument.
                  Up to 9 optional <arg> arguments are used to be able to take over variable text components
                  from the script in the called information text.
                  As placeholders for the <arg> arguments transferred by the function, the "%1" to "%9"
                  characters are used in the information text of the "User.ts".


Example 1 of ResText()
                  Up.MSG1 = ResText("T1")
                  MSG("$(Up.MSG1)")




                  Figure 7-137    Configuration in the "Resource Editor"




                  Figure 7-138    Package execution - Example 1

444                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                             Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                7.10 Configuring user interface languages for packages


Example 2 of ResText()

                         Up.Summand_1 = 2
                         Up.Summand_2 = 3
                         Up.Summe = Up.Summand_1 + Up.Summand_2
                         Up.MSG2 = ResText("ADD",Up.Summand_1,Up.Summand_2,Up.Summe)
                         MSG("$(Up.MSG2)")

7.10.11           Language selection
                      Configuration language
                      The project engineer specifies the language selection for the interface of the Package
                      execution in the "Package" > "Language" > "Selection" (Page 191) tab. The operator cannot
                      change this selection for the package execution.
                      The language is selected via the "Selection" property. If the "not configured" suffix is displayed
                      next to the language in the drop-down list, although you can select the language, no associated
                      language resources have been configured.

                  "Operator selection" configuration
                  In addition to the six standard languages available for selection, the project engineer can

                  selects the language by clicking the appropriate language button.

                  ● Expert: "Project folder" > "Package" tab > "Language" > "Selection" (project engineer)
                  ● Via configuration file, for command line (project engineer)
                  ● During "Operator selection" configuration: When the package execution (operator) is started
