7.10.12           Linking steps
                      Please note the following points when linking steps:
                      ● The language selection is specified in the main project.
                      ● The language resources of the linked steps are in a separate subproject and are also
                        managed in the subproject.
                      ● The language resources for the subproject are automatically taken into the main project
                        during the deployment of the main project.
                      ● The subproject has no access to the language resources of the main project.
                      ● After relevant changes to the subproject, the main project must be redeployed.
                      ● The main project must have access to the language resources of the subproject, i.e. any
                        links present there, must be accessible and terminable.
                      Further information can be found at Linking of steps (Page 295).




7.10.13           Conversion from projects with CMC version < version 4.8
                      From projects with the version "< CMC version 4.8", information texts in the form of files in
                      dialogs are converted in a call through the ResFile() function.
                      The information texts are retained. File calls are transferred in the ResFile() function.
                      Whereby the files in the "List of language resources" are taken into the "res" root directory
                      because they cannot automatically be assigned to any language.
                      You can assign these files later to a standard language by inserting the files via the "Export…"
                      context menu in a language folder, e.g. "deu", "eng".
                      Then remove the original files from the "res" root directory.
                      Information texts in plain text form are taken over unchanged during the conversion. To make
                      these texts language-dependent, proceed as described in Section Creation of the language
                      resource files (Page 431).

System variables for Expert

                      using the Package (Page 186), Dialogs (Page 192) andSteps (Page 285).

Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                        447
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.11 Reference list, system variables


                   Use of system variables is supported in the script editor for dialog, step and task scripts and in
                   tasks using the automatic completion function (IntelliSense).
                   Most system variables are provided with values for the first time during configuration. These
                   values can be modified when using configuration files for the deployment or executing the
                   package. Some variables are only available during the package execution.
                   During package execution as well, system variables can be changed in dialog, step or task
                   scripts or manipulation tasks by write accesses before these system variables come into effect
                   in the sequence.

                   Conventions
                   Take the following conventions into account:
                   ● Upper/lower-case is not relevant.
                   ● In compound names, the beginnings of words are written in uppercase for better legibility.
                   ● Values of enumerations are written in uppercase throughout.

Enable step - Up.$Step[id].Activated
                   The activation status of a specific step is defined in the step tree using
                   the Up.$Step[id].Activated system variable.
                   The Up.$Step[id].Activated system variable supplies the value "true" for all steps whose
                   step icon (option button or checkbox) are displayed in white or green with checkmark.
                   The value "false" is signaled for all other step icons that do not have a checkmark.
                   However, the activated step is still not considered during package execution as long as the step
                   is additionally assigned the "Execute" status and displayed in green.

                   You configure the step configuration for each step individually, either using the context menu

                   Note
                   Step activation
                   You can configure step activation directly in the step tree. The step activation becomes
                   immediately active.




Executing steps - Up.$Step[id].Processing
                   The execution status for package execution is defined in the step tree with
                   the Up.$Step[id].Processing system variable.
                   The Up.$Step[id].Processing system variable supplies the value "true" for all steps
                   whose step icon (option button or checkbox) has already been activated and are displayed in
                   green. The selected step in green and all of its higher-level steps are performed during package
                   execution. Activated substeps are marked in green and are thus executed if the higher-level
                   step is activated. The step in the first level is always assigned the execution status during
                   activation.
                   The value "false" is returned for all other step icons that have a white background.

7.12                Cross references


7.12.1              Overview


Cross reference objects
                       Projects generated in CMC Expert can be very complex, and generally contain a large number
                       of cross-reference objects.
                       Cross-reference objects are identifiers of machine data, user and system variables, linked files
                       and folders. These cross-reference objects are configured at various positions of use within the
                       project and the linked components. In the form of a table, the cross-reference function shows
                       you where all of the cross-reference objects are used.
                       This table can be exported using the context menu.




                                                                                      SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
472                                                                                    Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                       Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                           7.12 Cross references


7.12.2            Display cross references


Display options
                      There are several ways of displaying cross references. Cross references can be displayed for
                      a project with all linked components, for an individual component or for a cross-reference object
                      (e.g. an identifier in a manipulation task).
                      For the project with all linked components, select "Project > Display cross-references" and for
                      individual components "Component > Display cross-references."
                      Optionally you can display the corresponding cross references using the symbol bar.
                      To display individual cross-reference objects, put the cursor on the object in the editor and
                      select "Go to position of use" from the shortcut menu. The cross-references are then filtered
                      according to the object name. The object name of part of it can also be entered in the filter field
                      manually.


Overview of the user interface
                      The list of locations where cross reference objects are used is grouped using the two "Identifier"
                      and "Folder and file objects" tabs:

                      "Identifier" tab




Identifier            Identifier is the unique identification of the cross reference object within the list.
Operator              The operator specifies how the cross reference object is processed at the position where it is used.
Project/              Indicates in which project or in which component the cross-reference object is located.
Component
Step/                 Indicates in which step or task the cross-reference object is located.
task
Line                  Indicates in which line, the cross-reference object is located.

7.12.4            Filter according to identifier or object
                      You can enter a partial string in the input field, via which the column "Identifier" or "Object" is
                      filtered. All objects are listed that contain this character string at any position in the name.
                      You reset the filter by entering an empty string.

                      Procedure
                      If you want to filter the cross-references according to a certain string, proceed as follows:




                      To filter a selected identifier:
                      ● Enter the required character string into the field using the keyboard.
                      ● Or use the context menu "Go to position of use" in the Script Editor.




                      Filtering is applied to the "Identifier" or "Object" column.

                   Legal information on Open Source Software and Commercial off-the-shelf

                   these files.

                  To create a package, proceed as follows:
                  1. Select "Project" > "Deploy" and select whether you want to create a Windows package or a
                     Linux package.
                  2. Select a name and a target directory for the package.
                     An automatic verification run is started that checks the package for inconsistencies and
                     errors. You can also perform the verification run manually via the "Verification run" button.


                  Note
                  Note for the Linux package
                  In a Linux package, no file or path information with accented characters in the file names or
                  folder names can be used on the NCU.

                  Note
                  Package names
                  Avoid the designations "install", "installation" or "setup" in the names of packages.
                  These designations result in confirmation prompts from Windows and unmotivated error
                  messages on the PCU.




7.14           Password protection


7.14.1         Overview
                  Create MyConfig offers password protection for projects, components, packages and
                  logbooks. Using this password protection, you can protect your own know-how from being
                  viewed and changed by unauthorized persons.

                  NOTICE
                  Password protection - read-protection
                  Password protection protects the logbook from unwanted viewing by third parties.
                  Note that password protection provides only basic read protection.
                  Because the content of logbooks does not make any claim for confidentiality, no encryption is
                  provided.
                  The password protection does not provide any secure protection against cyber attacks.




                                                                         SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo

                                                                                                        Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                        7.14 Password protection


                      You can use the password list to define various access levels. You can then execute the
                      following activities only by entering the correct password:
                      ● Opening or saving a project or a component.
                      ● Executing a package at the machine or reimporting this package as project.
                      ● Viewing a protected logbook.

7.14 Password protection


                  Note
                  Observing security for projects and components
                  Note the following when handling projects and components, including any linked data:
                  ● As protection, regularly install security updates and patches for the installed operating
                    system
                  ● Transfer this data only over secure transmission routes
                    – Use signed or encrypted e-mails to ensure integrity.
                    – When using data storage media (USB sticks, hard disks, etc.), ensure that they are
                        classified as being secure. A regular virus check must be carried out for these data
                        storage media.
                    This applies to all CMC files, such as package and project configurations, manipulation
                    tasks.




7.14.2.1        Access levels
                  In Expert, a CMC project is protected using three access levels with different authorization
                  levels. The same access levels are also applied for components. It is necessary to specifically
                  protect components, because components can be opened and processed independently of
                  projects.
                  You can only view protected CMC projects or protected components if you have a password
                  with one of these access levels.
                  Converted projects from older versions or newly created projects are unprotected and can be
                  edited as previously. You can subsequently provide projects with protection at any time.
                  To enter a password that permits defined processing permissions, use "Project > Password
                  protection > Enter password...."


Access levels

                   Access level                                   Authorizations
                   "Read project"                                 ● Opening a project/component for reading
                   "Change project"                               ● Opening a project/component for reading
                                                                  ● Changing and saving a project/component
                   "Full access to project"                       ● Opening a project/component for reading
                                                                  ● Changing and saving a project/component
                                                                  ● Editing a project/component password list -
                                                                    transfer password list to components

7.14.2.2          Editing a password list


Requirement
                      You already define the password protection when you create a project on the Package tab
                      under Project - General > Access (Page 186).
                      To make changes at a later time, e.g. activate password protection or manage the password
                      list, use the main menu in Expert: "Project > Password protection > Edit password list...". The
                      dialog "Edit password list [Rights without a password]" is opened.
                      If there is already password protection, then you will be initially asked to enter the password for
                      "Full access".

                      By default, when creating a new project or an external component, an entry <Rights without

①            Add "New password"

             If you wish to protect your project/your component within the company, then you can extend the access rights.
             There must always be at least one password with full access. Expert checks that this really is the case. This means
             that it is not possible to completely lock a project / a component as a result of an incorrectly configured dialog.

             Here, you can assign a password with up to 24 characters for specific access permissions.

7.14.2.3           Transferring a password list to existing components



                      NOTICE
                      Password protection does not act for linked external files
                      Note that password protection (read protection) acts only for projects, packages as well as
                      internal linked components and files.
                      External linked files are ignored by the password protection.
                      Examples of external linked files:
                      ● Archives
                      ● Cycles
                      ● Manipulation tasks
                      ● Configuration files
                      ● etc.




Applications
                      The relevant dialog for transferring the password list is started via the
                      "Project or Component" > "Password protection" > "Transfer the password list" > "To project
                      components... / to components of an archive folder..." main menu.
                      For some applications, it is desirable to manually transfer your password list to your
                      components.
                      For example:
                      ● You have created a project with a lot of internal linked, internal unlinked as well as external
                        linked components.
                      ● You have created a new password list to protect the project or have changed it. You want
                        to transfer this password list to all of the components of your project.
                      ● You have created many unlinked components. You want to transfer subsequent changes to
                        the password list to these components.

                       ⑤      Action

                      Also observe the transfer of rights for "Rights without password"
                      If you have also changed the rights of the "Default password" for the "Rights without password"
                      in your source for the transfer (project or component) and also want to transfer this change, you
                      must also activate this password for the transfer. Generally, "Replace" makes sense as action.
                      This means that if you create new passwords in your password lists and transfer rights from
                      "Rechte ohne Kennwort", you remove these rights from the "Rights without password".
                      Ensure during transfer that you transfer not only your new passwords, but also the "Rights
                      without password", because otherwise this would still retain all rights and your components
                      would not be protected.




7.15              Package execution


7.15.1            Requirements


Processing or executing Create MyConfig packages
                      You can deploy Create MyConfig packages using Expert for Windows and Linux systems.
                      For Linux operating systems running on the NCU/PPU, Expert generates a file with the
                      extension ""*.usz"" (Linux package).
                      For Windows operating systems running on the PCU, PG or PC, a file with the extension
                      ""*.exe"" (Windows package) is generated.
                      The following sections describes the procedure for the Windows and Linux operating systems.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                                  485
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.15 Package execution


Package execution using NCU/PPU

                  Observe the following points if an NCU/PPU is involved during package execution (NCU/PPU
                  data area active):
                  ● To prevent errors during package execution, the NCU/PPU system state must be consistent.
                     – Before starting a CMC package, the NCU/PPU must be in a state in which the ""RDY""
                       and ""RUN"" LEDs are lit green and the 7-segment display displays a "6" with flashing
                       point.
                     – If a system software is located on the CF card, the NC status display must be at "6" and
                       the PLC status display should be "Green" before a package is started.
                       Use a service stick for a CF card without system software.
                     – Load the factory settings prior to a drive unit configuration if inconsistent data is found on
                       the control. Failure to adhere to this can lead to undefined conditions.
                     – For a drive unit configuration - automatic configuration or user-specified topology - the
                       PLC hardware configuration must be consistent with the hardware used with regard to
                       the NCU and NX configuration.
                       The PLC hardware configuration may contain more NX modules than are available on
                       the machine.
                     – The SINAMICS data must be consistent and match the hardware configuration.
                     – If you renumber the drive objects, then you are responsible for adapting the BICO
                       interconnections. The BICO interconnections are not adapted automatically by CMC.
                     – On the "End" dialog page, you must ensure that the package has been executed without
                       errors.
                       If processing took place with errors, you must check the log file as to whether there will
                       be any likely effects on functionality.
                  If this state is not present before the start of a CMC commissioning package, then it can be
                  achieved by a memory reset and loading of default data of the individual control components.

                  Procedure, memory reset / load standard data

                  For NCU/PPU, proceed as follows:
                  1. NC: S3 = 1 and OFF/ON.
                  2. Then S3 = 0 and S4 = 3 and OFF/ON.
                  3. Wait until ramp-up in "6" with flashing point, which can take several minutes. Only then
                     perform the memory reset request (S4 ...2.. 3.. 2..).
                  4. Then "S4" back to "0".
                  5. SINAMICS: Empty the folder "user/sinamics/data" on the CF card followed by ON/OFF.

7.15.2            Executing the package under Windows


7.15.2.1          Executing a standard package


Precondition
                      If the package to be executed under Windows should also access the NCU/PPU data (the
                      "NCU" area is activated in the package), the NCU/PPU must access a shared directory on the
                      Windows computer (PCU/PG/PC) on which the package is executed.

                      Note
                      If an active firewall prevents access from the NCU/PPU to the PG/PC, the package execution
                      cannot be started from the PG/PC.
                      In this case, the package can be executed on the PCU50 or deployed as a Linux package.
                      Further information can be found in Section Executing the package under Linux (Page 489).


                      The following is required for the execution of (Windows) packages that also access data of the
                      NCU:
                      ● A network connection to the NCU/PPU or PCU.
                      ● Create MyConfig NcuShareService
                        During the package execution, before establishing the connection to the NCU/PPU, a check
                        is made as to whether a sufficiently current version of Create MyConfig NcuShareService is
                        available on the Windows system.
                        If no sufficiently current version is found, the package execution installs a current version.
                        This version is part of the package.
                        During package execution, Create MyConfigNcuShareService shares the "C:\ProgramData
                        \Siemens\UpNcuShare" folder as exchange release.
                        Once the package execution has been completed, the service revokes the release again.


NcuShareService
                      The NcuShareService service is required to execute CMC packages with an NCU/PPU share
                      component for Windows PC or PCU50. The service activates an exchange release (share) on
                      the Windows system for the duration of the package execution.

                      The following options are available for installing the NcuShareService service on a Windows
                      PC (PG or PCU):
                      1. Automatically during the installation of the current CNC version.
                      2. Manual installation of NcuShareService
                      3. Automatically by the CMC package


Starting to execute the package under Windows
                      Establish a network connection between the PC and the control devices (NCU7x0, PCU) that
                      are to be processed with the package.


SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                        487
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.15 Package execution


                  The package created by Expert for Windows with the file extension "*.exe" can be started on the
                  PCU, the PG or the PC with "Run..." or by double-clicking.
                  If the package file is the only exe file in the "Install" folder of a USB medium inserted in the PCU
                  (USB FlashDrive, hard disk, CD), then the file is automatically started when the PCU is booted.

                  Note
                  Simultaneously starting several packages
                  Carefully note that it is not permissible to simultaneously start several packages.
                  A package may only be started if no other package is running.




                  Note
                  Package names
                  Avoid the designations "install", "installation" or "setup" in the names of packages.
                  These designations result in confirmation prompts from Windows and unmotivated error
                  messages on the PCU.




                  Note
                  Unknown USB medium
                  For existing PCU-base systems, carefully ensure that the USB medium is known to the PCU,
                  as a new medium is installed after the start routine for the package. This means that it may be
                  necessary to insert the USB medium and then switch-off and switch-on the PCU again after
                  approximately 30 seconds.




                  Note
                  In a PCU with Windows 7, various settings are required to permit package execution for
                  automated commissioning.




7.15.2.2       Executing the package on the PCU 50 from the network
                  Windows packages can be executed on the PCU 50. The package is on a network drive.

Requirements
                      Take the following requirements into account:
                      ● There must be a connection to the network drive.
                      ● The folder containing the Windows package must be released for a user of the PCU 50
                        (default user "auduser") for read and write access.
                      ● If the Windows package contains a restart of the PCU 50 (e.g. due to an installation), work
                        with the PCU-local default user "auduser" and password "SUNRISE".


Procedure
                      1. Deploy the project in Expert as Windows package.
                      2. Save the Windows package in a folder of the network drive.
                      3. Release the network drive folder for users of the PCU 50 (preferred default user "auduser").
                      4. Let the PCU 50 start up in the Service Desktop.
                         Note
                         Do not start SINUMERIK Operate.

                      5. In the Windows Start menu, select "Start > Run".
                      6. Enter the following command: "\\<IP address or UNC name>\<share name>
                         \<package name>"
                         e. g. \\10.8.6.16\Package folder\Machine_1.exe
                      7. Follow the instructions of the package dialogs.

7.15.3            Executing the package under Linux


7.15.3.1          Introduction
                      Expert can deploy the package to a "normal USB FlashDrive" (or hard disk or CD) or a service
                      USB FlashDrive from Siemens. Both versions result in a different system behavior which is
                      subsequently explained.


SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                       489
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.15 Package execution


Package execution from "normal USB FlashDrive":
                  If the package was transferred to a "normal USB Flash Drive" (or hard disk or CD) that cannot
                  be booted because it does not contain a Linux boot system from Siemens, the NCU/PPU starts
                  Linux from the CompactFlash card and then starts the package on the USB medium.
                  For this version, an operable Linux system (system software) must be available on the
                  CompactFlash card. The system software can be upgraded or reinstalled by the package.


Package execution from the service USB FlashDrive:
                  If the package was transferred to a service USB FlashDrive (from Siemens) that is bootable
                  because it contains a Linux boot system from Siemens, the NCU/PPU starts Linux from this
                  USB FlashDrive and then starts the package on the USB FlashDrive.
                  For this version, an operable Linux system is not required on the CompactFlash card (system
                  software), i.e. the CompactFlash card can also be empty.

                  Note
                  In this case, reinstallation of the system software is a precondition for package execution.


                  As soon as the installation on the CompactFlash card has completed, the package restarts the
                  NCU/PPU and forces Linux to start from the CompactFlash card.
                  If "None" or "Upgrade" is selected in the "CNC software" dialog and a system exists on the CF
                  card, the start is performed from the CF card during the dialog execution.
                  Package execution then continues as for a "normal USB FlashDrive".


7.15.3.2       Package execution on the NCU/PPU from the USB medium
                  The package generated by Expert for Linux with file extension "usz" should be transferred to the
                  root directory of a USB medium (USB FlashDrive, hard disk) – and this medium should be
                  inserted in a direct USB interface (X125 or X135) of the NCU 7x0. The package is automatically
                  started when the NCU/PPU boots.
                  If there are several packages in the start folder, they will be provided on the Package selection
                  dialog page.
                  If you select a package other than the default package for execution, clicking the Next button
                  ends the default package and starts the newly selected package.
                  This causes the VNC server of the NCU/PPU to restart. In this context, there is a loss of
                  connection to all VNC viewers.
                  The VNC viewer running on the TCU is then automatically ended and restarted.
                  An external VNC viewer running under Windows on your PC/PG or the PCU might possibly
                  have to be restarted if no automatic connection attempts were set for this.


7.15.3.3       Package execution on NCU/PPU from the CompactFlash card
                  Under some circumstances, Linux packages can be executed from the CF card of the NCU/
                  PPU that contains the CNC software.




                                                                         SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
490                                                                       Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                            Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                              7.15 Package execution


Requirements
                      The following requirements apply:
                      ● The CompactFlash card must contain a bootable CNC system.
                      ● Fresh installation or upgrading is not permissible.
                      ● The Linux package <name> can be stored under any path <path> on the CompactFlash
                        card.
                        We recommend storage according to the responsibility below "/oem" or "/user"


Procedure
                      1. Create an "sci.ini" file with the entry: "Start=<path>/<name>".
                         Example: Start=/user/Test.usz
                      2. Save this file in the "/<responsible>/system/etc" folder of the CompactFlash card.
                         Whereby, <responsible> can be ""siemens"", ""addon"", ""oem"" or ""user"".
                      3. Activate the "Off/on" main switch.
                      4. Follow the instructions of the package dialogs.
                         Note
                         The "sci.ini" file is deleted from the package once it has been started. This will ensure that
                         a package is not unintentionally executed several times.



7.15.3.4          Package execution on the NCU/PPU from the network
                      Linux packages can also be executed from a network drive.

                      Note
                      Executing the Linux package by the network
                      The execution of a Linux package by the network is only possible as of CNC-SW 4.5.
                      In earlier CNC SW versions, the package cannot be saved on the network, i.e. it is not possible
                      to back up or save the logbook.




Procedure
                      1. Create an "sci.ini" file with the entry:
                         Start=//<domain>/<user>%<password>@<Server>/<release>/<package
                         name>.usz
                         The specification of the domain is optional.
                         Example:
                         Start=//wwprod/user%pass@192.168.100.2/Share/NCU_Pack.usz
                      2. Save this file in the "/<responsible>/system/etc" folder of the CompactFlash card.
                         Whereby, <responsible> can be "siemens", "addon", "oem" or "user".




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                         491
Create MyConfig - Expert

                  3. Actuate the "Off/On" main switch.
                  4. Follow the instructions of the package dialogs.
                     Note
                     The "sci.ini" file is deleted from the package once it has been started. This will ensure that
                     a package is not unintentionally executed several times.

7.15.4         Package execution logbook


7.15.4.1       General information about the logbook
                  The logbook is automatically generated during package execution. The logbook contains
                  detailed information about the package. All package actions are documented.

                  Note
                  Logbook - diagnostics
                  Note that logbooks do not provide any proof of correct commissioning, but rather are used for
                  diagnosis.


                  For an unprotected logbook, the logbook is saved in the HTML format in a file with the extension
                  "*.htm".
                  A password-protected logbook is saved in the HTML format in a file with the extension "*.exe".
                  Both files are displayed in your Web browser, although the ""*.exe"" file is displayed only after
                  the correct password is specified.




                                                                         SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
492                                                                       Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                             Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                              7.15 Package execution


                      Start the "*.exe" file for display using "Run" or a double-click.

                      NOTICE
                      Password protection - read-protection
                      Password protection protects the logbook from unwanted viewing by third parties.
                      Note that password protection provides only basic read protection.
                      Because the content of logbooks does not make any claim for confidentiality, no encryption is
                      provided.


                      Project folder
                      When configuring, specify the "Storage location" and "File name" for the logbook in the project
                      folder on the "Finish" dialog page. This information is used as user-specified values in the "Save
                      project as" dialog when the package execution has completed.
                      If no details for "Storage location" and "File name" of the logbook are entered, the package
                      folder and "<package_<YYYYMMDDhhmm>" are used as storage location and file name,
                      respectively.
                      The values configured in Expert are saved in system variables
                      "Up.$Dialog.PackageEnd.LogDir" and "Up.$Dialog.PackageEnd.LogName", and
                      can be manipulated using a script during the package runtime.
                      Further information can be found at System variables for the Finish dialog (Page 461) and at
                      DateTime>Example (Page 409).


Automatic logbook archiving
                      In addition to "manually saving" the logbook, the package always automatically stores the
                      logbook on the control.
                      For the PCU 50, the logbook with the name "<Package name_YYYYMMDDHHMM>"
                      (unprotected) or "<Package name_YYYYMMDDHHMM.htmlog.exe>" (password-protected)
                      is located under D$\UP and on the NCU/PPU under /install.
                      If the PCU and the NCU/PPU are involved with the package execution, the package is
                      automatically stored only on the PCU.

7.15.4.3          Package selection
                      The package selection is not a dialog page that can be configured. This instance is always
                      displayed in the logbook.
                      The package only automatically displays the Package selection dialog if there is more than one
                      package available for execution - or no package was uniquely started by a (batch) command
                      or double-click. This dialog prompts users to enter the package that should be used.

                      The main Package selection instance contains the following information:
                      ● Time of day that this package was started.
                      ● Package:
                        Name of the package that was started.
                      ● UserVersion:
                        If a user version was entered, then it is displayed here.
                      ● Computer:
                        Name of the computer on which the package execution was started.
                      ● User:
                        The name of the user that logged onto the computer and started package execution.
                      ● Windows:
                        The Windows version of the computer on which the package was executed.

                    Example:

                    #If_201611291030.htm'
                    0 warning(s), 0 error(s), 0 fault(s)
                    End: Di 29. Nov 10:30:24 2016

                    Explanatory note about Warnings, Errors and Faults
                    ● Warnings are normally warnings set by the project engineer that require from the user a
                      decision with regard to a package termination or continuation.
                    ● Errors are errors detected by the package or error messages set by the project engineer that
                      force termination of the package because further useful execution is no longer possible.
                    ● Faults are faults reported by the control system that cause termination of the package
                      execution.

7.16              Command line call


7.16.1            Packaged deployed by Expert
                      To deploy a package, you can start Create MyConfig Expert in the Command line mode. The
                      command line call is envisaged for the automated deployment of packages.
                      For deployment in the Command line mode, specify command line parameters (switches),
                      which are in some instances optional.
                      You can also specify a package configuration file that replaces the configurations in the
                      package via the command line parameters.
                      If a package configuration file is specified, then these settings are applied to the package - and
                      this is followed by deployment with all of the specified command line parameters.


Call
                      Write the command subsequently shown as well as all associated switches and arguments in
                      one line to a batch file or a command line interface.

                      Deployment with verification run in the silent mode
                      Expert.exe /silent /deploy [/config <Path config file>] [/protect]
                      [/log <Path log file>] <Path project file>
                      The switches in square brackets are optional.

                      Example:
                      Expert.exe /silent /deploy /config ./update.upcfg /log "D:\Log\L1
                      V1.xml" D:\Projects\MyProject.upz


Notes

                      Note the following information for the command line call:

                      Note
                      Specification of the complete path for "Expert.exe"
                      Specify the complete path of the "Expert.exe", or transfer this in the environment variable
                      "Path".
                      Example:
                      "C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create MyConfig 4.8\Expert.exe"

                      Note
                      Observe the sequence of the switches
                      Write the switches in the specified sequence.
                      When doing this, observe Section "Call" and Table "Significance of the switches".




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                          503
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.16 Command line call


                  Note
                  Path data
                  ● If the path data contains spaces, write the path data in straight quotation marks.
                     Example:
                     "C:\path with spaces\Expert_Logfile.xml"
                  ● Paths must never end with '\'.

                  Note
                  Saving batch files
                  Always save batch files with ANSI/ASCII coding.

                  Note
                  Accented characters and special characters
                  Avoid using accented characters and special characters in path names.
                  To allow special characters or accented characters to be correctly processed in specified
                  paths, batch files with command line calls must be saved with the same character set as used
                  by the region-specific command line interpreter "cmd.exe".
                  For example, "Codepage850", also known as "DOS-Latin-1", applies to the region Western
                  Europe.
                  The "Notepad" editor integrated in Windows does not provide support when it comes to saving
                  files with this character set.

                  Note
                  Uppercase/lowercase
                  For the command line switches and arguments, always use the specified uppercase/lowercase
                  syntax.

                  Note
                  Absolute/relative path
                  You can specify the absolute path or the relative path.
                  The relative path with ".\" or "./" refers to the current work folder, where the batch or CMD
                  was called.
                  If no path is specified, the work folder also applies.

                  Note
                  Change to the command line interface
                  The command line interface supports the command line interface documented in
                  versions < CMC 4.7 SP1 HF1.
                  The new switch "/config" <"Path of the configuration file"> must not be used within the context
                  of the previous definition.

7.17              SINAMICS device configuration


7.17.1            Production of modular machines
                      The Create MyConfig (CMC) engineering software supports both the automated production of
                      modular machines for the machine manufacturer as well as the upgrade of machines for end
                      customers, which requires only a limited number of operator actions.
                      The production of machines with 840D sl requires a basic commissioning of the SINAMICS,
                      generally designated as "System configuration". The system configuration can be performed
                      with CMC either as "Automatic configuration" or as "User-specified topology."




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                                  513
Create MyConfig - Expert
7.17 SINAMICS device configuration


                  When the system configuration is configured in the CMC package, all the data sets and
                  optimization data in the step tree required within a series of modular machines in the maximum
                  machine configuration can be specified. The package is adapted to the specific version of a
                  modular machine either initially during the configuring or when the package is being executed
                  on the machine – either manually or using configuration files.




7.17.2         SINAMICS device configuration with Automatic configuration or user-specified
               topology


Applications

                  With regard to device configuration of the SINAMICS, a general distinction is made between
                  three use cases that CMC supports:
                  1. SINAMICS was commissioned previously with SINUMERIK Operate or with different
                     commissioning software.
                     The existing drive data can be checked with a CMC package via "Initial state" (online
                     access) on the dialog page "System configuration" at "DRV..." in the drive archive data,
                     including the topology. In addition, a further configuration or optimization of the SINAMICS
                     can be made.
                  2. The maximum configuration of the SINAMICS is wired on the machine, but the SINAMICS
                     has not yet been commissioned or configured. Using a CMC package, the "Automatic
                     configuration" at "DRV archive data / drive configuration" is selected from the "System
                     configuration" dialog page.
                     The checks, configurations or optimizations listed in item 1 in the same package are then
                     performed.
                  3. Not all the SINAMICS components provided for the maximum configuration of the machine
                     have already been wired on the machine. For example, DQI/SMI motors or also Motor
                     Modules are still missing. SINAMICS has not yet been commissioned and configured.
                     Using a CMC package, the "User-specified topology" at "DRV archive data / drive
                     configuration" is executed from the "System configuration" dialog page. In SINAMICS, the
                     user-specified topology installs your defined topology in the final configuration of the
                     machine.
                     The checks, configurations or optimizations listed in item 1 in the same package are then
                     performed.

Configuration in Expert
                      When configuring in Expert, on the "System configuration" dialog page in section "DRV..." at
                      "Origin of data", you can define which of the four applications "Initial state,"
                      "Automatic configuration," "User-specified topology," or "Offline archive" is applicable.
                      When you select the "User-specified topology" mode, it is imperative to generate a file with the
                      user-specified topology with Topo and to make it available to the package for execution on the
                      "SINAMICS topology" dialog page. The user-specified topology file has a binary format with the
                      file extension *.utz.
                      If "Automatic configuration" is performed, you can optionally use a file containing the
                      comparison topology in XML format and with the file extension *.ust or xml on the "SINAMICS
                      topology" dialog page. This is used for comparison with the automatically detected topology.
                      The two topology files can be configured in one package. During execution, the "Origin of data"
                      setting at "DRV archive data/drive configuration" on the "System configuration" page
                      determines which of the two settings will be used on the following "SINAMICS topology" page.
                      Both the user-specified topology and the comparison topology contain the topology of the
                      SINAMICS and other properties of the DOs and the components.

7.17.3          Drive data generation via "automatic configuration"


Basic procedure
                   The "automatic configuration" via SINUMERIK Operate or via CMC uses the same functions
                   internally. In both cases, SINAMICS determines its actual topology and saves it as target
                   topology ("p9903").
                   This also includes the creation of drive objects (DOs) and their assignment in a folder structure
                   according to bus number and slave number.
                   Each DO is represented as a PS file either in ACX or ASCII format "*.TEA".
                   The "PS000000" file is used to monitor the consistency. The "PS000099" file contains
                   configuration data of the internal PROFIBUS. This structure can be saved as drive archive and
                   imported later.

                      Figure 7-158     Drive data storage

                      For the "Automatic configuration", SINAMICS specifies, for example, DO names, DO numbers,
                      component names and component numbers as well as component properties such as article
                      number, component category and component type.
                      The parameters for the DOs are read out of the components, calculated or assigned with
                      factory settings.
                      The complete data is backed up in the drive data archive.

                      Note
                      First encoder on the CU or downstream of the HUB
                      If during a drive data generation via "Automatic configuration", a first encoder (SMI or SMC) is
                      connected downstream of a HUB or to the CU, then a complete automatic configuration of the
                      drive by SINAMICS and Shield is not possible.
                      SINAMICS sets parameter "P1982" (Pole position identification on) to "1". This value is not
                      correct and is not corrected automatically.
                      The user can correct the parameter manually or in the step tree of a CMC package.
                      Set parameter "P1982=0" in the step tree in a component for all drives whose first encoder is
                      connected downstream of the HUB or to the CU.

7.17 SINAMICS device configuration


Basic procedure
                  If the SINAMICS device configuration is performed with the "User-specified topology",
                  SINAMICS is assigned a user-specified topology file "*.utz" from the CMC package, which
                  corresponds to the final configuration of the machine.
                  The user-specified topology can contain (deactivated) components that were missing at the
                  time of the first commissioning. These components are added, wired and activated as part of
                  a step-by-step commissioning. These components can be, for example, DQI/SMI motors,
                  encoders, etc.
                  In addition to the topology, the user-specified topology file also contains:
                  ● DO name
                  ● DO number
                  ● Component name
                  ● Component number
                  ● Component properties
                     – Article number
                     – Component type
                  The structure with generalized drive data is also specified.
                  Finally during package execution, SINAMICS verifies this data based on the currently available
                  configuration and customizes it appropriately. In this way, the DO and component status are
                  defined.
                  As a result SINAMICS has a customized target topology p9903 and customized DOs for the
                  specified components.
                  The DO parameters are customized by SINAMICS with the factory settings, exported from the
                  components or calculated. All data is backed up in the drive data archive.
                  Because at this time components not yet present in the structure have already been created,
                  the associated user data is added to the step tree using manipulation tasks.
                  Or alternatively, for example with DQI/SMI motors, you can force an export of the data from the
                  electronic rating plate with the "Motor type" or "Encoder type" selection after activation.


Notes regarding the user-specified topology

                  Note
                  Faulty user-specified topology
                  ● If the drive system no longer ramps-up after a user-specified topology, you can assume that
                    the specified topology is faulty.
                  ● However, the drive system also signals a topology error in the commissioned state as usual.
                  ● Incorrect topology data is apparent in the HMI.

                                                                                               Create MyConfig - Expert

7.17.5            Assignment of the drive data using DO variables
                      Immediately after the "Automatic configuration" or after the "User-specified topology", the
                      physical drives have been assigned to the data in the archive structure. The DOs, however, are
                      not yet assigned to the technological drive and thus to the correct NC axis.
                      If optimized drive, motor or encoder data has been configured in a CMC package for a DO, it
                      must be known to which physical DO this technological data must be assigned. This means that
                      the path address of this DO must be known. The data is assigned using DO variables.


Diff
                      When configuring a package in production preparation, SINAMICS data of the modular
                      modules is extracted once as master data to ASCII files from drive archives of one or more
                      commissioned base machines with the comparison component Diff (e.g. drive data, motor
                      data, encoder data of the various axes, line module data, etc.). Appropriate filter settings mean
                      this data no longer contains any topology-specific component numbers when exported.
                      When exporting, Diff writes a section in front of the data that provides a reference to a topology-
                      specific PS file in the drive data archive. This reference in the section is a short form of the path,
                      e.g. [B3_S3_PS5] instead of [BUS3.DIR\SLAVE3.DIR\PS000005.TEA].
                      These modular data sets can be maintained and managed in freely selectable folder structures.


Expert
                      When configuring in Expert , the topology-specific path data can be replaced by symbolic,
                      topology-independent path data using a DO variable, e.g. [$(Up.doVar.psPath)]. By assigning
                      the drive-specific DO variables to a SINAMICS-DO and the associated simultaneous value
                      assignment of the DO variables using the package during runtime, the DO variable has a
                      defined value and thus also a defined path. The assignment of the DO variables to a SINAMICS-
                      DO can be done manually at runtime in a dialog or in advance during the configuration of the
                      comparison or user-specified topology. With this method, topology-independent SINAMICS
                      parameters (master data) can be flexibly and easily assigned to each DO, regardless of where
                      the drive-specific DO was placed in the SINAMICS group for the current machine.
                      As a result of the value assignment during the execution of the package, the symbolic path data
                      is replaced with absolute paths and the topology-independent SINAMICS data that do not
                      contain any component numbers are assigned to the drive-specific components in the current
                      topology.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo

Advantages for the configuration of the topology with Topo
                  ● Understandable topology creation thanks to a graphical wiring diagram
                  ● Support with component box, context menu, verification run and graphic / color-coded
                    visualization
                  ● Printing the wiring diagram of the SINAMICS components with legend for documentation
                    purposes
                  ● Comparison of topologies
                  ● Import of topologies from drive archives
                  ● Management of DO variables


Advantages of the topology file during the package execution
                  ● The actual wiring of the SINAMICS in the control cabinet can be checked using the machine
                    topology exported from SINAMICS. Warning or error messages are issued should
                    deviations occur.
                  ● You can check the properties of the components wired via DRIVE-CLiQ (DO type, article
                    number, etc.). Wildcards are allowed when specifying the article number, e.g. 1FK7042
                    xAF7x xFxx.
                  ● Sensor Modules not directly wired to a Motor Module, but rather to a hub or a CU, can be
                    uniquely assigned to a DO.
                  ● The specification of an OEM-ID is used to assign the SINAMICS-CU local component
                    number to a particular OEM global unique identifier. During package execution, the OEM
                    component number in the DO1 is written to parameter p7859 [component number].
                  ● For the comparison topology, the DO names, DO numbers and component names specified
                    by SINAMICS for the "Automatic configuration" can be replaced by user-specific data.
                    DO name
                    If a DO name change has been configured, then it is automatically entered in SINAMICS
                    parameter p199.
                    DO number
                    When configuring the drive unit, SINAMICS assigns the DO numbers for all DOs at the CU
                    and the NXs, i.e. CU local, starting from 1.
                    For a machine series, it is more understandable, for example, if the X-drive, irrespective of
                    its positioning in the SINAMICS group, always has the same number and that the DO
                    numbers in the SINAMICS group are unique. The value range for the DO numbers lies
                    between 2 and 54.
                    Component names
                    The component names can be freely assigned. The names of the SINAMICS components
                    are displayed on the dialogs and in the screen forms and messages of SINUMERIK Operate.

                      ● When a user-specified topology is used, the component numbers must also be specified in

7.18.1          Expanding or changing GUD definitions
                   The following example explains how you can specifically change a definition file.
                   In GUD.DEF you are shown how you can enter a definition without knowing in advance as to
                   whether it already exists.
                   If the definition already exists, then only the value is changed. If the definition does not exist,
                   then it is added as complete definition.
                   Process the definition in Create MyConfig Script Editor.




Figure 7-163   Example, ChangeDef.uplib

                   Definition example

                    ;Arg1:definition-file
                    ;Arg2:old-definition
                    ;Arg3:new-definition
                   proc ChangeDef($,$,$) {

                   ; definition-file
                   Up.FileName=Up.$1
                   ; search-string for old definition
                   Up.DefOld=Up.$2
                   ; new definition inclusive value
                   Up.DefNew=Up.$3




                                                                            SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
526                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                           Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                 7.18 Special configuration examples


                      ; read definition-file into Up-variable
                      Up.DefFile = FileRead(ARC, Up.FileName)
                      ; get type of the new definition (CHAN, REAL,...)
                      Up.DefType = StringMatch(Up.DefNew, "(DEF [A-Z]* [A-Z]*)") << ".*"
                      msg("DefType = " << Up.DefType)
                      ; get position of the search-string in the definition file
                      Up.DefPos = StringPos(Up.DefFile, Up.DefOld, 0)



                      If Up.DefPos != -1 ; Value of Up.DefOld found in Up.DefFile

                        ; replace the search-string in the definition file with the new
                        definition
                        Up.NewFile = StringReplace(Up.DefFile, Up.DefOld, Up.DefNew)

                      Else ; Up.DefOld not found, looking for definition type

                        Up.DefPos = StringPos(Up.DefFile, Up.DefType , 0)
                        ; searching for the last occurrence of the definition type
                        While Up.DefPos != -1
                         Up.Pos2 = Up.DefPos + StringLen(Up.DefType) ; Increment Up.Pos2
                         and search forward
                         Up.DefPos = StringPos(Up.DefFile, Up.DefType , Up.Pos2)
                        EndWhile

                        ; if variable Up.Pos2 exsits (not null), a definition of the same
                        type was found
                        ; the value of Up.Pos2 contains the position of the last occurrence
                        for the definition type
                        If Up.Pos2 != null
                           ; set position after newline
                         Up.DefPos = StringPos(Up.DefFile, "\n", Up.Pos2)+1
                        Else
                         ; getting the position right before "M17" or "M30"
                         Up.DefPos = StringPos(Up.DefFile, "M17|M30", 0)
                        EndIf



                        ; read begin and end from origin and concatenate with new
                        definition string
                        Up.NewFileBeg = StringSubStr(Up.DefFile, 0, Up.DefPos)
                        Up.NewFileEnd = StringSubStr(Up.DefFile, Up.DefPos)
                        Up.NewFile = Up.NewFileBeg << Up.DefNew << Up.NewFileEnd

Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                      527

                  EndIf

                  ; write modified string to file
                  FileWrite(ARC, Up.$1, Up.NewFile)



                  }




7.19            Reimporting packages


7.19.1          Overview
                  With Expert, packages can be reimported via "Project" > "Import package...", i.e. the project
                  used as basis is regenerated. The entire know-how of the project engineer is in this project. To
                  protect this know-how and prevent unauthorized use of a deployed package, you can assign 3
                  access levels with different authorizations.
                  Therefore, project development engineers can make the know-how of their package accessible
                  to a group of previously defined people.
                  You can find further information in Section "Password protection (Page 478)".
                  You can only execute or view (reimport) protected CMC packages if you have a password with
                  one of these access levels.


Access levels

                   Access level                                    Authorizations
                   "Execute package"                               ● Execute package
                   "Read package reimport"                         ● Only open project for reading after a reimport
                   "Full access to package reimport"               ● Open a project for reading
                                                                   ● Change or save project
                                                                   ● Edit password list of project




7.19.2          Reimport with password protection


Preconditions
                  In principle, it is always possible to reimport a package of the same version. However, to open
                  the project that has been created, you require a password which gives you the permission
                  "Read reimported package" or "Full access to reimported package."



                                                                         SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
528                                                                       Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                            Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                          7.19 Reimporting packages


Rules for a reimport
                      ● When opening a reimported project or a reimported component, all passwords are removed
                        that are not identical to the password used for opening.
                        The entry <permissions without password> remains unchanged with its configured rights. In
                        the result, in the password list, there are a maximum of 2 entries; the entry
                        <rights without password> and the entry of the password used.
                         Note
                         This point is only implemented, if you logged on with a password for "Package reimport full
                         access" and the project was subsequently saved.

                      ● If the password used has the permission "Package reimport full access," in addition to this
                        permission, after the reimport, all of the other permissions to the project/component will also
                        be assigned to it.
                      ● If the password used only has the permission "Package reimport read," no other additional
                        permissions are allocated.
                        The project or the component cannot be stored and any passwords with "Full access to
                        reimport" are therefore retained.
                      ● No permissions for reimporting a component have been granted, it can be deployed but not
                        viewed or modified.
                        Reimported components that have permissions for the project password used are opened
                        with this permissions without an additional query.
                        Otherwise, the password protection behaves in the same way as for reimported
                        components.

9.1.3           Industrial security

                   Note
                   Industrial security
                   Siemens provides products and solutions with industrial security functions that support the
                   secure operation of plants, systems, machines and networks.
                   In order to protect plants, systems, machines and networks against cyber threats, it is
                   necessary to implement – and continuously maintain – a holistic, state-of-the-art industrial
                   security concept. Products and solutions from Siemens constitute one element of such a
                   concept.
                   Customers are responsible for preventing unauthorized access to their plants, systems,
                   machines and networks. Such systems, machines and components should only be connected
                   to an enterprise network or the Internet if and to the extent such a connection is necessary and
                   only when appropriate security measures (e.g. using firewalls and/or network segmentation)
                   are in place.
                   For additional information on industrial security measures that can be implemented, please
                   visit:
                   Industrial security (https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity)
                   Siemens’ products and solutions undergo continuous development to make them more secure.
                   Siemens strongly recommends that product updates are applied as soon as they become
                   available, and that only the latest product versions are used. Use of product versions that are
                   no longer supported, and failure to apply the latest updates may increase customer’s exposure
                   to cyber threats.
                   To stay informed about product updates, subscribe to the Siemens Industrial Security RSS
                   Feed at:
