9.2               Introduction

                      Note
                      Setup of documentation: Operating Manual / Online Help
                      Section Topo has the same layout and structure in the Operating Manual and online help.




What is Topo?
                      The Topo software is used in Create MyConfig to configure, display, print and compare
                      SINAMICS topologies.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                     539
Create MyConfig - Topo
9.2 Introduction


                   Three different topology variants are available:
                   ● Comparison topology
                   ● User-specified topology
                   ● Extended user-specified topology


Comparison topology
                   An image of the SINAMICS topology is used for purposes such as:
                   ● Check the topology (wiring) of SINAMICS on the machine
                   ● Monitor module/component properties
                   ● Change module/component properties
                   ● Change DO numbers and DO names
                   ● Assign SINAMICS modules DO variables.
                     SINAMICS modules or components are, for example, Sensor Modules and Motor Modules.


User-specified topology
                   Instead of using the "automatic configuration", you can specify an external topology for
                   SINAMICS. This variant of the device commissioning supports a step-by-step production,
                   because modules/components and data that do not physically exist can be configured in the
                   control.
                   During series production of modular machines, generally a special version of the axis-drive
                   assignment is specified for each machine variant to be manufactured.
                   The objective is to split the axis-drive assignment into several modular objects in order to
                   handle their parameterization flexibly, irrespective of the physical design and wiring of the
                   machine. The functional interaction of the individual axis/drive configurations must be ensured
                   beforehand.



                   Note
                   Axis-drive assignment with user-specified topology - note the version
                   The axis-drive assignment with user-specified topology can only be used in connection with
                   CNC software as of version 4.5.




Extended user-specified topology
                   Topo also contains the "Extended user-specified topology" in addition to the comparison and
                   user-specified topology.
                   In addition to the SINAMICS wiring diagram, the "Extended user-specified topology" also
                   contains NC and DRV data.




                                                                         SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
540                                                                       Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                              Create MyConfig - Topo
                                                                                                       9.2 Introduction


                      The starting basis for the "Extended user-specified topology" is the archive import of a
                      functioning machine. After changing the topology or NC or DRV data, load the result directly to
                      the NC.
                      The "Extended user-specified topology" can be loaded directly to the control or deployed as
                      package for Windows or Linux.
                      Whereby, an Expert project with subsequent package is not required.
                      The "Extended user-specified topology" is used mainly for an existing machine in a service
                      case.

                      For example:
                      ● Wiring change
                      ● DO assignment
                      ● Axis-drive assignment
                      You can also change individual drive data or insert data from other sources. Similarly, drive
                      objects and modules from other archives, as well as new modules, can be added or existing
                      ones deleted.


Topo - Functions
                      Topo provides the following functions:
                      ● Creation of topologies via a graphical user interface using the context menu and additional
                        standard Windows tools.
                      ● Import of topologies from SINUMERIK archives, from deployed topologies (ECAD XML files)
                      ● Import of topologies from Siemens Data Exchange "*.sdx" from EPLAN Add-In, the
                        following applies as of CMC version V4.8.
                      ● Verification run for created topologies
                      ● Comparison of topologies
                      ● Assignment of module/component properties, e.g. component name, OEM ID.
                      ● Specification of criteria (article no.) that the package compares with the actual properties of
                        the SINAMICS modules on the machine to be produced (loaded target topology of the
                        SINAMICS) and reports any impermissible deviations.
                      ● Assignment of the DO variables to modules/components.
                      ● Creation of a user-specified topology based on generic modules. You can load the user-
                        specified topology directly to SINAMICS during package execution.
                      ● Support of a step-by-step commissioning for missing components through deactivation of
                        these components.
                      ● Use the axis-drive assignment (AAZ) to assign the configured axes to the drives that are
                        actually being used.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                         541
Create MyConfig - Topo
9.2 Introduction


                   ● A DOList Editor (Page 560) is integrated in Topo that provides effective support when
                     creating DO variables.
                     If you want to edit "*.uvdx", "*.uvd" DO variables independent or outside of Topo, start the
                     DOList Editor via the Windows start menu as a separate application.
                   ● As of SINAMICS 5.20, Topo supports the parallel connection of ALMs on a Control Unit in
                     the "user-specified topology" and in the "extended user-specified topology".


Assignment of DO variables and DO properties
                   You assign DO variables to the modules in Topo. These DO variables provide properties that
                   can be used for the configuration in Expert during package execution. In this way, it is possible
                   to work flexibly in Expert with defined DO variables whose absolute values only apply during the
                   package runtime on the machine.
                   SINAMICS modules that do not generate their own DO, can be assigned the DO-generating
                   modules via DO variables, e.g. Sensor Module to Motor Module.
                   The drive-specific parameters are therefore stored modularly in a package without reference to
                   a particular DO number, module number, or slave.
                   The assignment of the parameters to the topology-specific drive objects on the machine is
                   controlled flexibly via the DO variables according to the package configuration in the
                   manipulation tasks and step scripts.
                   The DRIVE-CLiQ wiring created in Topo and the assignments made for DO variables, DO
                   names and DO numbers are saved via a deploy function to a "*.ust" comparison topology or
                   "*.utz" user-specified topology file. The comparison topology files or the user-specified
                   topology files are access during a package execution.

9.4                   Topo - operation


9.4.1                 Creating a topology
                        Topo offers the option of creating a new topology from the module catalog. This makes it
                        possible to import and edit a topology from an electrical design system or directly from a control
                        via an archive.
                        The topology can also be displayed from a drive archive, imported, or directly imported from a
                        control and subsequently edited. In this case, the original component numbers and article



                                                                                 SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
550                                                                               Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                             Create MyConfig - Topo
                                                                                                 9.4 Topo - operation


                      numbers determined by SINAMICS are entered in the properties of the components. New DO
                      variables are also automatically generated and assigned to the imported components.
                      The DO variables used for CNC commissioning are stored in the control and can be assigned
                      and displayed again.

                      Topology tree / topology graph display forms
                      A topology is displayed in two ways in Topo. On the one hand, in a structurally hierarchic tree,
                      and on the other hand, in a systematic graphic form which allows the wiring to be more easily
                      understood and individual components to be simply identified.
                      Both ways offer the same functionality with regard to creating and editing a topology. As a
                      consequence, you can work with one or both of these display forms. The topology tree or the
                      topology graph can be shown or hidden via the menu "View > Topology Tree" and "View >
                      Topology Graph" .
                      To display and edit several topologies, they can be selected in the list of topologies by making
                      a multiple selection. Just the same as for Comparing topologies (Page 575), both
                      technologies are displayed next to one another.

9.4.4.1        Local DO list
                  Each topology of a project has a separate variable table for local DO lists. Earlier CMC versions
                  used a global list.
                  If the same variables are configured for different topologies or projects, link them to an external
                  list. The behavior so remains the same as for previous CMC versions.
                  When importing archives, DO variables are automatically formed from the DO names. When
                  commissioning with Create MyConfig, the DO variables are stored in SINAMICS and are
                  therefore available again for the archive import.
                  Unlike previous Topo versions, all data is now retained after the archive import.


DO variables
                  The yellow     icon shows that data is already linked to the DO.
                  If the icon is grayed-out, no data is linked. During renaming or deleting, all axis/drive data is
                  lost. Further information can be found in the Extended user-specified topology (Page 604)
                  section.

9.4.4.3           Extended DO list


Introduction
                      The configuration of components has been added to the DO list. The DOList Editor can be used
                      to create a cross-topology list of drive objects with their respective components and properties.
                      When configuring specific topologies, such a list can be used to quickly select the correct
                      component properties.
                      You can predefine an axis-drive assignment for the processing of topologies taken from
                      "EPLAN electric P8".


Using the extended DO list
                      Components can be added to the DOs in the DO list for the preconfiguration of an assignment
                      of components to specific DOs.

                      The capability to permanently configure specific drive objects (DO) is used in the following
                      scenarios:
                      1. Use in Topo as basis for configuring topologies
                         An extended DO list can be configured and exported in Topo. The extended DO list is stored
                         centrally in the enterprise, for example, for a machine series.
                         Previously, you manually entered and assigned the component properties and DO
                         properties when creating new topologies. Alternatively, you can now use an extended DO
                         list as basis for the configuration. The "*.uvdx" file is imported or referenced from any
                         storage location.
                         The DOs and components configured in the DO list are offered for use when creating the
                         topology.
                         Only preconfigured DOs and components are used for a referenced DO list.
                      2. Use for configuring the EPLAN with the DQ topology export
                         As described in item 1, the configured DO list in Topo is used in the Siemens DQ topology
                         export (EPLAN Add-In) for deriving a topology.
                         Whereby, the individual modules in EPLAN are assigned DOs and components from the DO
                         list.
                         Further information
                         A detailed description of the Siemens DQ topology export can be found in the "SINUMERIK
                         Create MyConfig - EPLAN Electric P8 Add-In (https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/ww/
                         en/view/109763413)" documentation.


                      Note
                      "*.uvd" format
                      For compatibility reasons, the existing format "*.uvd" is still supported for DO lists without
                      components.




Editing the component list
                      The interface of the component list is described below.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                             569
Create MyConfig - Topo
9.4 Topo - operation




                                                                                                                   



















                                                                                                                         

①         Open DO
          Clicking the blue plus character opens a drive object (DO).
          A new dialog displays the components that belong to the DO.
②         Component display of a DO.
          The component properties are changed in the components dialog.
          Components can be added and/or deleted.
③         DO-independent components
          These components are not permanently linked with the DO.
          For example, these components are not retained when components are deleted.
④         Preconfigured components
          Preconfigured components when components are created below a DO.
          These components are not permanently linked with the DO and used only together with the DO.
          The preconfigured components are also automatically copied when a DO is copied.
          When a module in the topology is deleted, the associated preconfigured components are not deleted.

Exporting an extended DO list
                      For exporting an extended "*.uvdx" DO list, all components linked with the DOs are exported,
                      irrespective whether the components were configured via the DO list or assigned from the
                      topology to the DO.


Importing an extended DO list
                      When importing a "*.uvdx" extended DO list into an existing topology, all DO assignments are
                      deleted. The behavior is also identical when importing a "*.uvd" DO list from existing CMC
                      releases.


Linked extended DO list
                      When linking an extended DO list, all existing assignments in the topology are removed. The
                      DO assignment to components is only possible when a component of the correct type, which
                      has not been used on any other component of the topology, is available for the selected DO in
                      the DO list.
                      You can edit and add new DOs and components in the linked DO list. This is possible only
                      within the DO list by clicking the button.
                      After editing, save the DO list to apply the changes.


Using an extended DO list when creating a new topology

                      The following variants are available for creating a new topology:




                                                                            

① Without preconfiguration: Opening an empty topology.
② Imported DO list: An empty topology with an imported "*.uvdx" extended DO list opens.
③ Linked DO list: An empty topology with a linked "*.uvdx" extended DO list opens.
④ Cancel: The operation is canceled.

9.4.4.4           Predefined axis assignment for the EPLAN add-in
                      With the aid of the table in the "Predefined axis assignment" dialog, the required assigned for
                      the axis can be configured for each DO in the DO list.
                      The predefined axis assignment is only used for the import of a topology from the EPLAN Add-
                      In via the Siemens Data Exchange "*.sdx" format.
                      Whereby, the preconfiguration of the DOs used in the specific topology is performed in the axis-
                      drive assignment.
                      You can specify an axis name, the setpoint type, as well as the NC drive to be used for the
                      transport, for a selected axis.
                      In addition to the setpoint interface, you can also specify the axis to which the two encoders are
                      to be assigned. You can also configure the actual value type to be used and the NC measuring
                      system.
                      The table allows any number of DOs to be assigned to the same axis. If the topology selected
                      for the import in Topo uses several DOs, for which the assignment to the same axis has been
                      configured, this assignment is rejected with a message.

Marking the differences in the component properties
                   The Properties table displays differences in the properties of the components and at the same
                   time offers the option of editing the properties. In addition, it is also possible to synchronize
                   individual properties of the component or also complete components between two topologies
                   via the context menu. Differences in the properties of the two components that have been
                   selected are shown in color.
                   For the article number, differences at the individual positions are also shown in color.
                   The colors have the following meanings:

                    Red              Property is available in both components, but is different
                    Blue             Property is only available in the component selected in the right-hand topology
                    Green            Property is only available in the component selected in the left-hand topology
                    Gray             Digit of the article number irrelevant (x)

9.6               Axis-drive assignment
                      For the SINAMICS drive configuration, there is no assignment between the NC axes and
                      drives / drive objects (DOs).

                      The NC axes can be assigned to the drives in the following ways:
                      ● Manually setting machine data via SINUMERIK Operate
                      ● Calculating and assigning machine data in the manipulation task of a CMC package
                      ● Configuration in Topo and execution by the CMC package, using "*.utz" user-specified
                        topology or "*.ust" comparison topology
                      If an axis-drive assignment has been configured on a machine, Topo can perform a diagnosis
                      via an NC-DRV archive and represent the axis-drive assignment.



SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                        579
Create MyConfig - Topo
9.6 Axis-drive assignment




                  Note
                  Axis-drive assignment only after the drive unit configuration
                  The axis-drive assignment is made on the basis of online information from the NCUs, which
                  reflects the currently applicable HW configuration. The axis-drive assignment can only be used
                  after the configuration of the drive units and not for "Initial condition" or "Offline archive".


                  Further information is provided for the following topics:
                  ● Configuring the axis-drive assignment by Topo. (Page 580)
                  ● Execution by the CMC package. (Page 582)
                  ● Diagnosis by Topo. (Page 585)




9.6.1          Configuration


Requirement
                  First of all, the topology must be available as a comparison topology or user-specified topology.
                  DO variables must already have been assigned to the components of the drive objects.


Axis-drive assignment call table
                  Via the Topo menu bar Data > "Manage axis-drive assignment" or directly via the toolbar            ,
                  the table for the display and configuration of the axis-drive assignment is called.
                  The data relevant for a configuration is displayed. The assignment of the machine data, e.g. I/
                  O address, is not performed until runtime of the package. Therefore, this data cannot be
                  displayed at the time of configuration.

                  Activation: Yes
                   Activation "Yes" means that the axis-drive assignment is performed online while the package
                  is running.
                  The precondition is that the axis-drive assignment must also have been activated in Expert or
                  during package execution on the "SINAMICS topology" dialog page.
                  By activation, with equal rights, of the Axis-drive assignment in Topo and Expert, there is a
                  guarantee that not only the expert for Expert, but also the expert for Topo will agree to this
                  assignment.
                  Moreover, it is possible for the project engineer for Expert and the operator during package
                  execution to deactivate this automatic Axis-drive assignment without having to open and edit
                  the topology files.

                  Activation: No
                  If "No" is selected for activation, the stored Axis-drive assignment is not used.

9.6 Axis-drive assignment


Meaning of table columns

                      The table for configuration of the axis-drive assignment is composed of the following table
                      columns:

Table column         Meaning
Axis                 Display of machine axes AX1 to AX31, including the two possible measurement systems MS1 and MS2.
Axis name            For the configuration, the machine axis name must be entered that when executing the package was
                     written to MC machine data N10000 $MN_AXCONF_MACHAX_NAME_TAB.
Setpoint / actual    In this column, the Setpoint output can be activated via a drop-down list and the encoder type specified.
value type           This data is entered in the following NC machine data:
                     N30130 $MA_CTRLOUT_TYPE
                     N30240 $MA_ENC_TYPE
                     N30200 $MA_NUM_ENCS
                     Activated axes and measurement systems are displayed with a white background - deactivated ones are
                     displayed with a gray background.
Input                In this column, the input can be configured for the measuring systems. This states whether it is the first
                     or the second encoder.
NC drive             This column is only activated by Topo after assigning theDO variables and contains the drive number.
                     The assignment of a drive number to an axis can be automatically realized using Topo, corresponding to
                     a                            or                             .
                     Manual assignments are also possible using drop-down list, whereby a "user-defined axis-drive assign‐
                     ment" (yellow display) can be obtained.
DO variable          These columns show the relevant DO properties, and cannot be separated.
DO No.               The NC axis can be assigned a DO variable via the drop-down list.
DO name              The DO variables that were assigned in the topology to the Motor Modules or the Sensor Modules are
                     available.
                     Note
                     Selection is only possible if the DO variable table is correctly filled out.

                      If you import an NC/DRC archive via the Project > Display/import topology... menu, the topology
                      will be shown on a gray background.
                      When you open the "Axis-drive assignment" dialog box, you see the "Display: Diagnosis". This
                      contains all consistent information required to represent the exact assignment of the relevant
                      machine data as they have been set on the machine by automatic axis-drive assignment or
                      manually.
                      This table is used for diagnostics and checking the axis-drive assignment. If, with the "Import"
                      button, you take over the topology on a gray background into the topology list of Topo, you can
                      perform another configuration and the displayed list under "Diagnostics" becomes invalid.

                      Starting Topo
                      Topo is started with the following command, and a file can be displayed and edited.

                      Topo <Topology path>

                      Comparing topologies
                      Two topologies can be compared with the following command, i.e. two files are displayed and
                      can be edited.

                      Topo /diff <File1> <File2>

                      Automated Topo deployment
                      Create MyConfig Topo can be executed in command line mode for automated deployment.

                      Topo /silent <Topology path>
                             /deploy [<Deployment name>] [/deploydir <Deployment directory>]
                             /target (UST|UVDX|(UTZ|USZ|EXE[27|44|45|47|48])) [/autocomplete]
                             [/log <Log file>] [adduvdx <Uvdx path>] [extendcompnames]

                      The possible deployment modes are listed in the following table.

                      Table 9-14     Deployment modes

                       Deployment mode      Explanation
                       UST                  Comparison topology
                       UTZ                  User-specified topology
                       EXE                  Extended user-specified topology as Windows package.
                       USZ                  Extended user-specified topology as Linux package.
                       UVDX                 DOs and components used in the topology as extended DO list.



Notes

                      Note the following information for the command line call:

                      Note
                      Deployment version
                      If no deployment version is specified for the "UTZ", "USZ" and "EXE" deployment modes, the
                      defined deployment versions are used in the source for the individual CUs. If no deployment
                      version is defined, the newest version is deployed.

                      Note
                      Observe the sequence of the switches
                      The switches should be written to in the specified sequence.
                      When doing this, observe the "Call" section and the "Significance of the switches" table.

9.7 Command line call


                  Note
                  Path data
                  ● Paths must be specified in straight quotation marks if spaces are included.
                     Example:
                     "C:\Path with spaces\Expert_Logfile.log"
                  ● A command line call with '\' at the end of the specified path leads to an error and the return
                     value "0".
                     Paths must never end with '\'.

                  Note
                  Saving batch files
                  Always save batch files with ANSI/ASCII coding.

                  Note
                  Accented characters and special characters
                  Avoid using accented characters and special characters in path names.
                  If special characters or accented characters are to be correctly processed in specified paths,
                  then batch files with command line calls must be saved with the same character set as used by
                  the region-specific command line interpreter (cmd.exe).
                  For example, Codepage 850, also known as DOS Latin 1, applies for the region Western
                  Europe.
                  The Notepad Editor integrated in Windows does not support saving files with this character set.

                  Note
                  Uppercase/lowercase
                  For the command line switches and arguments, always use the specified uppercase/lowercase
                  syntax.

                  Note
                  Absolute / relative path
                  Either the absolute path or the relative path can be specified.
                  The relative path with ".\" or "./" refers to the current work folder, where the batch or CMD was
                  called.
                  If no path is specified, the work folder also applies.

9.8               SINAMICS device configuration


9.8.1             Production of modular machines
                      The Create MyConfig (CMC) engineering software supports both the automated production of
                      modular machines for the machine manufacturer as well as the upgrade of machines for end
                      customers, which requires only a limited number of operator actions.


SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                          591
Create MyConfig - Topo
9.8 SINAMICS device configuration


                 The production of machines with 840D sl requires a basic commissioning of the SINAMICS,
                 generally designated as "System configuration". The system configuration can be performed
                 with CMC either as "Automatic configuration" or as "User-specified topology."
                 When the system configuration is configured in the CMC package, all the data sets and
                 optimization data in the step tree required within a series of modular machines in the maximum
                 machine configuration can be specified. The package is adapted to the specific version of a
                 modular machine either initially during the configuring or when the package is being executed
                 on the machine – either manually or using configuration files.




9.8.2          SINAMICS device configuration with Automatic configuration or user-specified
               topology


Applications

                 With regard to device configuration of the SINAMICS, a general distinction is made between
                 three use cases that CMC supports:
                 1. SINAMICS was commissioned previously with SINUMERIK Operate or with different
                    commissioning software.
                    The existing drive data can be checked with a CMC package via "Initial state" (online
                    access) on the dialog page "System configuration" at "DRV..." in the drive archive data,
                    including the topology. In addition, a further configuration or optimization of the SINAMICS
                    can be made.
                 2. The maximum configuration of the SINAMICS is wired on the machine, but the SINAMICS
                    has not yet been commissioned or configured. Using a CMC package, the "Automatic
                    configuration" at "DRV archive data / drive configuration" is selected from the "System
                    configuration" dialog page.
                    The checks, configurations or optimizations listed in item 1 in the same package are then
                    performed.
                 3. Not all the SINAMICS components provided for the maximum configuration of the machine
                    have already been wired on the machine. For example, DQI/SMI motors or also Motor
                    Modules are still missing. SINAMICS has not yet been commissioned and configured.
                    Using a CMC package, the "User-specified topology" at "DRV archive data / drive
                    configuration" is executed from the "System configuration" dialog page. In SINAMICS, the
                    user-specified topology installs your defined topology in the final configuration of the
                    machine.
                    The checks, configurations or optimizations listed in item 1 in the same package are then
                    performed.

Configuration in Expert
                      When configuring in Expert, on the "System configuration" dialog page in section "DRV..." at

                      user-specified topology with Topo and to make it available to the package for execution on the
                      "SINAMICS topology" dialog page. The user-specified topology file has a binary format with the
                      file extension *.utz.
                      If "Automatic configuration" is performed, you can optionally use a file containing the
                      comparison topology in XML format and with the file extension *.ust or xml on the "SINAMICS

                      setting at "DRV archive data/drive configuration" on the "System configuration" page
                      determines which of the two settings will be used on the following "SINAMICS topology" page.
                      Both the user-specified topology and the comparison topology contain the topology of the
                      SINAMICS and other properties of the DOs and the components.

9.8.3           Drive data generation via "automatic configuration"


Basic procedure
                   The "automatic configuration" via SINUMERIK Operate or via CMC uses the same functions
                   internally. In both cases, SINAMICS determines its actual topology and saves it as target
                   topology ("p9903").
                   This also includes the creation of drive objects (DOs) and their assignment in a folder structure
                   according to bus number and slave number.
                   Each DO is represented as a PS file either in ACX or ASCII format "*.TEA".
                   The "PS000000" file is used to monitor the consistency. The "PS000099" file contains
                   configuration data of the internal PROFIBUS. This structure can be saved as drive archive and
                   imported later.

                      Figure 9-26    Drive data storage

                      For the "Automatic configuration", SINAMICS specifies, for example, DO names, DO numbers,
                      component names and component numbers as well as component properties such as article
                      number, component category and component type.
                      The parameters for the DOs are read out of the components, calculated or assigned with
                      factory settings.
                      The complete data is backed up in the drive data archive.

                      Note
                      First encoder on the CU or downstream of the HUB
                      If during a drive data generation via "Automatic configuration", a first encoder (SMI or SMC) is
                      connected downstream of a HUB or to the CU, then a complete automatic configuration of the
                      drive by SINAMICS and Shield is not possible.
                      SINAMICS sets parameter "P1982" (Pole position identification on) to "1". This value is not
                      correct and is not corrected automatically.
                      The user can correct the parameter manually or in the step tree of a CMC package.
                      Set parameter "P1982=0" in the step tree in a component for all drives whose first encoder is
                      connected downstream of the HUB or to the CU.

                      configuration".

Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                              595
Create MyConfig - Topo
9.8 SINAMICS device configuration


Basic procedure
                  If the SINAMICS device configuration is performed with the "User-specified topology",
                  SINAMICS is assigned a user-specified topology file "*.utz" from the CMC package, which
                  corresponds to the final configuration of the machine.
                  The user-specified topology can contain (deactivated) components that were missing at the
                  time of the first commissioning. These components are added, wired and activated as part of
                  a step-by-step commissioning. These components can be, for example, DQI/SMI motors,
                  encoders, etc.
                  In addition to the topology, the user-specified topology file also contains:
                  ● DO name
                  ● DO number
                  ● Component name
                  ● Component number
                  ● Component properties
                     – Article number
                     – Component type
                  The structure with generalized drive data is also specified.
                  Finally during package execution, SINAMICS verifies this data based on the currently available
                  configuration and customizes it appropriately. In this way, the DO and component status are
                  defined.
                  As a result SINAMICS has a customized target topology p9903 and customized DOs for the
                  specified components.
                  The DO parameters are customized by SINAMICS with the factory settings, exported from the
                  components or calculated. All data is backed up in the drive data archive.
                  Because at this time components not yet present in the structure have already been created,
                  the associated user data is added to the step tree using manipulation tasks.
                  Or alternatively, for example with DQI/SMI motors, you can force an export of the data from the
                  electronic rating plate with the "Motor type" or "Encoder type" selection after activation.


Notes regarding the user-specified topology

                  Note
                  Faulty user-specified topology
                  ● If the drive system no longer ramps-up after a user-specified topology, you can assume that
                    the specified topology is faulty.
                  ● However, the drive system also signals a topology error in the commissioned state as usual.
                  ● Incorrect topology data is apparent in the HMI.




                                                                         SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
596                                                                       Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                 Create MyConfig - Topo

9.8.5             Assignment of the drive data using DO variables
                      Immediately after the "Automatic configuration" or after the "User-specified topology", the
                      physical drives have been assigned to the data in the archive structure. The DOs, however, are
                      not yet assigned to the technological drive and thus to the correct NC axis.
                      If optimized drive, motor or encoder data has been configured in a CMC package for a DO, it
                      must be known to which physical DO this technological data must be assigned. This means that
                      the path address of this DO must be known. The data is assigned using DO variables.


Diff
                      When configuring a package in production preparation, SINAMICS data of the modular
                      modules is extracted once as master data to ASCII files from drive archives of one or more
                      commissioned base machines with the comparison component Diff (e.g. drive data, motor
                      data, encoder data of the various axes, line module data, etc.). Appropriate filter settings mean
                      this data no longer contains any topology-specific component numbers when exported.
                      When exporting, Diff writes a section in front of the data that provides a reference to a topology-
                      specific PS file in the drive data archive. This reference in the section is a short form of the path,
                      e.g. [B3_S3_PS5] instead of [BUS3.DIR\SLAVE3.DIR\PS000005.TEA].
                      These modular data sets can be maintained and managed in freely selectable folder structures.


Expert
                      When configuring in Expert , the topology-specific path data can be replaced by symbolic,
                      topology-independent path data using a DO variable, e.g. [$(Up.doVar.psPath)]. By assigning
                      the drive-specific DO variables to a SINAMICS-DO and the associated simultaneous value
                      assignment of the DO variables using the package during runtime, the DO variable has a
                      defined value and thus also a defined path. The assignment of the DO variables to a SINAMICS-
                      DO can be done manually at runtime in a dialog or in advance during the configuration of the
                      comparison or user-specified topology. With this method, topology-independent SINAMICS
                      parameters (master data) can be flexibly and easily assigned to each DO, regardless of where
                      the drive-specific DO was placed in the SINAMICS group for the current machine.
                      As a result of the value assignment during the execution of the package, the symbolic path data
                      is replaced with absolute paths and the topology-independent SINAMICS data that do not
                      contain any component numbers are assigned to the drive-specific components in the current
                      topology.

                      Note
                      We recommend that the drive data is assigned to the drive objects via the assignment of DO

                      There are two ways of assigning the DO variables to the SINAMICS components:

9.8.6             The advantages of using comparison or user-specified topology
                      The configuration of a comparison or user-specified topology with Topo and the use of the file
                      in the package, offer a number of additional advantages.



SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                        599
Create MyConfig - Topo
9.8 SINAMICS device configuration


Advantages for the configuration of the topology with Topo
                 ● Understandable topology creation thanks to a graphical wiring diagram
                 ● Support with component box, context menu, verification run and graphic / color-coded
                   visualization
                 ● Printing the wiring diagram of the SINAMICS components with legend for documentation
                   purposes
                 ● Comparison of topologies
                 ● Import of topologies from drive archives
                 ● Management of DO variables


Advantages of the topology file during the package execution
                 ● The actual wiring of the SINAMICS in the control cabinet can be checked using the machine
                   topology exported from SINAMICS. Warning or error messages are issued should
                   deviations occur.
                 ● You can check the properties of the components wired via DRIVE-CLiQ (DO type, article
                   number, etc.). Wildcards are allowed when specifying the article number, e.g. 1FK7042
                   xAF7x xFxx.
                 ● Sensor Modules not directly wired to a Motor Module, but rather to a hub or a CU, can be
                   uniquely assigned to a DO.
                 ● The specification of an OEM-ID is used to assign the SINAMICS-CU local component
                   number to a particular OEM global unique identifier. During package execution, the OEM
                   component number in the DO1 is written to parameter p7859 [component number].
                 ● For the comparison topology, the DO names, DO numbers and component names specified
                   by SINAMICS for the "Automatic configuration" can be replaced by user-specific data.
                   DO name
                   If a DO name change has been configured, then it is automatically entered in SINAMICS
                   parameter p199.
                   DO number
                   When configuring the drive unit, SINAMICS assigns the DO numbers for all DOs at the CU
                   and the NXs, i.e. CU local, starting from 1.
                   For a machine series, it is more understandable, for example, if the X-drive, irrespective of
                   its positioning in the SINAMICS group, always has the same number and that the DO
                   numbers in the SINAMICS group are unique. The value range for the DO numbers lies
                   between 2 and 54.
                   Component names
                   The component names can be freely assigned. The names of the SINAMICS components
                   are displayed on the dialogs and in the screen forms and messages of SINUMERIK Operate.




                                                                       SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
600                                                                     Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                                         Create MyConfig - Topo
                                                                                           9.8 SINAMICS device configuration


                        ● When a user-specified topology is used, the component numbers must also be specified in
                          addition to the DO names, DO numbers and component names.
                          The use of the DO names, DO numbers and component names corresponds to the above
                          explanations for the comparison topology.
                          The component numbers must also be specified for the user-specified topology.
                          The CU and the NX must contain the 1; the numbers on the CU or NX must not be assigned
                          more than once. The value range for the numbers lies between 2 and 199.
                          In Topo, the component numbers can also be automatically assigned via the context menu.
                        ● When configuring a user-specified topology, the activation status of the DOs and
                          components can still be specified.
                          The following is true:
                           – 0        Inactive and available
                           – 1        Active and available
                           – 2        Not available
                           The status is entered in the following parameters:
                           – p105 DO activation/deactivation
                           – p125          Motor Module activation/deactivation
                           – p145 Sensor Module activation/deactivation

9.8.8           Generation of the comparison topology using external software
                    The structure and the contents of the comparison topology for a package is an open and
                    documented interface, the Topo XML interface. The file format is XML.
                    You will find more information on this in Section Interface - Topo-XML (Page 607).
                    Through the Topo XML interface, it is also possible to generate the comparison topology using
                    external software, which is integrated in the PLM process of the machine manufacturer, e.g.
                    EPLAN, ELCAD or similar. When required, the externally generated comparison topologies
                    can also be read-in in Topo as part of the production preparation for control purposes or
                    adaptations, before they are integrated in the project when configuring with Expert or placed
                    next to the package as configuration file.

                       The Topo XML interface is available in the version SCI 2.6, CMC V4.4/4.5 and CMC V4.6.

9.9 Extended user-specified topology


9.9            Extended user-specified topology

Requirement
                  Create MyConfigTopo contains the "Extended user-specified topology" as a third mode in
                  addition to the comparison and user-specified topologies.




                  Figure 9-31   Topologies display: "Extended user-specified topology"

                  In addition to the SINAMICS wiring diagram, the "Extended user-specified topology" also
                  contains NC and DRV data.
                  The main application area of the "Extended user-specified topology" is the rewiring of the
                  SINAMICS topology on an existing machine.

                  You can make the following changes for the topology:
                  ● Extension with additional drive objects or components
                  ● Removal of drive objects or components
                  ● Editing of the existing NC and DRV machine data.
                  The starting basis for the "Extended user-specified topology" is the archive import of a
                  functioning machine.
                  After the import, in addition to the wiring diagram, additional NC and DRV data is available in
                  the background for manipulation.
                  All of the data remains available until it is deleted and can be saved as Topo project
                  "<Name>.uptz".
                  During the import, DO variables are automatically assigned to the drive objects (DO). DOs are
                  required for the drive or encoder assignment.




                                                                           SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
604                                                                         Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                           Create MyConfig - Topo
                                                                              9.9 Extended user-specified topology


                      Components can be deleted, added or moved using the known mechanisms such as drag-and-
                      drop, copy and paste.

                      Note
                      Observe the drive data format
                      ● The "Extended user-specified topology" is only possible based on ARC archives with ASCII
                        drive data files.
                      ● Drive data in ACX format and ARD archives are not supported.
                      ● For an "Extended user-specified topology" based on an archive, an ARC archive must be
                        used for the SINUMERIK 828D control.


                      Drive objects
                      The "Extended user-specified topology" works only with complete drive objects.
                      This means that:
                      ● When a DO is moved, the complete dataset is always moved, including all of the
                        components used in it.
                      ● All of the DO data is symbolically displayed by the "Motor Module" component (TM, hub).
                      ● The complete DO is always considered when adding or deleting a Motor Module.
                      If you want to edit individual measuring systems, change these via the topology graph.

                      Note
                      Measuring system / Motor data
                      Note that it is not possible to assign a measuring system or motor data to a different DO by
                      moving a component.




Example of moving a "Double Motor Module" from Slave 12 to Slave 13
                      In the following example, the selected "Double Motor Module" is moved from NX Slave 12 X103
                      to NX Slave 13 X102. During the move, a prompt requests whether attached components, NC
                      or drive data should also be moved or deleted.
                      The colored highlighting denotes the attached data.

                  Note
                  No more than 6 Motor Module (MM) may be connected to a Slave.




Deployment methods
                  You can select between the following deployment methods:

                           The "Extended user-specified topology" is transferred directly to the control.
                           The user can optionally select or deselect the PLC and NC data.
                           The "Extended user-specified topology" is deployed as a Windows "*.exe" or Linux
                           "*.usz" package, as already known from Expert.
                           The user can optionally select or deselect the PLC and NC data.


Display of the AX and DO symbols on the component
                  If the assignment has been made in the axis-drive assignment, the "AX" symbol is displayed on
                  the module. The "DO" symbol is displayed when the module has been assigned a "DO".
                  If data is available for the axis or the drive, the "AX" symbols for axis data and "DO" for DO data
                  are displayed in color. Available axis data is always shown in orange and available DO data
                  always in yellow.

9.10.2            Description of the XML structure


SINAMICS components
                      SINAMICS components should be specified in the structure as XML elements based on their
                      device class. To further reduce the recognition tolerance level, restrictive attributes can be
                      specified (Article number).

                      Device classes:
                      control_unit_ncu, control_unit_nx, control_unit_cu,
                      line_module, voltage_sensing_module,
                      motor_module, sensor_module, motor, encoder,
                      motor_module_hf, damping_module, sine_filter_module
                      hub_module, terminal_module, terminal_board
                      motor_module_hf, damping_module, sine_filter_module




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                          609
Create MyConfig - Topo
9.10 Interface Topo XML


Composite modules
                 For composite modules, such as Double Motor Modules and 120 combi modules, their internal
                 structure must be mapped in the XML structure. To ensure the correct display as composite
                 module in Topo, all the internal components belonging to such a module must be identified with
                 the attribute group="<name of the composite component>". In addition, the "index" attribute
                 with the position inside the module must be specified (MM1 → index=1, etc.) for components of
                 the same device class (here Motor Module).

DO-forming DRIVE-CLiQ components
                      SINAMICS automatically creates drive objects (DO) for specific DRIVE-CLiQ components.



                      DO-forming DRIVE-CLiQ components:
                      control_unit_ncu,
                      motor_module_hf control_unit_nx, control_unit_cu, line_module,
                      motor_module, hub_module, terminal_module,
                      terminal_board.
                      SINAMICS components for which a DO is created, can be assigned a "dovar" attribute. The
                      component is assigned a DO variable via the "dovar" attribute. This DO variable contains
                      properties of the DO that can be used subsequently by the package during the package
                      execution.




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                    611
Create MyConfig - Topo
9.10 Interface Topo XML


                 If such a component was assigned a DO variable manually or via the Topo XML file, this DO
                 variable can also be used to specify the user-specific DO name and DO number. For each
                 component that is assigned a DO variable, an appropriate type must also be specified via the
                 "dotype" attribute.

                 The possible DO types are:
                 ● SINAMICS S
                 ● Integrated (NCU)
                 ● Extended (NX)
                 ● ACTIVE INFEED CONTROL
                 ● SERVO
                 ● SMART INFEED CONTROL
                 ● BASIC INFEED CONTROL
                 ● TB30
                 ● DMC20 / DME20
                 ● TM31
                 ● TM41
                 ● TM15
                 ● TM120
                 ● CULINK
                 ● Determine INFEED from hardware
                 ● Determine TM from hardware


DO - referencing components
                 DRIVE-CLiQ components that do not generate their own DO, but are assigned to a DO, can be
                 assigned to any existing drive objects.

                 DO - referencing components:
                 sensor_module,
                 damping_module voltage_sensing_module
                 The specification of "doref" references a DO and thus specifies the association of the
                 component to the DO. To do this, the same DO variable is used as that specified for the required
                 DO via the "dovar" attribute. This allows, for example, Sensor Modules on a hub to be assigned
                 to a SERVO-DO.
                 The "sm" attribute of the "sensor_module" element designates the encoder as 1st or 2nd
                 encoder of the DO. It must then be used if the encoder cannot be assigned uniquely.
                 For modeling DQI/SMI motors, a motor must be specified on the sensor_module along with the
                 encoder. The motor must also be removed from the associated motor_module.
                 The associated components must be identified with the attribute group="<name of the
                 composite component>".

                      <motor_module nam=“eMM1" dovar="var1" dotype="11" donr="20"
                      doname="do">
                         <cliq index="0" uplink="true"/>
                         <cliq index="1"/>
                         <cliq index="2">
                            <sensor_module name="SM1" group="DQI_01" doref="var1" sm="1">
                                   <cliq index="0" uplink="true"/>
                                           <encoder name="Enc1" group="DQI_01"/>
                                           <motor name="Mot1" group="DQI_01"/>
                               </sensor_module>
                         </cliq>
                      </motor_module>


                      Non-DRIVE-CLiQ components (motor, encoder, sine_filter_module) must be adequately
                      defined using their subordinate hierarchical position.
                      The "cliq" element designates a port of a DRIVE-CLiQ component. The "index" attribute
                      specifies the last position of the terminal designation (for X104 → 4, for X501 → 1, etc.).
                      The "uplink=true" attribute in the "CLiQ" element specifies that it involves an "incoming
                      connection" from a higher-level component.
                      Each component can be assigned an ID using the "oemid" attribute.
                      This ID is written to SINAMICS parameter p7859[component number] in DO1. Using this
                      parameter, the machine manufacturer can address additional information, such as additional
                      error texts, spare part numbers, etc.
                      In order to use a comparison topology to generate a user-specified topology without further
                      manual processing in Topo, a unique name as well as a unique component number for each
                      slave ("compnr/compnr2" attribute) must be assigned for each component.
                      To deactivate individual components of a DO or whole DOs, the "compstate" and "dostate"
                      attributes with appropriate valid values can be assigned to the corresponding components.

10.1              Restoring the original status of a USB memory stick
                      To be able to use a USB memory stick for CMC, you must make sure that the partitions are
                      created correctly.
                      A USB memory stick can be used without problems on a PC, whereas it cannot be used to run
                      a CMC package on an NCU/PPU. This may be due to the partitions or the file system on the
                      USB memory stick.


Prerequisite
                      Observe the following information about formatting a USB memory stick:
                      ● No special program is required on a Windows PC
                      ● Administrator rights are required


Formatting a USB memory stick

                      Carry out the following instructions if your USB stick does not start with a CMC package on an
                      NCU/PPU or if similar problems arise:

                       diskpart
                       list disk
                       sel disk <n>
                       clean
                       create part primary
                       format quick fs=fat32 label="CMC"
                      On a Windows PC, you enter the instructions at the command prompt. On LINUX PCs, use
                      other options such as "gparted".




SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                      625
Create MyConfig - FAQs
10.2 Help for problems with NcuShareService


Procedure
                  1. Open the command prompt on the Windows PC and enter diskpart. The utility for
                     partitioning hard disks and removable data storage media is started in a new window. It is
                     possible that a Windows UAC prompt appears, which you must confirm with "Yes".
                  2. The data storage media detected are displayed after you enter list disk. Here, you must
                     find out the number of the data storage medium on the basis of the USB memory stick's
                     memory capacity. In our example, it is data storage medium 1.
                  3. Sel disk 1 selects this data storage medium. You must use the right number on the basis
                     of your existing data storage medium.

                      NOTICE
                      Select Sel disk
                      A data storage medium that you did not want could be destroyed if you specify a wrong
                      number.

                  4. clean erases the data storage medium chosen via the number. All data on it is erased!
                  5. create part primary creates a primary partition on the data storage medium.
                  6. format quick fs=fat32 label="CMC" runs fast formatting with fat32. The stick is
                     given the name "CMC".




10.2           Help for problems with NcuShareService
                  An exchange release is required for the package execution of Windows packages with NCU/
                  PPU share.
                  A setup is available for the installation of the service.




10.2.1         Installation
                  There are three ways to install the "Create MyConfig NcuShare" service.
                  1. Installation with the setup of Create MyConfig.
                  2. Manual installation through the execution of "NcuShareServiceSetup.msi".
                     After installing Create MyConfig, the setup file is available in the installation folder at "/
                     Shield".
                  3. Automatic installation during package execution.
                  When the service is installed, a folder can be configured for the installation types 1 and 2, which
                  is used as the exchange folder.




10.2.2         "Create MyConfig NcuShare" service
                  The service is installed during the installation on the Windows computer with the program name
                  "Create MyConfig NcuShareService" with the specified service version.


                                                                              SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
626                                                                            Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                            Create MyConfig - FAQs
                                                                        10.2 Help for problems with NcuShareService


                      The service is entered with the name "Create MyConfig NcuShare" in the list of services.
                      The service is in the service status "Finished" after installation.
                      The service is started with the execution of Windows packages with NCU/PPU share for the
                      duration of the package execution and is then closed again.
                      When the service is started, it automatically activates the exchange release for the NCU/PPU
                      access.
                      ● "UpNcuShare" with the "%Public%\UpNcuShare" folder for Windows 7
                      ● "%ALLUSERSPROFILE%\UpNcuShare" for WinXP.
                      This permits the exchange of data between NCU/PPU and PC/PCU during the package
                      execution.




10.2.3            Error checking


What must be checked in the event of an error?

                      Use of virtual machines
                      In connection with virtual machines, problems may occur when establishing a connection,
                      because the share of the NCU cannot be achieved.
                      To ensure the NcuShareService functions correctly, only operate the virtual machine in
                      "Bridged Mode". In "Bridged Mode", the share can be achieved by another computer while the
                      service is running.

                      Created user
                      During installation, the user "UpNcuUser" is created and the password is automatically
                      assigned.
                      For security reasons, the password is changed each time the "UpNcuShareService" is started.

                      Note
                      If no user is available when the "UpNcuShareService" is started, a new user is automatically
                      created.




Configuration of the service
                      The service is terminated and automatically removes the share if no package is executed.
                      The service does not need to be configured.

                      Note
                      The default settings of the UpNcuShare service must not be changed.

Changing the share folder
                      The share folder is defined during the installation of the "UpNcuShareService".
                      In case of an installation with Create MyConfig or manual setups, the user can change the path
                      during the installation.
                      If the "UpNcuShareService" is installed during the package execution, the standard path is
                      always used.
                      To subsequently change the exchange folder, the "UpNcuShareService" must first be
                      uninstalled and then re-installed.

10.4              Simulating a project based on offline archives

Requirement
                      A package that has been configured for the use of an NCU or PCU, is simulated under certain
                      constraints without the real existing NCU or PCU.



SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG                                                                             629
Create MyConfig - FAQs
10.4 Simulating a project based on offline archives


Constraints
                   Take the following constraints into account:
                   ● All configurations that refer to a non-existing NCU are not processed by the package during
                     simulation.
                      Note
                      The NCU is not simulated.

                   ● If data for the simulation of the PCU is available, configurations for the PCU are processed
                     by the package.
                      – The statements for "Execution of:" of the "Execute" action are not executed in
                        components.
                      – If target files exist in the simulation path, file changes are executed.
                   ● If archives are available, the configurations relevant for archive data are executed.
                      – The statements for "Execution of:" of the "Execute" action in components are excluded
                        from this.
                   ● A package for the Archive, PCU and NCU/PPU data areas can be simulated as follows:
                      – The complete package with all data areas
                      – Without the NCU/PPU and PCU controls
                      – Only with a real existing control
                      – Only the non-real existing control part is simulated
                   ● The package execution with real NCU and PCU in simulation is possible as well as the
                     execution with real PCU and exclusion of the NCU. The latter variant is rather not a
                     simulation.
                   ● The "System configuration" dialog is only available when a real NCU is used, not with
                     deactivated data area of the "NCU/PPU".
                   ● An automatic configuration of the drives or a user-specified topology is not simulated
                     directly. However, if you use an appropriate drive archive as initial offline archive, you can
                     simulate the "SINAMICS topology" dialog in the "Comparison topology" version.
                   ● Control versions of the PCU are evaluated in the package when there is a "Version.txt" file
                     on the simulation PCU at "D$\UP".
                     The versions to be evaluated must be in the following form line-for-line in the "Version.txt"
                     file:
                     <Application name> <Tabulator> <Version>
                     Example

                       SINUMERIK Operate                           ⇒        04.08.02.03
                       SINUMERIK PCU Basesoftware                  ⇒        11.06.00.00
                      Shield creates and uses this file during the package run with a real PCU.
                   ● Control versions of the NCU are not evaluated and not simulated.




                                                                          SINUMERIK Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
630                                                                        Operating Manual, 06/2019, A5E36537479B-AG
                                                                                              Create MyConfig - FAQs
                                                                  10.4 Simulating a project based on offline archives


Procedure
                      To simulate a package without using a real NCU/PPU or PCU, use the settings described in the
                      following in Expert in the "Project folder".

                      "Package" tab
                      ● In the Package tab, set "Deployment" > "Runtime system" > "Windows package (PC/PCU)".
                        A package is always only simulated under Windows.
                      ● The configuration at "Exclude data areas" has no significance for the simulation, only for the
                        size of the deployed package.
                      ● Since the NCU/PPU is not really available, select "No" for "Use NCU/PPU" at "Data areas".
                        All package parts that are relevant for the NCU are therefore ignored for the package
                        execution.
                        The NCU is not simulated.
                      ● Set the "Use PCU" setting to:
                         – "Yes" if you want to simulate a PCU.
                         – "No" if you want to ignore the configurations relevant for the PCU.

                      "Dialogs" tab
                      ● Enter the path to your simulation PCU at "Address" > "Preselection", e.g. D:\temp
                        \mySimPCU, in the "PCU access" dialog in the "Dialogs" tab.
                        The path must contain the folder and file structures that you want to process in the package,
                        starting with the standard drive release D$, C$.
                        If you do not create these structures, the package automatically creates the essential
                        structures, e.g. the path D$\Install.
                        The configured actions are executed on these structures during the Package execution.
                      ● Store the archives that serve as basis for all archive data manipulations in the "Select offline
                        archive" dialog.
                        Use an "NCPLCDP" archive of your control, in part or as a whole, from the initial state before
                        the package execution.
                      ● You can store control versions of the PCU that are to be evaluated on the simulation PCU
                        at D$\UP in a "Version.txt" file.
                        The versions to be evaluated must be in the following form line-for-line in the "Version.txt"
                        file:
                        <Application name> <Tabulator> <Version>
                        Example

                          SINUMERIK Operate ⇒                            04.08.02.03
                          SINUMERIK PCU Basesoftware ⇒                   11.06.00.00

                      Further procedure
                      ● Deploy the package.
                      ● Start the package.
                      ● If the dialogs do not run automatically, edit the dialogs manually.

                  ● The "Update.arc" result archive is next to the package after the Package execution.

                    \mySimPCU.




10.5           First encoder of a drive on the CU or downstream of the HUB

Automatic configuration not possible
                  If during a drive data generation via "Automatic configuration" a first encoder (SMI or SMC) is
                  connected downstream of a HUB or to the CU, then a complete automatic configuration of the
                  drive by SINAMICS and Shield is not possible.
                  Parameter "P1982" (Pole position identification on) is set to "1" by SINAMICS instead of "0"
                  and is not corrected automatically.


Remedy
                  The user can correct the parameter manually or in the step tree of a CMC package.
                  Set parameter "P1982=0" in the step tree in a component for all drives whose first encoder is
                  connected downstream of the HUB or to the CU.




10.6           Parallel connection of Active Line Modules (ALM)

Requirement
                  The following versions are required:
                  ● Create MyConfig V4.8 SP1
                  ● SINUMERIK V4.91
                  ● SINAMICS V5.20


Active Line Module
                  As of SINAMICS 5.20 you can connect 2 Active Line Modules (ALM) to a CU or NX. The Active
                  Line Modules are operated in parallel connection. The parameters of both ALM are saved in
                  one drive object (DO).
                  The required function module is created automatically in all commissioning variants. This
                  function is only possible with components greater than 55 kW. The deployed components must
                  have the same power parameters.

10.7              SINAMICS Starter: No access to drive after CMC package

SINAMICS Starter cannot access the drive after the CMC package
                      When configuring the "Servcoup" function in SINAMICS, note that you must remove the article
                      no. manually when creating the virtual Sensor Modules in Topo.


Remedy
                      Deleting the article no. avoids a subsequent problem with SINAMICS Starter. If you do not
                      observe this procedure, Starter cannot access the drive unit.




10.8              Certain package names result in a Windows error message

Avoiding the Windows message "This program might not have installed correctly"
                      Windows packages that have the designations "install", "installation" or "setup" in their names
                      result in a confirmation prompt from Windows when starting the package on a PCU. As a rule,
                      Windows signals that the program has not been installed correctly.

                 For example, avoid package names such as "Install.exe", "Test_Install.exe".
